name: Olio e Più
summary: Inspired by the warmth and comfort of the Italian countryside, Olio e Più and chef Danilo Galati bring tradition and authentic Italian cuisine to the West Village.
address: 3 Greenwich Avenue, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Inspired by the warmth and comfort of the Italian countryside, Olio e Più and chef Danilo Galati bring tradition and authentic Italian cuisine to the West Village. Enjoy fresh, house-made pastas dressed with the highest quality ingredients and a hand-selected collection of excellent wines and cocktails to pair with your dish. An expertly crafted wood-fire oven crackles and glows, cooking house-made dough into perfect, crisp pizza while creating an inviting atmosphere.

name: Quality Bistro
summary: This bustling, steak-centric brasserie in Midtown Manhattan offers contemporary takes on bistro classics.
address: 120 West 55th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: This bustling, steak-centric brasserie in Midtown Manhattan offers contemporary takes on bistro classics. The restaurant holds a welcoming bar, airy conservatory and open dining room, accented by custom light fixtures, floor-to-ceiling wine cabinets, zinc tabletops and vintage touches.

name: Bananas
summary: Bananas is an expression of the chef-owners' take on Asian American food, incorporating classic Asian flavors with Western cuisine—a signature menu of American favorites with elements of Asian cooking.
address: 174 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10009, United States
summary2: Bananas, a New American restaurant from chef-owners Chris Ng (previously of Blue Ribbon and Bond St) and Kyaw Lwin (previously of Yakiniku Futago, Hasalon and Michelin-starred Shmoné), is located in the East Village. Bananas is an expression of the team’s take on Asian American food, incorporating classic Asian flavors with Western cuisine. The phrase “Bananas” has previously been used as a slur to describe Asian Americans who are ‘yellow’ presenting but culturally white due to their upbringing in America. Bananas offers a signature menu of American favorites with elements of Asian cooking.

name: Ocean Prime
summary: This award-winning restaurant and lounge from renowned restaurateur Cameron Mitchell is designed to please all palates.
address: 123 West 52nd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: This award-winning restaurant and lounge from renowned restaurateur Cameron Mitchell is designed to please all palates. The chef-led menu unites fresh seafood and choice steaks, while a service team steeped in the traditions of Midwestern hospitality works to ensure that each and every guest feels like a VIP. With its exceptional food and drink and a luxurious atmosphere, this distinctive Midtown spot is an ideal place to socialize, talk business, celebrate and indulge.

name: Masseria East
summary: Masseria East continues the fine dining legacy of the old Parma Restaurant, which was established in this location in 1977.
address: 1404 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10075, United States
summary2: Masseria East is an Italian restaurant on Manhattan's Upper East Side. Masseria East continues the fine dining legacy of Parma Nuova and the old Parma Restaurant, which was established in this location in 1977.

name: Yama Ramen
summary: This Japanese eatery serves ramen, sushi, teriyaki, pork buns and more on its extensive menu.
address: 60 West 48th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: This Japanese eatery serves ramen, sushi, teriyaki, pork buns and more on its extensive menu. It's located in Midtown right by Rockefeller Center.

name: Dinosaur Bar-B-Que - Harlem
summary: Healthy portions of pork ribs, Texas-style brisket and pulled pork, along with plenty of cocktails and seasonal brews, are on the menu at this barbecue spot.
address: 700 West 125th Street, New York, New York 10027, United States
summary2: Long before NYC became a destination for decent ’cue, Dinosaur’s Syracuse, N.Y.-based pit masters rescued the City from infamy with its honky-tonk Harlem branch underneath the Riverside Drive bridge. Done up like a gritty roadhouse, this cavernous meat haven is known for its gut-busting platters of pork ribs, Texas-style brisket and pulled pork. Pick your protein-heavy meal and wash it all down with an ice cold beer from the wide array of artisanal brews.

name: The Greenhouse Cafe
summary: There's almost always a party at the Greenhouse Café, a popular Bay Ridge venue where many local Brooklynites celebrate their weddings, anniversaries and other special events.
address: 7717 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10029, United States
summary2: There’s almost always a party at the Greenhouse Café, a popular Bay Ridge venue where many local Brooklynites celebrate their weddings, anniversaries and other special events. But it’s also a fine and welcoming place to have an intimate meal, particularly if you’re a meat-eater—everything from roasted duckling to lamb to filet mignon graces their vast menu.

name: Meet the Meat
summary: This highly-regarded steakhouse in Astoria serves prime cuts of meat aged to perfection in a unique way, accompanied by superior customer service.
address: 23-92 21st Street, Astoria, New York 11105, United States
summary2: After 25 years of experience working in elite Manhattan establishments, the proprietors of Meet the Meat decided to bring their extensive experience to Astoria, Queens. This highly-regarded steakhouse serves prime cuts of meat aged to perfection, and accompanied by superior customer service. Outdoor seating is available seasonally. Meet the Meat also accommodates corporate parties and private functions.

name: Jupiter
summary: Jupiter brings handmade pastas, New Italian wines, seasonal vegetables, grilled meats, and a boisterous spirit to Rockefeller Center.
address: 20 West 50th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Jupiter is the second restaurant from Clare de Boer, Annie Shi and Jess Shadbolt, the team behind King. Jupiter brings handmade pastas, New Italian wines, seasonal vegetables, grilled meats, and a boisterous spirit to iconic Rockefeller Center.

name: Morgan's Brooklyn Barbecue
summary: Morgan's is Brooklyn through and through, a restaurant with a DIY edge that is as mindful of families with young kids as it is of the borough's bearded whiskey fanatics.
address: 267 Flatbush Avenue Extension, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Morgan's is Brooklyn through and through, a restaurant with a DIY edge that's as mindful of families with young kids as it is of the borough's bearded whiskey fanatics. The Texas-style barbecue is treated seriously (very good brisket, pulled pork and ribs), but there's also the whimsical, crowd-pleasing frito pie smothered with Texas red chili and loaded baked potatoes. The restaurant offers outdoor dining.

name: Sushi of Gari 46
summary: Masatoshi “Gari” Sugio is the Japanese owner-chef of several highly regarded sushi spots known for procuring the freshest fish on the market.
address: 347 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Gari initially came to the United States to help a friend with the opening of a new Japanese restaurant in New York City. He worked as a sushi chef for several Japanese restaurants, and observed many of the guests eating sushi with too much soy sauce, which masked the taste of the delicate succulent fish. He decided to create his own brand where sauce was put directly onto the sushi during the preparation stage, so customers did not need to add soy sauce to truly enjoy the taste of each piece. Gari was determined that he could create a variety of sauces that would go well with sushi. Since opening his first restaurant in 1997, the main focus has been to serve sushi with the original sauces and toppings Chef Gari has created. These sauces serve to enhance the sensitive taste and flavor of each morsel of fish.

name: Calvert's
summary: Calvert's, at the Park Lane Hotel New York on Central Park South, represents elegance redefined. From oysters to pasta, the menu offers reinvented contemporary classics with thoughtfully foraged ingredients.
summary2: Calvert's, at the Park Lane Hotel New York on Central Park South, represents elegance redefined. From oysters to pasta, the menu offers reinvented contemporary classics with thoughtfully foraged ingredients. At daybreak, an array of a la carte menu options elevate any morning, then as the day wanes on, indulge in decadent fare and innovative twists on contemporary cocktails. A nod to Calvert Vaux, the esteemed co-designer of the iconic park across the street, this is a contemplative wisdom-seeking respite. Like a walk in Central Park, Calvert’s is delightfully epiphanous.

name: Champers Social Club
summary: Champers serves a French-adjacent twist on bar classics including oysters, roasted mushroom toast, deviled eggs, and Nicoise, alongside a large selection of champagne and sparkling wines.
address: Crosby Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Champers Social Club, set in a lovingly restored historic cast-iron and brick store front in SoHo, is a reflection of the vibrant street, the storied neighborhood, and a curated and considered design aesthetic. Uniquely beautiful, casually refined, and infinitely photographable, the space is complimentary to the cultured and well-heeled crowd. Champers is led by Brenna Gilbert and Andrew McCaughan, a husband and wife team who, with more than 40+ years of executive leadership, hospitality, events production, design, and creative management in their resumes across LVMH, USHG, Shake Shack, and Anthropologie, embody the warm and approachable hospitality at the heart of the restaurant. Indulge in their French-adjacent twist on bar classics including oysters, roasted mushroom toast, deviled eggs, and the Champers Nicoise. Champers beverage program specializes in champagne. Their list includes non-traditional pours so guests can explore and discover sparkling wines from around the world. In addition, their coffee bar serves up artisanal coffee by New York favorite Joe Coffee.

name: Baciccia Pizza e Cucina
summary: Baciccia offers a number of classic Ligurian delicacies, including their neighborhood-famous Trofie al Pesto Genovese, as well as brick oven Roman-style pizza.
address: 426a Seventh Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Baciccia Ristorante, founded by two Northern Italians, is a unique neighborhood staple in Park Slope that offers the wonderful flavors of authentic Ligurian cuisine. Guests have the option of sitting in the dining room, the colors of which evoke a warm day in the Cinque Terre, or al fresco on their outdoor patio. Baciccia offers a number of classic Ligurian delicacies, including their neighborhood-famous Trofie al Pesto Genovese, as well as brick oven Roman-style pizza. The wine list is curated with the Italian wine-lover in mind, but the bar is stacked with classic spirits.

name: Mishik
summary: Executive chef/partner Markee Manaloto brings his experience working with Edomae sushi to his new venture, a modern Japanese restaurant in Hudson Square.
address: 259a Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Executive chef/partner Markee Manaloto brings more than a decade of experience working with Edomae sushi at Japanese restaurants to his new venture, Mishik, a modern Japanese restaurant in Manhattan's Hudson Square neighborhood. Chef Manaloto's experince includes the Michelin-starred Sushi Yasuda, East Village favorite Kissaki, and his own Japanese-Filipino izakaya Gugu Room (as co-chef and partner). With Mishik, chef Markee showcases his devotion to Japanese tradition and techniques, along with a rigorous sourcing program of fish from Tokyo’s Toyosu Market.

name: Pappardella
summary: This longstanding Italian restaurant—on the Upper West Side since 1983—serves Tuscan cuisine.
address: 316 Columbus Avenue, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: This longstanding Italian restaurant—around since 1983—serves Tuscan cuisine, along the lines of cured meats, grilled steak, tagliatelle spinachi and an array of pizzas and other pastas.

name: Salt + Charcoal
summary: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar.
address: 171 Grand Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Salt + Charcoal is Williamsburg’s one of a kind Japanese robata grill and bar. Preparation of their signature steaks start with the chef hand selecting each piece of beef at the purveyor. It is then dry-aged for 28 to 50 days before charcoal-grilling using their unique crank grill. The result is a super-tender steak with all of the umami trapped inside. Salt + Charcoal also has a wide selection of seafood, a raw bar, and Japanese-inspired appetizers. The full bar features original cocktails crafted by award-winning mixologists, a variety of Japanese spirits, and wines specially crafted to pair with the food offerings.

name: Frenchette
summary: This classic French brasserie and bar in Tribeca has a friendly attitude and bistro favorites like duck frites. Stay for a meal or have a drink at the welcoming long bar.
address: 241 West Broadway, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Frenchette feels built to last: a classic brasserie with glossy wood, curvy booths, golden lighting and a long bar where it’s easy to imagine becoming a regular. The staff is friendly and professional, a reflection of the decades-long rapport between chef-owners Riad Nasr and Lee Hanson (ex-Balthazar, Minetta Tavern). Its exquisite yet not-so-serious French fare includes duck frites, roasted chicken and whole turbot with buttered potatoes. Natural wines dominate the list, with by-the-glass options poured from magnums and jeroboams.

name: ABC Cocina
summary: ABC Kitchen has a design of ethereal lightness, while its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina, is all dark magic.
address: 38 East 19th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: ABC Kitchen has a design of ethereal lightness, while its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina, is all dark magic. They also share an ethos of green technology via building materials and lighting, and they source their menu items from small, sustainable farmers. At this, the more casual of the two ABC eateries, chef de cuisine Ian Coogan combines influences from Spain, Mexico and Argentina for a user-friendly tapas style menu as seen through a New American prism. Reservations are recommended or there's walk-in seating available at the bar or communal table.

name: Grotta Azzurra
summary: After a hundred years in Little Italy, Grotto Azzurra is holding down its history as host to Caruso and Sinatra; that same hospitality extends to the travelers and locals who pack the recently renovated restaurant.
address: 177 Mulberry Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: After a hundred years in Little Italy, Grotto Azzurra is holding down its history as host to Caruso and Sinatra; that same hospitality extends to the travelers and locals who pack the restaurant. A prix-fixe lunch menu is still under $10, and homemade pasta specialties are fine starters to entrées like veal Milanese and osso buco. The brick-lined wine cellar room is particularly lovely and great for large private parties.

name: Sweet Catch
summary: Sweet Catch is an ode to the connection between African-American people and their rich history of seafood culinary mastery.
address: Nostrand Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11205, United States
summary2: From the low country of Charleston, South Carolina to the clear blue waters of the Chesapeake Bay, down through the muddy swamps and rushing rivers of the Louisiana Bayou, African-Americans boast a rich history of seafood culinary mastery, a connection to the land, and a respect for the fruits of the sea. Sweet Catch is an ode to this connection—a love letter to African-American culture, African-American people, and African-American love; a place of remembrance for what history has erased and a celebration of their spirit.

name: Mission Ceviche - Upper East Side
summary: Mission Ceviche, from chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca, has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.
address: 1400 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10021, United States
summary2: Mission Ceviche was born in 2015 when chef Jose Luis Chavez and partner Brice Mastroluca outfitted a modest stall within Gansevoort Market to create an homage to the flavors of Peru. The initial success at Gansevoort Market spurred the establishment of a second fast-casual spot in Canal Street Market, and building on the momentum, the partners took Mission Ceviche to new heights with the opening of its first sit-down restaurant on the Upper East Side in 2019. The restaurant found immediate critical success after launching, earning a star from Pete Wells at the New York Times and a feature in the Michelin Guide. Mission Ceviche has become synonymous with modern Peruvian cuisine, offering a diverse array of dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients.

name: Socarrat Paella Bar - Chelsea
summary: Socarrat Paella Bar Chelsea reflects an ambiance rich in warmth, comfort and hospitality, and brings out the Spaniard in New York: it's elegant, bold and sexy. A neighborhood staple comprised primarily of one large communal table with a bar and smaller communal tables scattered throughout, Socarrat Chelsea also has a private dining room that can can accommodate up to 28 people.
address: 259 West 19th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Socarrat Paella Bar Chelsea reflects an ambiance rich in warmth, comfort and hospitality, and brings out the Spaniard in New York: it's elegant, bold and sexy. A neighborhood staple, the restaurant is a destination for those looking to experience a little bit of Spain in Chelsea. There are wines from all Spanish regions and a number of specials, including happy hour.

name: Il Buco Alimentari & Vineria
summary: Find a restaurant, market, salumeria and bakery all in one spot.
address: 53 Great Jones Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Il Buco Alimentari & Vineria is a restaurant, market, salumeria and bakery that feels like a “village inside a restaurant.” The seasonal menu features salumi and cheese boards, small sharing plates, fresh pastas and roasted meats and fish.

name: Malii Gramercy
summary: Malii Gramercy is a creative Thai restaurant in the Gramercy Park area in Manhattan.
address: 391 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Malii Gramercy is a creative Thai restaurant in the Gramercy Park area in Manhattan. Their mission is to provide high-quality Thai food for those who seek skillful cooking and an extraordinary dining experience.

name: Industry Kitchen
summary: Industry Kitchen serves simply prepared modern American dishes with views of the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges and Brooklyn skyline.
address: 70 South Street, New York, New York 10005, United States
summary2: Nestled along the East River next to historic South Street Seaport, Industry Kitchen is steps from the water’s edge, affording views of the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges and Brooklyn skyline. Industry Kitchen uses market ingredients for simply prepared modern American dishes, including seasonal salads and wood-oven grilled meats and pizza.

name: Mark's Off Madison
summary: This restaurant-bakery combines rustic Italian and European cooking and traditional Jewish food. Alongside fresh homemade pastas, entrée salads and Belgian fries, there's Jewish deli rye and hand-rolled bagels and bialys.
address: 41 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Mark’s Off Madison, just off the corner of Madison Avenue and East 26th Street, is a venture from acclaimed chef Mark Strausman, formerly of Freds at Barneys New York and Campagna restaurants. The restaurant-bakery combines rustic Italian and European cooking and traditional Jewish food, so in addition to fresh homemade pastas, entrée salads and Belgian fries, there's Jewish deli rye and hand-rolled bagels and bialys.

name: AperiBar
summary: This chic restaurant and cocktail bar serves uncomplicated food and cocktails in warm, stylish surroundings that invite conversation and sharing.
address: 120 West 41st Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: A chic restaurant and cocktail bar by Charlie Palmer Collective, AperiBar serves uncomplicated food and cocktails in warm, stylish surroundings that invite conversation and sharing. It's a fresh, Italianesque concept by celebrated master chef and entrepreneur Charlie Palmer. The menu offers small and large plates perfect for sharing and lingering at the table over wine or an aperitif. In the morning, there's coffee, pastry, fruit and yogurt or a breakfast pizza. Or enjoy dinner with antipasti, oysters and crudo of the day, salads, pizza, pasta as well as some of Charlie's favorites from land and sea.

name: Pera Mediterranean Brasserie
summary: This gem of a bistro serves innovative interpretations of classic Greek and Turkish dishes in Murray Hill.
address: 303 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Serving innovative interpretations of classic Greek and Turkish dishes in Murray Hill, this gem of a bistro is designed around its open kitchen, where chefs can be seen busily toiling over open flames. The specialties are spice-drenched dishes like meze platters, shrimp and lamb skewers, traditional breads and mini-pizzas called pidettes. Live jazz performances are scheduled every Saturday.

name: Hearth
summary: Hearth is everything its name implies...a warm, comfortable restaurant with hospitality as its goal.
address: 403 East 12th Street, New York, New York 10009, United States
summary2: Hearth is the East Village restaurant from chef Marco Canora, recipient of the James Beard Award for Best Chef New York City, 2017. Chef Canora’s cuisine, with a warm nod to Tuscany, employs seasonal, locally-sourced ingredients that taste delicious and make you feel good. The intimate restaurant spaces provide the perfect backdrop for cozy first dates, celebratory family gatherings, and refined business experiences. The Hearth wine cellar features smaller, independent producers, and a bounty of organic, natural, and biodynamic bottles.

name: Palermo Argentinian Bistro - NYC
summary: Meat lovers will love Palermo Argentinian Bistro on Restaurant Row, where beef reigns supreme.
address: 373 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Meat lovers will love Palermo Argentinian Bistro, where beef reigns supreme. Orhan Cakir, the force behind the Pierre Loti wine bar in Gramercy, has teamed up with executive chef Carlos Barroz, formerly of La Pulperia, to open this latest addition to Manhattan’s Restaurant Row. The steakhhouse draws it inspiration from Palermo, a destination in Buenos Aires known for its fashionable bars and restaurants. Set in a three-story brownstone built in 1894, the bi-level restaurant brings traditional Argentinian barbecue centering on prime steaks sourced from the nearby century-old Piccinini Brothers butcher shop.

name: Kubeh
summary: Kubeh, a Greenwich Village restaurant dedicated to lesser known cuisines of the Middle East, is the product of chef Melanie Shurka and husband David Ort.
address: 464 Sixth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Kubeh, a Greenwich Village restaurant dedicated to lesser-known cuisines of the Middle East, is the product of Persian-Israeli chef Melanie Shurka and husband David Ort. Kubeh is named after a dumpling soup combo found in Kurdish, Iraqi and Syrian cuisines. In addition to their kubeh, the variety of delectable mezes, spreads and small plates they serve are meant to be shared like a big Middle Eastern family dinner.

name: Urban Cove Society & Kitchen
summary: With an elevated, yet relaxed dining room, Urban Cove sets the table for a blending of Modern American and global cuisines.
address: 33 Peck Slip, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: Urban Cove Society & Kitchen is a culinary experience nestled within 33 Hotel, New York City, Seaport. With an elevated, yet relaxed dining room, Urban Cove sets the table for a blending of Modern American and global cuisines. The brunch and dinner menus are as diverse as they are comforting, paying homage to the rich tapestry of cultures that define New York City and the historic Seaport district. Poised to become a beloved neighborhood haunt, the social club offers experiential dinners, craft cocktail classes, diner rewards, and more for its members.

name: Vino &... - Eataly NYC Downtown
summary: Vino &..., the wine bar in the heart of the marketplace at Eataly NYC Downtown, brings the best of Italian wines into one restaurant and bar in downtown New York.
address: 4 World Trade Center, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: Vino &..., the wine bar in the marketplace at Eataly NYC Downtown, brings the best of Italian wines into one bar-restaurant in downtown New York. Vino &... celebrates the craft of wine artisans and the craft of authentic Italian food, carrying forward regional traditions that have been at the center of the Italian table for generations. Discover a diversity of Italian wines and ingredients, and ask their experts for the story behind each bottle to find your perfect pour any time of day.

name: La Pizza & La Pasta
summary: Eataly has teamed up with experts Rossopomodoro to present classic Neapolitan pizza, while their Fresh Pasta Counter offers expertly prepared pasta dishes.
address: 4 World Trade Center, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: For La Pizza & La Pasta, Eataly has teamed up with experts Rossopomodoro to present classic Neapolitan pizza, while their Fresh Pasta Counter offers expertly prepared pasta dishes with a choice of fresh pasta made in-house or the highest quality dry pastas cooked al dente. Enjoy antipasti salads using only the freshest of ingredients, including sweet San Marzano tomatoes and other chef-selected market vegetables. Don’t forget to ask the waiters to help you pair it with an Italian beer or a glass of white or red wine.

name: La Pizza & La Pasta
summary: For La Pizza & La Pasta, Eataly has teamed up with experts Rossopomodoro to present classic Neapolitan pizza, while their Fresh Pasta Counter offers expertly prepared pasta dishes with a choice of fresh pasta made in-house or the highest quality dry pastas cooked al dente.
address: 200 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: For La Pizza & La Pasta, Eataly has teamed up with experts Rossopomodoro to present classic Neapolitan pizza, while their Fresh Pasta Counter offers expertly prepared pasta dishes with a choice of fresh pasta made in-house or the highest quality dry pastas cooked al dente. Enjoy antipasti salads using only the freshest of ingredients, including sweet San Marzano tomatoes and other chef-selected market vegetables. Don’t forget to ask the waiters to help you pair it with an Italian beer or a glass of white or red wine.

name: La Contenta Oeste
summary: La Contenta Oeste offers a traditional Mexican menu with French accents and also features one of NYC's largest tequila, mezcal and alt agave selections.
address: 78 West 11th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: La Contenta Oeste, helmed by chef-owner Luis Arce Mota, is an authentic Mexican restaurant and bar located in the West Village neighborhood of Manhattan. La Contenta Oeste offers a traditional menu with French accents and also features one of NYC's largest tequila, mezcal and alt agave selections, in addition to the first all-Mexican wine list in the United States with more than 150 different bottles.

name: Da Andrea - Greenwich Village
summary: Experience the beauty of authentic Italian dining with a menu that specializes in the art of homemade pasta, traditional Italian dishes, delicious risottos, and more.
address: 35 West 13th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Da Andrea is a neighborhood Italian ristorante located in Greenwich Village in Manhattan. Experience the beauty of authentic Italian dining with a menu that specializes in the art of homemade pasta, traditional Italian dishes, delicious risottos, and more. Each dish is meticulously prepared with fresh, locally sourced ingredients and an abundance of experience. Dining is a shared experience and every detail matters. Whether you’re in the mood for a glass of wine or a full four-course meal, Da Andrea takes patrons on a delectable journey in a warm and inviting ambiance.

name: Dos Caminos Times Square
summary: Dos Caminos Times Square spans two floors and features a 40-seat mezcal and margarita bar on the street level and a guacamole bar on the subterranean level.
address: 1567 Broadway, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Dos Caminos Times Square spans two floors and features a 40-seat mezcal and margarita bar on the street level and a guacamole bar on the subterranean level. Look out for an expanded menu of chef Ariel Fox's healthy Mexican dishes as well as a selection of 120 premium tequilas and delicious new cocktails.

name: Bryant Park Grill
summary: It's hard to beat the restaurant's location: It overlooks Bryant Park, one of the City's most elegant gardens.
address: 25 West 40th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: It’s hard to beat the restaurant’s location: It overlooks Bryant Park, one of the City’s most elegant gardens. The menu ranges widely—from steak frites to grilled mahimahi to tomato ravioli with goat cheese and sun-dried tomatoes—to suit all tastes. For appetizers, fish figures prominently, including a salad topped with crispy calamari and a seafood salad with lobster, shrimp and crab.

name: Obao Hell's Kitchen
summary: Obao bridges the gap between the streets of Southeast Asia and the culinary sensibilities of NYC, bringing diners a combination of Thai and Vietnamese comfort foods that have a twist.
address: 647 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Obao bridges the gap between the streets of Southeast Asia and the culinary sensibilities of NYC, bringing diners a combination of Thai and Vietnamese comfort foods that have a twist. The restaurant takes traditional dishes from Thailand and Vietnam—among them Pad Thai and pho noodles—and adds a touch of luxury without compromising on authenticity. Obao features high-quality ingredients, allowing visitors to experience a culinary blend of ease and elegance that satisfies the palate.

name: Warren Street Bar & Restaurant
summary: This modern neighborhood brasserie offers an all-day menu of much-loved classics and fresh, seasonal dishes filled with flavors and ingredients from around the world.
address: 86 Warren Street, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: The Warren Street Bar & Restaurant is a modern neighborhood brasserie offering an all-day menu of much-loved classics and fresh, seasonal dishes filled with flavors and ingredients from around the world. The space itself is a celebration of color and creativity, with an eclectic art collection and characterful interiors. Executive chef Diego Chaparro was born in Lima, Peru, but most recently comes from Miami, Florida. His passion for storytelling throughout each dish stems from the relationship and connection he feels getting to work with local farmers and purveyors.

name: Central Park Boathouse
summary: Nestled in the park, right on the lake, is the Central Park Boathouse, an iconic and elegant restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating, and different menus (in different price ranges) for each seating area.
summary2: Nestled in the park, right on the lake, is the Central Park Boathouse, an iconic and elegant restaurant with both indoor and outdoor seating, and different menus (in different price ranges) for each seating area. After you eat, rent a bike or a rowboat to experience Central Park further, or take a gondola ride—but be sure to make reservations ahead of time.

name: The Dining Room at Gramercy Tavern
summary: Executive chef and partner Michael Anthony’s menu consists of elegant dishes with a rustic influence that showcases the restaurant’s relationships with local farms and purveyors.
address: 42 East 20th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Gramercy Tavern’s contemporary American cooking, warm hospitality, and unparalleled service has garnered the restaurant nine James Beard Awards. Executive chef and partner Michael Anthony’s menu consists of elegant dishes with a rustic influence that showcases the restaurant’s relationships with local farms and purveyors.

name: Felice on Hudson
summary: Felice on Hudson fits seamlessly into the picturesque West Village, bringing an array of daily specials inspired by seasonal ingredients and an extensive Italian wine list to the neighborhood.
address: 615 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Nestled amongst brownstones, historic buildings and angled streets, Felice on Hudson fits seamlessly into the picturesque West Village, bringing an array of daily specials inspired by seasonal ingredients created by the executive chef and an extensive Italian wine list to the neighborhood. The knowledgeable front-of-house team can guide you through the menu and the curated cocktail and wine program, to enjoy in the intimate dining room or the well-appointed bar. Sam Tannehill Designs has created an inviting, warm space that feels like it has been in the neighborhood for years.

name: Panda Harlem
summary: Panda Harlem is a unique dining experience inspired by fine cuisine, high-energy hospitality and hip-hop culture.
address: 2331 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10027, United States
summary2: Panda Harlem is a unique dining experience inspired by fine cuisine, high-energy hospitality and hip-hop culture. All the sights, sounds and tastes of this immersive experience will make you feel as if you’ve been transported to Beijing. The selections at Panda have roots in Asian culture with added American twists, and the cocktails combine premium spirits with the freshest ingredients, creating a foodies' paradise. The nightlife will also support the local community with events curated for all. The menu, decor and values are all inspired by Harlem itself. Dress code is "dress to impress," and entry is subject to doorman discretion.

name: Meadowsweet
summary: At Williamsburg's modern, chic Meadowsweet, executive chef Polo Dobkin has a deft touch with seasonal ingredients, crafting dishes with a Mediterranean bent.
address: 149 Broadway, Brooklyn, New York 11211, United States
summary2: At Williamsburg's modern, chic Meadowsweet, executive chef Polo Dobkin has a deft touch with seasonal ingredients, crafting dishes with a Mediterranean bent. Crispy artichokes, house-made pastas and octopus with piquillo peppers and chorizo are among the highlights. Rolls hot from the oven are dusted with sea salt, luscious when spread with thyme-honey butter. Dobkin's wife, Stephanie Lempert, has devised some refreshing cocktails that are garnished with fresh herbs harvested from the loft garden overhead. That garden, plus patterned tiled floors, comfortable caramel banquettes and bare wood tables, makes it a pretty place to gather.

name: Tommy Bahama Restaurant–Bar–Store
summary: Tommy Bahama Restaurant–Bar–Store, the flagship location for the island-inspired luxury lifestyle brand, features Marlin Bar, a second-story oasis-like dining room, and a 5,000-square-foot store.
address: 551 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10176, United States
summary2: Tommy Bahama Restaurant–Bar–Store is the flagship location for the island-inspired luxury lifestyle brand. This Midtown outpost features Marlin Bar, the only free-standing bar on Fifth Avenue between the Empire State Building and Central Park, a second-story oasis-like dining room with views of the City hustle and bustle below, and a 5,000-square-foot store boasting an extensive collection of men's and women's apparel, swimwear, footwear, accessories and home décor. Chef Shannon Mills, formerly of Ritz Carlton, delivers classic American cuisine with an emphasis on fresh seafood, all with a hint of the Pacific Isles.

name: La Baraka
summary: La Baraka is a Little Neck destination for the best French dining experience...with a touch of North Africa.
address: 11362 Queens Boulevard, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: La Baraka is a local destination for the best French dining experience...with a touch of North Africa. The Little Neck, Queens institution gained food lovers' attention by being one of the first in the 1970s to introduce couscous, the signature dish of North African cuisine.

name: Crave Fishbar - Upper West Side
summary: Crave Fishbar—NYC’s first 100% sustainable seafood restaurant—is home to the #Oystergram Happy Hour, one of NYC’s best oyster happy hour deals.
address: 428 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: Crave Fishbar—NYC’s first 100% sustainable seafood restaurant—is home to the #Oystergram Happy Hour, one of NYC’s best oyster happy hour deals. This Upper West Side location serves creative seafood in an upscale neighborhood setting, complete with warm hospitality. Global flavors and innovative preparations highlight their sustainable seafood, heritage meats, and organic produce. The raw bar features a daily selection of East Coast and West Coast oysters, sometimes up to 20 varieties each night. For business dinners, special occasions, and dining out just-because, Crave serves a sustainable and memorable meal.

name: The Fulton
summary: Dine at Jean-Georges Vongerichten's celebration of fresh seafood in the Seaport.
summary2: Breathtaking views of the Brooklyn Bridge and Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s seafood-centric menu are reason enough to head to the end of Pier 17 in the Seaport. The world-renowned chef wows patrons with warm octopus astride fresh mozzarella, signature egg toast caviar, and a decadent swordfish Milanese with sauce gribiche. The bi-level space is huge, decked out in romantic nautical murals and featuring floor-to-ceiling windows plus an outside patio to enjoy the waterfront view.

name: Gallaghers Steakhouse
summary: Back in the prohibition years, Gallaghers Steakhouse served as a speakeasy.
address: 228 West 52nd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Back in the prohibition years, Gallaghers Steakhouse served as a speakeasy. Now, 80 years later, this signature New York establishment is a prime spot for a genuine steak. The restaurant’s meat-aging room is stocked with USDA Prime dry-aged beef, which is sure to bring a tear to the eye of any carnivore. The dinner menu features chicken, seafood and even a veggie plate, but the steak is where it’s at.

name: The Paris Cafe
summary: Find old-school charm and French-American food at this historic bar.
address: 119 South Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: Established in 1873, The Paris Café is one of New York City's oldest brasseries. Located in the historic South Street Seaport district, The Paris Café is a landmark in the federal registry of historic buildings and a landmark among restaurants everywhere. Bob Dylan, Thomas Edison, Teddy Roosevelt, Lauren Bacall and Butch Cassidy were all guests of this iconic establishment. It's an ideal location for craft cocktails, a wide-ranging food menu, nightlife and events.

name: Tuscan Hills
summary: Tuscan dishes such as the house specialty, cacciucco alla livornese, can be found at this rustic Italian restaurant in Forest Hills.
address: 110-60 Queens Boulevard, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Tuscan dishes such as the house specialty, cacciucco alla livornese—fish stew in fresh tomato sauce, topped with a bread crust—can be found at this rustic Italian restaurant in Forest Hills.

name: Tucci
summary: Tucci, New York's newest Italian restaurant, serves refined modern Italian cuisine and family recipes in a warm and inviting atmosphere.
address: 643 Broadway, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: For five generations, the Tucci family has gathered at their beloved "Tavola" at their villa in Firenze, enjoying family, friendship, and food. Today that legacy continues with Tucci, New York's newest Italian restaurant, which serves refined modern Italian cuisine and family recipes in a warm and inviting atmosphere. Tucci is a labor of love that honors Max Tucci and the Tucci family legacy.

name: Nice Matin
summary: A culinary venture through Nice in the fall of 2002 inspired partners Simon Oren (Marseille, Sushi Samba and L’Express) and chef Andy d’Amico (Sign of the Dove and Little Dove) to open Nice Matin in 2003.
address: 201 West 79th Street, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: A culinary venture through Nice in the fall of 2002 inspired partners Simon Oren (Marseille, Sushi Samba and L’Express) and chef Andy d’Amico (Sign of the Dove and Little Dove) to open Nice Matin in 2003. The Upper West Side restaurant features an extensive breakfast, lunch, brunch and dinner menu whose influences pull from the cuisine of the coastal city in southern France.

name: Atrio Wine Bar & Restaurant
summary: Atrio Wine Bar & Restaurant serves seasonally-inspired New American cuisine from a dramatic open kitchen.
address: 102 North End Avenue, New York, New York 10282, United States
summary2: Atrio Wine Bar & Restaurant, located in Conrad New York Downtown, masterfully pairs refined cuisine with expansive views of the Hudson River and Lower Manhattan for a casual yet luxury dining experience. Located under the lobby’s striking 15-story atrium, the restaurant serves inventive American fare from locally sourced ingredients for breakfast, brunch, lunch, and dinner. The restaurant also offers a fresh happy-hour experience as guests indulge in hand-crafted libations, extensive wine offerings, and small bites.

name: Chez Nick
summary: Three chefs have collaborated to create an elevated neighborhood dining experience at this Upper East Side seasonal New American restaurant.
address: 1737 York Avenue, New York, New York 10128, United States
summary2: Seasonal New American cuisine shines at this Upper East Side restaurant, where three chefs have collaborated to create an elevated neighborhood dining experience. The menu features roast chicken, short ribs and braised Moroccan chickpea entrees, as well as lighter options like sandwiches, soups and composed salads.

name: Trattoria Dell'Arte
summary: A favorite of concert goers at nearby Carnegie Hall, Trattoria Dell'Arte is a design landmark, thanks to an interior done by the legendary Milton Glaser, and a entrance marked by a giant white nose.
address: 900 7th Avenue, New York, New York 10106, United States
summary2: A favorite of concertgoers at nearby Carnegie Hall, Trattoria Dell'Arte is a design landmark, thanks to an interior done by the legendary Milton Glaser, and a entrance marked by a giant white nose. The kitchen serves homey Italian fare, done to high standards: pizza with a nicely singed crust; osso bucco, served with tomatoes, tart capers and risotto; and a seafood pappardelle, with a white-wine sauce studded with clams, shrimp and crab. Fiends for variety can opt for sampler plates culled from the snaking antipasto bar, which offers cured meats, and an ocean of seafood.

name: Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar
summary: The cuisine at Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar is inspired by international tapas, putting an updated spin on classic dishes and bringing creative new ones.
address: 127 East 55th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Gather your crew for an unforgettable tapas-style dining experience accompanied with a fine selection of wines and crafted cocktails. With more than 10 years of experience in hospitality, aspiring restauranteurs Kevin Cardenas and Ruben Cabrera launched themselves with their first venture, Ceviche Fussion, which was an overwhelming success. An opportunity arose that bore this intimate and inviting venue, Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar, inspired by the Japanese bonsai tree (a miniature tree cultivated to resemble nature in a modest space and nurtured with artistic interaction). Bonsaii Tapas & Wine Bar is the ultimate representation of its namesake. Their cuisine is inspired by international tapas, putting an updated spin on classic dishes and bringing creative new ones, so every patron will feel welcomed and find something of their taste.

name: Le Rivage
summary: This traditional French restaurant is located in the heart of the Theatre District and has been operated since 1984 by the Denamiel family.
address: 340 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: This traditional French restaurant, located in the Theatre District, has been operated since 1984 by the Denamiel family. The romantic French atmosphere is the setting for elegant yet affordable classic French cuisine (roast duck, frogs’ legs, escargot). Specializing in pre-theater dining, Le Rivage ensures that patrons finish their meals with enough time to make the opening curtain. The restaurant also is open for lunch and post-theater dining.

name: Gabriel's Bar & Restaurant
summary: A staple for more than three decades, Gabriel's brings the quintessential flavors of Italy to Midtown Manhattan.
address: 40 Central Park South, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Gabriel's Bar and Restaurant has been a NYC staple for more than three decades. Gabriel's brings the quintessential flavors of Italy to Midtown Manhattan. Established in 1991 by Gabriel Aiello, the restaurant is known for providing excellent service and great food throughout the years, and for hosting many famous personalities. With rare dedication towards his craft, Gabriel will still find time to greet patrons at the front of the house and make their experience memorable. Now at its new home at 40 Central Park South, Gabriel's continues the same tradition, with the same sensibility and care.

name: Gran Morsi
summary: Gran Morsi, named after the Italian word for "bites" epitomizes elegant simplicity.
address: 22 Warren Street, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: Gran Morsi, named after the Italian word for “bites,” epitomizes elegant simplicity. This airy and convivial TriBeCa restaurant, on the border of the Financial District, specializes in boldly flavored Italian fare with a strong focus on small and shared plates, many of which are cooked in the brick oven. Gran Morsi provides downtown Manhattan residents and visitors with a dining experience fit for whatever they’re in the mood for, whether it’s a special occasion celebration, an intimate evening or a casual night out with friends. Gran Morsi also has a private event space perfect for any and all special occasions.

name: Stout NYC Penn Station
summary: The first Stout NYC location, located near Penn Station, Madison Square Garden, and Macy’s flagship, is an ideal gathering place for lunch, after-work drinks, and before (and after) that game, concert or events.
address: 215 West 35th Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: The first Stout NYC location is located just two blocks from Penn Station, Madison Square Garden, and world-famous shopping including Macy’s flagship store at Herald Square. It's an ideal gathering place for lunch, after-work drinks, and before (and after) that game, concert or special event.

name: STK Downtown
summary: Simply put, STK is not your daddy's steakhouse.
address: 26 Little West 12th Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Simply put, STK is not your daddy's steakhouse. The restaurant brings high-energy dining to Manhattan, breaking down the barriers of a normal steakhouse by losing the overly masculine vibe that has long been the trademark of the genre. As a modern and vibrant take on the traditional steakhouse, STK Downtown is a quintessential part of experiencing NYC's nightlife and dining scene. STK offers a bustling bar that builds on the energy of a DJ spinning tracks nightly. The restaurant layout and striking décor create an intimate, one-of-a-kind dining experience.

name: Haven Rooftop
summary: Haven is a swanky rooftop lounge and restaurant at the Sanctuary Hotel that offers a welcome retreat from the hectic streets below.
address: 132 West 47th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Located on top of the Sanctuary Hotel New York near Times Square and Rockefeller Center, Haven Rooftop offers guests a chance to view Manhattan's skyline while enjoying modern American cuisine and crafted cocktails. This year-round multi-level rooftop transforms its design with each season. Haven boasts 3,000 square feet of event space, with lush greenery complemented by custom-built cedar furnishings, creating a vibrant and inviting aesthetic. It’s a perfect venue up to 300 people corporate events, social gatherings and celebrations above the lights of Times Square.

name: Bar Milano by Eataly
summary: Amidst a cosmopolitan ambiance inspired by Italy's most fashion-forward city, enjoy elevated, rich Milanese cuisine, iconic drinks like the Negroni, and more.
address: 200 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Take a trip to the vibrant atmosphere of mid-century Milano without ever leaving New York at Bar Milano by Eataly, the restaurant in the middle of the bustling market inspired by Italy's style capital. Amidst a cosmopolitan ambiance inspired by Italy's most fashion-forward city, enjoy elevated, rich Milanese cuisine, such as the saffron-infused Risotto allo Zafferano, bone-in Veal Cotoletta sourced from local farms, iconic drinks like the Negroni, and more.

name: American Cut Tribeca
summary: American Cut Steakhouse pays homage to the best original and aspirational New York dining experience, the steakhouse.
address: 363 Greenwich Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: American Cut Steakhouse pays homage to the best original and aspirational New York dining experience, the steakhouse. Run by LDV Hospitality, the restaurant offers exceptional food and spirits in a modern setting punctuated by Art Deco accents. Diners will be filled with a sense of culinary intrigue, surrounded by prime cuts and modern interpretations of classic dishes.

name: Brass & the Tusk Bar
summary: Through the Art Deco lobby of the historic Evelyn Hotel, find The Tusk Bar for bright takes on classic cocktails, raw bar and seafood-driven small plates, and Brass, an NYC take on the French brasserie.
address: 7 East 27th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Through the Art Deco lobby of the historic Evelyn Hotel, find Brass & The Tusk Bar. Tusk is a jewel of a classic cocktail and oyster bar, named one of Esquire’s "Best Bars in America, 2024." Look for bright takes on classic cocktails, raw bar and seafood-driven small plates. The glamorous bar room marries the spirit of the roaring '20s with the convivial attitude of mid-century cocktail parties, sharing the timelessness of a warm welcome, a well-made drink, a freshly shucked oyster...and a good time. Located through the bar, Brass restaurant is a New York City brasserie that takes inspiration from the style of French brasseries but without adhering to their playbook. Brass showcases the playful contemporary spirit that characterizes chefs Jeremiah Stone and Fabian Von Hauske Valtierra’s cuisine.

name: Cebu Bar & Bistro
summary: The New American cuisine at Cebu Bar & Bistro includes roast chicken, burgers and risotto balls with porcini mushroom.
address: 8801 3rd Avenue, North Bergen, New Jersey 07047, United States
summary2: The New American cuisine at Cebu Bar & Bistro includes roast chicken, burgers and risotto balls with porcini mushroom. Open for lunch, brunch and dinner, Cebu has some inventive cocktails and a patio that's heated in the colder months.

name: Wayan
summary: Intoxicating Indonesian food from a talented chef in Nolita.
address: 20 Spring Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: This beautifully designed Indonesian restaurant is the brainchild of Cédric and Ochi Vongerichten, a couple deft at providing wonderful food and hospitality. A bar and some small tables are up front; a narrow passage winds past the chef’s counter to an amber-lit dining room. Cédric (son of Jean-Georges) is both a gifted and rigorously trained chef, evidenced by lightly fried baby squid, intoxicating corn fritters, nasi goreng (fried rice with a runny egg) and noodles with lobster and basil. Don’t miss the sundae with bruléed bananas and violet-hued ube ice cream.

name: Benjamin Steakhouse
summary: This opulent gem near Grand Central Terminal is the offspring of Peter Luger alumni Benjamin Prelvukaj and chef Arturo McLeod, who bring with them more than 20 years of experience.
address: 52 East 41st Street, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: This opulent gem near Grand Central Terminal is the offspring of Peter Luger alumni Benjamin Prelvukaj and chef Arturo McLeod, who bring with them more than 20 years of experience. The succulent steaks at Benjamin Steakhouse are only the beginning: from the beautifully marbled cuts of dry-aged beef to the perfectly refined Old World service and charm, Benjamin's prides itself on providing first-class service in an elegant, bi-level setting complete with brass chandeliers, plush leather banquettes and a roaring fireplace. Benjamin has established itself as one of Manhattan's premier steakhouses, attracting business professionals and celebrities alike.

name: Flava of the Bronx
summary: Diners feel the tropical breeze and experience yard-man and yard-woman flava style cooking.
address: 3114 Third Avenue, Bronx, New York 10451, United States
summary2: The goal at Flava of the Bronx, in the Woodstock neighborhood, is to make diners feel the tropical breeze and experience "yard-man and yard-woman flava" style cooking that will have them coming back for more of their authentic Caribbean cuisine.

name: Junoon
summary: Junoon's name, meaning "passion" or "obsession," is an indication of the dedication that went into this restaurant.
address: 19 West 24th Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: "Junoon" is an Urdu word, also frequently used in Hindi, meaning "passion" or "obsession," and it's an indication of the dedication that went into this restaurant. In addition to the 100-seat restaurant is a 45-seat private dining area and a 50-seat cocktail bar and lounge. The refined menu covers all the bases of Indian cooking, from tandoor to cast-iron and open-fire-pit cooking to stone-searing. Highlights include lobster tandoori, Cornish hen with pomegranate and roasted cumin, and lamb shoulder with papaya juice and garam masala. Other unusual touches for an Indian restaurant: organic, sustainably raised ingredients and an impressive wine list.

name: Fushimi - Times Square
summary: Fushimi is a buzzing eatery and lounge in Hell's Kitchen near Times Square.
address: 311 West 43rd Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Fushimi is a buzzing eatery and lounge in Hell's Kitchen near Times Square, with striking glossy decor—an appropriate setting for its fusion of traditional Japanese sushi and sashimi with modern French accents. Fushimi also offers creative cocktails, Japanese whiskey, sake and beer.

name: Archer & Goat
summary: An intimate global restaurant in Harlem serves impressive cocktails.
address: 187 Malcolm X Boulevard, New York, New York 10026, United States
summary2: This modern Harlem restaurant stretches along the ground level of a townhouse and features outdoor seating in front and in a back patio. The name Archer & Goat is drawn from the husband-and-wife owners’ zodiac signs: Alex Guzman is a Sagittarius (the Archer) and Jenifar Chowdhury is a Capricorn (the Goat). Their multicultural backgrounds dictate tantalizing dishes that use or combine South American and Indian flavors, like arepas with chicken vindaloo and carne asada with crispy tostones. At brunch, look for hot chicken biscuit sliders sweetened with maple aioli and pickled strawberries.

name: Marsanne
summary: The team at Marsanne are passionate about sharing the rich and diverse flavors of Mediterranean cuisine with the community.
address: 233 8th Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: The team at Marsanne are passionate about sharing the rich and diverse flavors of Mediterranean cuisine with the community. The restaurant was founded by a group of experienced restaurateurs and friends—Miljan Komnenic, Igor Drca, and Milos Kostadinovic teamed up with executive chef Zivko Radojicic— who wanted to bring the warmth and hospitality of the Adriatic Mediterranean coast to Chelsea. They believe that great food has the power to bring people together, and they're committed to providing the most welcoming and inclusive dining experience for everyone who walks through the doors.

name: The Terrace and Outdoor Gardens
summary: Dine amidst the abundant greenery at The Terrace Restaurant, a casual, all-day eatery inspired by the French brasseries and American chophouses chef and restaurateur John Fraser worked at early in his career.
address: 701 7th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Dine amidst the abundant greenery at The Terrace Restaurant, a casual, all-day eatery inspired by the French brasseries and American chophouses chef and restaurateur John Fraser worked at early in his career. The hearty menu includes homemade pastas, steaks, and chops as well as a variety of vegetable dishes, always a signature of Fraser’s restaurants.

name: Sofrito on the Hudson
summary: Throw back a mojito in the dimly lit bar and savor authentic and affordable Latin American cuisine.
summary2: After throwing back a mojito in the dimly lit bar—where rows of liquor bottles are sleekly backlit in blue—and savoring authentic and affordable Puerto Rican cuisine, you’ll quickly get the feeling that you’re not on Sutton Place anymore. Start your meal at Sofrito with an assortment of empanadas or a Puerto Rican-style gumbo, followed by a plate of arroz con pollo (chicken and rice), ropa vieja (shredded beef) or a heaping paella. Sofrito features live Latin music six days a week, with DJs spinning on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.

name: Roey's
summary: This sister restaurant to West Village mainstay Rosemary’s is an all-day Italian café-bar serving wholesome Italian fare in a casual and sophisticated setting.
address: 1 Perry Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Located in Manhattan's West Village, Roey's is a casual eatery inspired by Florence's cafes and Neapolitan pizzerias. A sibling to Rosemary's, it offers Italian cuisine and sourdough pizzas from its wood-burning oven. Renowned for hosting one of the City's best happy hours, Roey's welcomes both friends and families with its seasonal Italian menu. The restaurant features a cozy, hidden standing bar, emphasizing a friendly, neighborhood vibe.

name: Café Boulud
summary: Daniel Boulud's tribute to the original Café Boulud in Lyon, France, serves finely executed cuisine.
address: 100 East 63rd Street, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: Daniel Boulud’s tribute to the original Café Boulud in Lyon, France, this version doesn’t evoke a sense of “town folk charm” like the original does, but it is quite comfortable and well appointed with murals of the French countryside, elegant place settings and even sidewalk seating. The avuncular clientele here enjoy the finely executed cuisine, and the standouts include the Hudson Valley foie gras, the braised octopus terrine and the English pea raviolini with bacon.

name: Strip House Midtown
summary: Strip House Midtown brings all the Strip House signatures to a bi-level space on 44th Street that offers lunch, dinner and private dining.
address: 15 West 44th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Strip House Midtown brings all the Strip House signatures to a bi-level space on 44th Street that offers lunch, dinner and private dining. Diners can relax with a classic cocktail at the bar, or delve into the full steakhouse experience. The charred cuts are paired with decadent sides, and the siren-red interior matches Old World glamour—the walls are adorned with original Studio Manassé prints of 1930s burlesque stars—with modern style and sophistication. The namesake cut isn't the only thing to marvel upon at this restaurant, which was named a top steakhouse by Zagat and awarded four stars by Forbes.

name: Broadway Lounge
summary: With spectacular views of Times Square and sophisticated and comfortable décor, this lounge is perfect for cocktails or pre-theater snacks above Times Square.
address: 1535 Broadway, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: With spectacular views of Times Square and sophisticated and comfortable décor, the all-new Broadway Lounge, located in the New York Marriott Marquis, is perfect for cocktails or pre-theater snacks above Times Square. The Broadway Lounge offers exciting menus, snacks, appetizers and drinks to fit the schedule of those looking for pre- or post-theatre fare. Guests can also enjoy the outdoor patios overlooking Times Square.

name: Zero Otto Nove - Flatiron
summary: Roberto Paciullo's Flatiron District restaurant combines the menu of Paciullo's other Bronx outpost, Roberto's Restaurant, with that of the original Zero Otto Nove.
address: 15 West 21st Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Roberto Paciullo, a native of Salerno (a port city south of Naples) opened the original Zero Otto Nove ("089") on Arthur Avenue in 2008, named after Salerno's telephone area code. Riding a wave of Naples-style pizza fetishism, the place focused on pies, but a full southern Italian bill of fare was also available, delivered in belly-busting portions. This branch in the Flatiron District combines the menu of Paciullo's other Bronx outpost, Roberto's Restaurant, with that of the original Zero Otto Nove.

name: Morandi
summary: Morandi's rustic space is a fitting setting for its sublime Italian dishes.
address: 211 Waverly Place, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Restaurateur Keith McNally named his first Italian trattoria for the still-life painter Giorgio Morandi, an Italian artist from Bologna. Inspired by his images of bottles and glasses as well as his epicurean hometown, Morandi's rustic West Village space has a beautiful tiled floor, exposed brick and a crowd that's a mix of locals and Europeans. Various regions of Italy are represented on the menu, with a wide range of antipasti, pasta and secondi like agnolotti di capesante (scallops ravioli) or meatballs with pine nuts and raisins.

name: Sicily Osteria
summary: Located on Restaurant Row in Manhattan's Theatre District, Sicily Osteria is a dining destination that appeals to local residents and office workers, as well as Broadway theatergoers.
address: 330 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Located on Restaurant Row in Manhattan's Theatre District, Sicily Osteria is a dining destination that appeals to local residents and office workers, as well as Broadway theatergoers. The restaurant offers several dining experiences, from its more formal main dining room that exudes a rustic elegance enhanced by vintage green walls, exposed brick, custom tiled floor and white tablecloths. It's front dining room features an expansive bar, perfect for casual dining; plus, several bistro-style tables; and in the far back, a spacious, naturally lit, enclosed patio garden and atrium transports guests to a lush garden oasis.

name: The Queensboro
summary: This modern, spacious American restaurant also has a great cocktail list.
address: Queens Boulevard, Sunnyside, New York 11104, United States
summary2: The Queensboro opened in 2018 in Jackson Heights with a goal to provide a welcoming environment for great food and drinks and the intention to be a community resource. They serve food inspired by Queens and their team's diverse experiences and cultures. The Queensboro serves locally-brewed beer and coffee roasted in Long Island City by Native Roasters, and they source ingredients from local businesses and the Jackson Heights Farmers Market.

name: Aqua Boil
summary: Aqua Boil is a noteworthy seafood spot serving Cajun-inspired seafood boils, lobster rolls and fried fish platters plus nautically themed cocktails.
address: 750 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Aqua Boil is a noteworthy seafood spot serving Cajun-inspired seafood boils, lobster rolls and fried fish platters plus nautically themed cocktails.

name: Pera SoHo
summary: Pera SoHo is an eastern Mediterranean retreat inspired by its namesake Istanbul neighborhood.
address: 54 Thompson Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Pera SoHo is an eastern Mediterranean retreat inspired by the renowned namesake Istanbul neighborhood where food, culture, nightlife and the cosmopolitan converge. Pera SoHo seduces with an environment that is simultaneously warm and vibrant. The culinary philosophy is to look beyond the current day borders of the eastern Mediterranean and instead appreciate their culinary and cultural richness as a whole. Seasonal garden and rooftop accommodations with 180-degree views of the Manhattan skyline are available.

name: Passerine
summary: This seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District celebrates the intersection of chef Chetan Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy.
address: 36 East 20th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Passerine is a seasonal Indian restaurant in the Flatiron District led by acclaimed chef Chetan Shetty alongside owners Maneesh K. Goyal and Alvina Patel Buxani. The restaurant celebrates the intersection of Chef Shetty’s Indian heritage and New York’s culinary vibrancy, blending traditional Indian techniques with seasonal ingredients sourced from the Union Square Greenmarket and spice blends crafted by Chef Shetty’s mother in Pune. Guests can savor Chef Shetty’s inventive menu in the intimate Drawing Room, the elegant bar, and the vibrant main dining room. There is also a private dining room located downstairs who can host up to 28 guests. Walk-ins are welcome and reservations are available.

name: Estiatorio Milos
summary: Pristine Mediterranean-style seafood shines in an industrial-chic Midtown setting at Milos.
address: 125 West 55th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Pristine Mediterranean-style seafood shines in an industrial-chic Midtown setting at Milos. Amid stark concrete walls and a giant white curtain studded with garlic cloves, customers get to pick their meal from the display of glistening, gorgeous chilled fish. It’s then prepared simply in the kitchen and grilled to perfection with a dash of olive oil and lemon. Just remember that you’ll be charged by the pound, so don’t be too shocked by the bill for that gargantuan Greek snapper.

name: Le Fleur Rouge
summary: Le Fleur Rouge, a unique culinary experience rooted in Brooklyn, merges the vibrant flavors of Chinese cuisine with French culinary finesse, helmed by a Michelin-trained chef.
address: 392 Grand Army Plaza, New York, New York 10019, United States

Additionally, the unique cocktail menu draws inspiration from both cultures, presenting a delightful alchemy of flavors. In a warm and inviting ambiance, the focus on high-quality ingredients, expert service, and exceptional beverages promises an unforgettable journey for all who enter.

name: Next Door

Their thoughtfully crafted menu offers a variety of shareable dishes, exceptional Japanese robata-grilled specialties, exquisite sushi and curated wine selection. The restaurant sources their ingredients from Wegmans' most trusted partners, with their seafood flown in directly from Japan’s famous fish market, exclusively for Next Door.

name: Hard Rock Cafe

address: 1501 Broadway, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: As continually mobbed as the Beatles at Shea, the Hard Rock Café is an ongoing international phenomenon. Waits are common and the volume is up to 11, but the burger and bar-style snacks are hard to resist. Rock and roll memorabilia covers every square inch—remember that Elvis, Led Zeppelin and the Beatles are watching over your every bite.

name: Maizal
summary: Maizal Restaurant is a family-owned restaurant featuring authentic Mexican cuisine from Puebla.
summary2: Maizal Restaurant is a family-owned restaurant featuring authentic Mexican cuisine from Puebla. Opened in early 2010, Maizal does dishes like tequila-lime shrimp, classic pozole and enchiladas topped with labor-intensive mole poblano. You'll also find crowd pleasers like nachos and burritos with all the fixings.

name: Hawksmoor

address: 109 East 22nd Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Hawksmoor was inspired by a labor of love to find the best possible beef and perfect the seemingly simple art of cooking steak. The menu revolves around all-natural beef from family-run farms, many based in upstate New York, Pennsylvania, and New England, simply seasoned with flaked sea salt and seared over live-fire charcoal. Hawksmoor's home, near Gramercy Park in the historic United Charities Building—which was closed from public view for over a century—boasts a 26-foot vaulted ceiling, a 35-seat bar, and two private dining spaces.

name: Tao Uptown

address: 42 East 58th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: For a place to see and be seen, look no further. This pan-Asian hotspot leaves no stone unturned with its menu, which covers Thai, Chinese and Japanese cuisines. Nibble on pork potstickers and Kobe beef with wasabi, or go for broke with the Peking duck for two. The food and the scene will cost you, but you’re sure to leave smiling.

name: Barbalu Bklyn

address: 68 Bergen Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States

name: Alta Calidad
summary: Try innovative Mexican fare in Prospect Heights.
address: 552 Vanderbilt Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11238, United States
summary2: Alta Calidad sets the bar high for modern Mexican fare, particularly with its wide array of tacos made with hand-pressed corn tortillas. The chef at this beachy, windowed storefront in Prospect Heights is Akhtar Nawab, who’s worked at Gramercy Tavern, Craft and La Esquina. Dinner dishes, too, are insanely delicious; you might find octopus skewers over poblano rice or an al pastor pork shoulder. Vegetarians can get in on the madness, too, thanks to pumpkin blossom quesadillas and pea shoot tacos.

name: BOTA Supper Club

summary2: BOTA Supper Club is Staten Island’s hottest destination for elevated modern American cuisine, where chic vibes meet sultry sophistication. Embrace the evening in style—BOTA encourages guests to dress elegantly for the occasion. Tailored shorts are welcome, but athletic wear and baseball caps are not permitted. Dress to impress and enjoy a night of refined luxury.

name: Strip House Downtown

address: 13 East 12th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Strip House Downtown delivers on dishes and décor, creating a steakhouse unlike any other in New York. The menu by executive chef John Schenk features prime cuts of beef charred to perfection, signature side dishes such as truffle creamed spinach and goose fat potatoes, and the famed 24-layer chocolate cake. The wine list is comprehensive and interesting. Part of the experience is the sumptuous, all-red decor, mood lighting and vintage black-and-white photographs. These rare images of captivating females from the original 1900s Studio Manasse collection reference an era of decadence and seduction. Reservations are suggested.

name: Patrick's on the Hill
summary: The menu at this Hamilton Heights restaurant features a mix of traditional Caribbean dishes and creative fusion offerings, with standout favorites like jerk chicken, oxtails, and Jamaican beef patties.

Walk-ins are always welcome, and reservations are accepted up to 28 days in advance.

name: Koi New York
summary: Koi New York's chic and sexy surroundings, inventive cocktails and beloved signature dishes set the scene for a fun and sophisticated dining experience.
address: 40 West 40th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States

Its chic and sexy surroundings, inventive cocktails and beloved signature dishes set the scene for a fun and sophisticated dining experience.

name: La Pecora Bianca NoMad

address: 1133 Broadway, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: This Italian café restaurant has good energy, with an enthusiastic staff and executive chef Cruz Goler in the open kitchen. Goler takes Italian fare back to its roots, sourcing the best local produce, fish, meat and grains and making pasta from scratch. Everything's seasonal; you might encounter dishes like einkorn wheat gramigna (a curled pasta) with pork sausage, garlic and broccolini and chitarra with braised lamb ragu, watercress pesto and citrus breadcrumbs. For drinks, La Pecora Bianca offers an extensive selection of spritzes and negronis made with Italian amari, inspired by the tradition of aperitivi.

name: Frankie & Johnnie’s Steakhouse

address: 320 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: With two locations in Midtown, plus some serious steaks and chops, this welcoming and unpretentious spot has quite the history as a real Prohibition-era speakeasy. name: Maiella

address: 4610 Center Boulevard, Long Island City, New York 11109, United States
summary2: Long Island City’s Maiella brings the feel of a rustic, causally elegant Italian eatery to the Queens waterfront. Located just behind the iconic Pepsi-Cola sign, it features incredible views of the Manhattan skyline as you feast on modern Italian specialties like fresh charcuterie, a homemade pappardelle with lamb ragout and goat cheese, hand-rolled ricotta cavatelli pasta with basil pesto and pine nuts, oven-roasted Cornish hen with porcini mushroom pancetta Brussels sprouts, a pan-seared porter house veal chop, plus a selection of pizzas and other Italian specialties.

name: Tamarind Tribeca

summary2: Avtar Walia, owner of Tamarind in the Flatiron District, has opened Tamarind TriBeCa in a handsome art deco building at the corner of Hudson and Franklin Streets. Further, Tamarind has always focused on pairing fine wines with the dishes Mr. Walia's chefs prepare. Anchoring the dining room at the TriBeCa site is a tandoor kitchen with glass walls and a ceiling-high black metal roof. There's also a mezzanine that is used for dining, private parties and special events.

name: Union Square Cafe

summary2: Atlantis Prime offers a refined surf-and-turf experience near Herald Square in Manhattan. For Restaurant Week, they offer a curated prix fixe menu highlighting their signature dishes.

summary2: Sotto la Luna, located in Astoria, Queens, is an open-kitchen pasta bar and Neapolitan pizzeria that serves modern Italian food in an industrial, high-ceiling, open vibrant space. Guests have the option to sit at the kitchen pasta bar or in the adjacent dining area.

name: Mr Chow New York - 57th Street

summary2: Michael Chow's first New York City location has been an institution for hosting NYC's famous events in the fashion, art and music industries for more than 30 years. Every night since the opening of their first location in London, clients have enjoyed the hand-pulled noodle show.

summary: Midtown East holds a luxurious Northern Chinese restaurant and lounge.
address: 731 Lexington Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Hutong has a dramatic, glittering and sleek interior, occupying the former Le Cirque space. The Northern Chinese restaurant features a hall of illuminated wine bottles stacked floor-to-ceiling that separates the dining room from the bar/lounge. Wherever you sit, get the fiery dan dan noodles in a creamy, pork-laced emulsion, a dim sum platter and ma la chili prawns with garlic and ginger.

name: Rosemary's East

Leave room for the restaurant's equally decadent desserts.

Liebman's is in a well-traveled shopping area of the Bronx, surrounded by quiet, attractive residential streets. They're justly celebrated for sweet-and-sour stuffed cabbage, matzo ball soup and sliced brisket of beef. Hot dog fans will also be pleased by the mustard-slicked version found here. Round, homemade knishes filled with potato, kasha, meat or spinach are another specialty.

name: Qanoon

address: 180 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Qanoon is a nostalgic Middle Eastern tribute to chef-owner Tarek Daka’s vivid memories of his mother’s Palestinian cooking. The contemporary, brick-walled Chelsea space has 40 seats at tables plus 10 at the broad bar. Share thick, satisfying spreads like muhammara, a blend of walnuts, sun-dried peppers and pomegranate molasses (meant to be scooped up with soft pita). The tabbouleh is bright with parsley and mint. Another must-have is a pita pocket sandwich of kofta (meatballs) and cauliflower dripping with tahini.

name: Bobo

address: 181 West 10th Street, New York, New York 10014, United States

address: 30 West 39th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States

This stylish Nolita eatery also offers a selection of tapas and extensive list of wines.

name: Akoya

name: Glass House Tavern

Fresh, seasonal ingredients are the emphasis here, including a daily fish special, fresh salmon and trout, and several succulent meat options. The warm, inviting bar is the perfect place to enjoy a drink, and the late-night menu is available until 3am.

name: The Flatiron Room - NoMad

summary2: Since opening in 2012, The Flatiron Room has reenergized the Manhattan nightlife scene as a home for nostalgia. Try small plates like shrimp and scallop meatballs or chimichurri steak bites, or main dishes like bourbon smoked fried chicken under glass (with ghost pepper honey) or bison and bacon meatloaf.

name: Takumen

address: 5-50 50th Avenue, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States

The kitchen is open, and a compact bar displays shelves of highly sought-after sake. In addition to sashimi, sushi rolls and restorative ramen noodles are big salads like black sesame and kale with fried peanuts. Hawaiian tuna poke is another standout, the rosy fish cubes heaped over rice and circled by avocado salad, seaweed salad, potato salad, tangy cauliflower and broccoli.

name: Ben & Jack's 44th Street

If you can manage to squeeze in dessert, try the hot-fudge sundae or the German apple strudel. An extensive wine list is available too.

name: Tasca NYC

name: Rivercrest

Blackbarn features four distinct private dining rooms including a wine cellar, with full dining capacity of 500 guests for corporate, social and wedding events.

name: Zuma

Its three kitchens present authentic yet alluring options, with bold flavors and simple presentation, highlighting quality ingredients.

name: T. Brasserie

name: Mr Chow New York - Tribeca

The menu offers both authentic Beijing cuisine and Mr Chow’s original recipes like chicken satay, Mr Chow Noodles, green prawns and ma mignon. There’s also live entertainment nightly as the skilled pasta chefs demonstrate the artistry of the original Beijing style of hand-pulled noodle-making.

name: Tha Phraya
