address: 1553 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10028, United States
summary2: Enjoy pure, original, unfiltered Thai food on Manhattan's Upper East Side at Tha Phraya. Chef Rattana has more than 15 years culinary experience in New York, and comes from a family of restaurateurs in Thailand. Her menu consists of authentic, homestyle traditional dishes from Thailand with amazing flavors in all their glory, with a focus on high quality ingredients to maintain the high standard of Thai cuisine.

name: Torch & Crown Brewing Company

address: 12 Vandam Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Torch & Crown Brewing Company is Manhattan’s only production brewery and restaurant, a thirst-quenching gathering place with a New York-centric food and drinks program. A full outdoor seating area gives you easy access to the sunshine and vibrancy of the City.

name: Copinette

summary2: Midtown East's Copinette serves American cuisine with strong French influences. The dining room has modern decor, and there is a heated canopy for outdoor dining. The menu encompasses dishes such as pan-roasted salmon, steak frites and some Italian-leaning entrees like fettucine Bolognese.

name: Jazba
summary: Jazba is a tribute and celebration of India's famous eateries—their take on some of the iconic dishes which are more than a century old.
address: 207 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Jazba is a vibrant new East Village restaurant from the team behind the trailblazing Flatiron District Indian restaurant, Junoon. Jazba is a tribute and celebration of India's famous eateries—their take on some of the iconic dishes which are more than a century old. These diverse eateries, integral to India’s culinary identity, typically serve a single specialty dish until sold out for the day. Jazba's menu is inspired by the soul and diversity of these eateries’ strong connection to the roots that run deep across the country, bringing India’s beloved everyday dining culture to the East Village.

name: Benjamin Prime
summary: Offering high quality food in luxurious environments, Benjamin Prime melds together classic steakhouse fare and fresh and vibrant seafood with the grill as the main focus.
address: 23 East 40th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Founded in 2006, the family owned and operated Benjamin Restaurant Group has grown to comprise some of the New York metro area's premier culinary destinations, including Benjamin Steakhouse and The Sea Fire Grill. Offering high quality food in luxurious environments, Benjamin Prime melds together classic steakhouse fare and fresh and vibrant seafood with the grill as the main focus. All locations offer the quintessential New York dining experience that business executives, locals and celebrities have come to know and love.

name: Ai Fiori
summary: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue’s signature restaurant celebrates cuisine from the Italian and French Riviera.
address: 400 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue’s signature restaurant, from acclaimed chef Michael White and the Altamarea Group, Ai Fiori celebrates cuisine from the Italian and French Riviera. The inspired menu blends traditional Italian fare with a brave, modern perspective. Ai Fiori features an inviting bar and lounge with an extensive cocktail and wine list crafted by the restaurant's renowned beverage professionals. Located a short walk up the Langham’s sweeping grand staircase to the second floor, Ai Fiori's ambiance is elegant yet welcoming. The restaurant's striking floral arrangements and décor will embrace you in warmth and refinement.

name: Pastai
summary: Located in the heart of West Chelsea, near the Highline, Pastai is a Southern Italian restaurant and bar, serving dishes inspired by their family tradition.
address: 186 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Located in West Chelsea, near the Highline, Pastai is a Southern Italian restaurant and bar, serving dishes inspired by their family tradition. They hope to inspire curiosity about the fresh house-made pastas and other dishes they serve from their open kitchen. When dining at Pastai, you become part of their personal family narrative and get to witness the journey the pasta has taken to arrive on your plate.

name: Tuome
summary: Tuome is a critically acclaimed East Village restaurant by chef/owner Thomas Chen, whose ingredient-driven contemporary American menu showcases his classic culinary training with Asian influences.
address: 536 East 5th Street, New York, New York 10009, United States
summary2: Tuome is a critically acclaimed East Village restaurant by chef/owner Thomas Chen, whose ingredient-driven contemporary American menu showcases his classic culinary training with Asian influences. The menu features items like octopus with pork XO sauce; chicken liver mousse with New York maple; and crispy deviled eggs with chili; and larger dishes like chicken porridge with basil sauce, and fan favorite, Pig Out for two (Berkshire pork, spicy peanut noodle and condiments), along with sides like sticky rice with duck fat. Evoking the East Village's relaxed character, the intimate space showcases rustic reclaimed materials given a modern update.

name: Antica Pesa
summary: The Willliamsburg, Brooklyn eatery is the sister restaurant of the well-known Roman dining establishment, which has been run by the same family.
address: 115 Berry Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Antica Pesa Brooklyn, "your home away from Rome," opened in 2012 as the first outpost of the legendary restaurant owned and operated by the Panella family since 1922 in Rome, Italy. Antica Pesa is named after the antique scales of the 17th-century customs post in Trastevere where Antica Pesa Rome stands today. Antica Pesa Brooklyn pays homage to their homeland with a focus on the traditionally innovative dishes that transport diners directly to Rome.

name: Filé Gumbo Bar
summary: Beyond the signature gumbo, dining at Filé is an educational feast of the culinary subtleties of Cajun and Creole food.
address: 275 Church Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Filé Gumbo Bar is inspired by the iconic ingredient used to thicken and flavor their gumbo. The name refers to the dried and ground leaves of the North American sassafras tree—an essential ingredient introduced to the Cajuns by the Choctaw Indians in the 18th century. The centerpiece of the menu is Tiny’s Gumbo, inspired by the owner’s larger-than-life grandfather, Aubrey “Tiny” Gaines, who believed there was nothing better than shellfish and spice. Beyond the signature gumbo, dining at Filé is an educational feast of the culinary subtleties of Cajun and Creole food.

name: Robert
summary: Robert, located atop the Museum of Arts and Design on Columbus Circle, offers an expansive view of Central Park and Broadway.
address: 2 Columbus Circle, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Robert, located atop the Museum of Arts and Design on Columbus Circle, offers an expansive view of Central Park and Broadway. Celebratory and romantic, Robert serves modern American cuisine from Chef Armando Cortes. Robert is open for lunch, brunch and dinner, and features live jazz music five times a week. Reservations are recommended and accepted up to 30 days in advance. Call if you are hoping for a window table.

name: Bar Primi - Penn District
summary: Bar Primi is a casual Italian pasta shop devoted to "primi piatti," the pasta course.
address: 349 West 33rd Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Bar Primi is a casual Italian pasta shop devoted to "primi piatti," the pasta course. What began as an idea for a small space in Manhattan’s East Village has since become a downtown New York staple, housed on the Bowery for the last ten years. With this second location in the Penn District area of Chelsea, the team carries on the same tried and true methods of making fresh pasta traditionally prepared and cooked to order, using a variety of non-GMO semolina and specialty ‘00’ flours, organic eggs and family recipes.

name: J’s On The Bay
summary: Chef Joe Salimeni recreates classic American dishes using fresh local ingredients with a focused seasonal menu.
summary2: Chef Joe Salimeni opened J’s On The Bay in Rosebank, Staten Island, in 2014 as a hip, playful retro diner with the vision of transforming it into the trendy New American restaurant it is today. His mission from its inception was to recreate classic American dishes using fresh local ingredients with a focused seasonal menu.

name: Tarallucci e Vino - Upper West Side
summary: Tarallucci e Vino Upper West Side is a locals’ favorite restaurant known for expertly crafted coffee, housemade pastries, fresh pastas and authentic Italian cuisine.
address: 475 Columbus Avenue, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: Tarallucci e Vino Upper West Side is a locals’ favorite restaurant known for expertly crafted coffee, house-made pastries, fresh pastas and authentic Italian cuisine. The restaurant and its outdoor patio are a cozy spot for quick breakfasts, elegant lunches, relaxed dinners or lazy weekend brunches. Located a short walking distance from The American Museum of Natural History and Central Park, Tarallucci e Vino Upper West Side welcomes New Yorkers and visitors alike for a bite to eat or some people-watching with a happy hour drink.

name: Amali
summary: Chef Alex Tubero's updated Mediterranean menu features house-made pasta, sustainably caught seafood, seasonal produce and meat from family farms.
address: 115 East 60th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Amali’s aesthetic is inspired by the Mediterranean way of life, emphasizing vegetables, olive oil, cheese, grains and fish. Chef Alex Tubero's updated Mediterranean menu features house-made pasta, sustainably caught seafood, seasonal produce and meat from family farms. The menu is suitable for a variety of diets including gluten-free, dairy-free, vegetarian and vegan. Their wine list offers approximately 400 selections and has been called one of the best Mediterranean selections in Midtown.

name: La Masseria
summary: Masseria means farmhouse in Italian, and this restaurant’s inspiration is evident in the stone walls and exposed wooden beams.
address: 235 West 48th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Masseria means farmhouse in Italian, and this restaurant’s inspiration is evident in the stone walls and exposed wooden beams. La Masseria is close to Broadway, making it an ideal pre-theater dining alternative to Times Square’s chain restaurants. Warm and inviting, this West Side jewel serves scrumptious dishes from the Puglia region in Italy. A large assortment of entrees satisfies the pasta-lover, the carnivore and the vegetarian alike.

name: Altesi Downtown
summary: You don't have to go all the way to Italy for authentic Tuscan cuisine—just as far as Spring Street.
address: 200 Spring Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: You don’t have to go all the way to Italy for authentic Tuscan cuisine—just as far as Spring Street. Altesi Downtown's light, healthy and seasonal menu uses locally procured ingredients to create its traditional Italian dishes, like goat cheese ravioli and grigliata di pesce, a grilled seafood medley. If the weather is cooperating during the milder months, dine alfresco at Altesi Downtown’s roomy sidewalk tables. The wine list is finely curated, but real connoisseurs will want to take a seat in Boutique del Vino, the restaurant’s wine bar.

name: The Ivory Peacock
summary: The Ivory Peacock offers distinct, imaginative cocktails complemented by a variety of vibrant shareable plates.
address: 38 West 26th Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Perched within Manhattan's Flatiron and NoMad neighborhoods, The Ivory Peacock pays homage to its original location, which boasts 139 years of history as a bona fide neighborhood destination. As such, they pride themselves on offering distinct, imaginative cocktails complemented by a variety of vibrant shareable plates. The cocktail program, led by head bartenders Carlos Soto and Daniel Benitez, is filled with seasonal spins on classic cocktails utilizing technical French kitchen techniques. The culinary roster includes a raw bar with fresh oysters arriving daily and a selection of familiar French fare—deemed "luxe finger food" by chef Grayson Altenberg.

name: Brooklyn Chop House - Downtown
summary: This clubby Financial District spot serves steakhouse classics and Asian dishes in an airy industrial space.
address: 150 Nassau Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: This clubby Financial District spot serves steakhouse classics and Asian dishes in an airy industrial space. Dine on strip steak, rib-eye or filet mignon, and enjoy clever appetizers like deli-sandwich-influenced dumplings (including pastrami and Rueben). There are plenty of other options, too—including chopped house salads, Kung Pao chicken and a slow-roasted seven-pound Peking duck.

name: HanGawi
summary: Slide off your shoes and sit down on a comfortable pillow at this fine-dining establishment serving Korean-inspired vegetarian cuisine in Manhattan's Koreatown.
address: 12 East 32nd Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Slide off your shoes and sit down on a comfortable pillow at this fine-dining establishment serving Korean-inspired vegetarian cuisine in Manhattan's Koreatown. The menu offers exquisite meals showcasing the flavors of mushrooms, vegetables and tofu and includes both a la carte selections as well as prix-fixe options. Dishes like porridge, Mongolian hot pot and tofu pudding mingle with the serene atmosphere, heightening the culinary experience.

name: Suprema Provisions
summary: Suprema, home of the top-rated burger in NYC, was inspired by the great salumerias of Rome, tapas bars of Barcelona and sidewalk cafés of Paris.
address: 305 Bleecker Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Suprema, home of one of the top-rated burgers in NYC, was inspired by the great salumerias of Rome, tapas bars of Barcelona and sidewalk cafés of Paris. The restaurant offers a standout selection of pasta, salumi and cheese boards, small plates, and savory entrées, including the award-winning Suprema Burger, along with a fine wine and cocktail program crafted by renowned sommelier Joshua Wesson. From truffled deviled eggs to pork shoulder lasagna, Suprema's menu journeys across Europe and America, with a particular emphasis on artisanal cured meat and cheese, and small-production wines, beers, and spirits.

name: Leonetta
summary: Bringing Mediterranean warmth to Murray Hill at the edge of Kips Bay, Leonetta offers a refined yet inviting dining experience inspired by the coastal flavors of Southern Europe.
address: 181 Lexington Avenue, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Bringing Mediterranean warmth to Murray Hill at the edge of Kips Bay, Leonetta offers a refined yet inviting dining experience inspired by the coastal flavors of Southern Europe. Helmed by Top Chef finalist Ed Cotton, the menu blends traditional techniques with modern flair, rooted in fresh, seasonal ingredients. The villa-inspired space features more than 100 live plants and a raw bar, while downstairs, Leo’s Famous cocktail lounge invites guests to unwind with expertly crafted drinks in a stylish, intimate setting.

name: The Bronx Beer Hall
summary: In historic Arthur Avenue Retail Market, Bronx Beer Hall offers a selection of local craft beers and food.
address: Avenue, New York, New York 10039, United States
summary2: The Bronx Beer Hall is the premier destination for New York State craft beer in the Bronx. Nestled in the historic Arthur Avenue Retail Market, the beer hall offers a rotating selection of local craft beers, as well as a food menu sourced from within the market and neighborhood merchants. The Bronx Beer Hall features a full event calendar that includes karaoke, trivia and live music.

name: Baci & Abbracci
summary: Baci & Abbracci offers traditional Neapolitan fare as well as Italian classics from all over the "Boot."
address: 204 Grand Street, Brooklyn, New York 11211, United States
summary2: Baci & Abbracci offers traditional Neapolitan fare as well as Italian classics from all over the "Boot." The Cappiello brothers, Paolo and Mimmo, along with partner Rocco Cadolini, opened their doors in 2006 and have kept the business a family affair since its inception. Whether it's personally shopping for the freshest, local ingredients or hand making the pasta and mozzarella, Baci & Abbracci strives for excellence and authenticity. Even Mother Rosa lends a hand, making her Sorrentinian delicacies. Winner of Eat Out NY's "Best New Pizza Joint" 2007 and Michelin Guide recommended, Baci & Abbracci features a variety of pizza baked in a wood burning over imported directly from Naples.

name: Manhatta
summary: Feast on stunning views of the City and a compelling New American menu.
address: 28 Liberty Street, New York, New York 10005, United States
summary2: Manhatta is a restaurant from Danny Meyer’s USHG, located at the top of the 28 Liberty building in Lower Manhattan. Leading the kitchen is executive chef Jason Pfeifer, whose New American cooking is served à la carte at lunch on weekdays and prix fixe at dinner and weekend lunch, with a bar menu available throughout the day. Set 60 stories high over Liberty Street with 360 degree exposures, Manhatta and its adjacent event space offer stunning views extending north to Midtown, east to Brooklyn’s bridges and waterways, and southwest to New York Harbor and the Statue of Liberty.

name: Malibu Farm
summary: An indoor-outdoor, California-style restaurant that has views of the Brooklyn Bridge from Pier 17.
summary2: This sprawling, relaxed ode to Southern California is on the revamped Pier 17 in the Seaport District, sporting views of docked tall ships and the Brooklyn Bridge. Proprietor-chef Helene Henderson started out on a West Coast pier (in Malibu, naturally), with a mission to source ingredients from small farms and sustainable fisheries. Fish tacos and cauliflower crust “pizza” crowned with mozzarella and tomatoes are brightly flavored pleasures, as is the fried egg sandwich (when available)—one of the best around.

name: Cosme
summary: Mexican inspired rather than straightforward Mexican describes the innovative, vibrant dishes at Enrique Olvera's Cosme.
address: 35 East 21st Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Mexican inspired rather than straightforward Mexican describes the innovative, vibrant dishes at Enrique Olvera's Cosme. This Flatiron District venue manages to be both casual and top-drawer thanks to its savvy chef, who trained at the Culinary Institute of America and knows what New Yorkers like. Olvera, who has the critically acclaimed restaurant Pujol in Mexico City plus a few others in Mexico, sources the best chilies, heirloom beans and corn from his native country and looks to local purveyors for meat, fish and seasonal produce. There are roughly 130 seats spread out over the ample bar area and back dining room and a 14-seat private room for parties.

name: Maya
summary: Chef Richard Sandoval’s modern Mexican restaurant evokes the essence of Acapulco, from its decor to its cuisine.
address: 1191 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: Chef Richard Sandoval’s modern Mexican restaurant evokes the essence of Acapulco, from its decor to its cuisine. Sandoval blends earthy traditional flavors with global influences and creative techniques. With guacamole served in lava-rock bowls and a tequila list a mile long, Maya is a destination for brunch, dinner and happy hour specials.

name: Ammos Estiatorio - Grand Central
summary: Features upscale authentic cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences.
address: 52 Vanderbilt Avenue, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Open design, light woods and weathered stones conjure the sun-drenched atmosphere of the Greek islands at Ammos, which features upscale authentic Greek cuisine from various regions of Greece, emphasizing seafood and incorporating Mediterranean and North African influences. Many of the ingredients—sea salt, dried oregano, capers and caperberries—are imported from Greece, while many of the staples like olive oil, honey and halloumi cheese are produced on a family farm in Cyprus. The wine list, featuring 200 Greek wines, is supplemented by signature cocktails and an extensive list of beers, liquors and spirits.

name: La Voglia
summary: La Voglia is an elegant restaurant offering contemporary interpretations of Italian classics on the Upper East Side.
address: 1645 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10128, United States
summary2: La Voglia is an elegant uptown restaurant offering contemporary interpretations of Italian classics on Manhattan's Upper East Side. The inviting atmosphere sets the stage for a delightful dining experience. Indulge in the meticulously crafted menu that masterfully blends classic recipes with a contemporary touch.

name: Le Rock
summary: Le Rock is a bustling French Brasserie that serves traditional French fare alongside some more unexpected offerings.
address: 45 Rockefeller Plaza, New York, New York 10111, United States
summary2: Le Rock is a bustling French Brasserie that serves traditional French fare alongside some more unexpected offerings, such as crisp barbajuans, Duck au Épices, and Halibut au Vin Jaune. To celebrate New York Restaurant Week, Le Rock offers a four-course lunch menu featuring its signature dishes and seasonal selections.

name: 5 Napkin Burger - Hell's Kitchen
summary: 5 Napkin Burger serves up hearty and delightful fare, including their signature burger.
address: 630 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Offering elevated comfort-food classics and mixed drinks, 5 Napkin Burger serves up hearty and delightful fare. Consider the signature burger, for instance: 10 oz. of all-natural beef, Gruyère cheese, caramelized onions and rosemary-garlic aioli. In other words, bring an appetite.

name: Cafe D'Alsace
summary: Café D'Alsace has been an Upper East Side institution for more than two decades, serving Alsatian cuisine in a uniquely special setting.
address: 1703 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10128, United States
summary2: Café D'Alsace has been an Upper East Side institution for more than two decades, serving Alsatian cuisine in a uniquely special setting. Entirely New York owned and operated, they buy local whenever possible, and love serving their community and this great city. Executive chef Philippe Roussel is one of New York's greatest, working at iconic restaurants from Windows on the World to Restaurant Daniel. His dedication to culinary excellence is reflected in every plate, and has drawn recognition from the likes of the New York Times, Wine Spectator, Eater, Forbes, and more.

name: Dagg Thai
summary: In Thai, "Dagg" means to eat in the warmest, friendliest way possible, just like inviting close friends to enjoy a meal together.
address: 10 East 39th Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: In Thai, "Dagg" means to eat in the warmest, friendliest way possible, just like inviting close friends to enjoy a meal together. Dagg Thai, in Midtown Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood, brings patrons that same easygoing, heartfelt experience. Their dishes are served with a side of warmth, just as you’d find in a Thai family kitchen.

name: Rossini's
summary: Located in charming Murray Hill, Rossini's has been serving fine Northern Italian cuisine since 1978.
address: 108 East 38th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Located in charming Murray Hill, Rossini's has been serving fine Northern Italian cuisine since 1978. The genuine friendliness and warm service make diners feel right at home in this family-owned restaurant. Select from a wide variety of pasta, veal or fish entrees that reflect their Northern Italian roots, as well as selections from throughout other regions of Italy. Music is an important part of the dining experience: Rossini's features a pianist nightly from Sunday to Friday, and Saturday evenings they present the "Trio Romantico," which performs light opera and Broadway favorites—requests are always accepted.

name: The Independent
summary: The Independent is a snug and stylish space for notable drinks and food in Times Square, not far from Broadway theaters, the Garment District and Bryant Park.
address: 147 West 40th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: The Independent is a snug, stylish space for drinks and food in Times Square, not far from Broadway theaters, the Garment District and Bryant Park. You’ll find handcrafted cocktails, local beers and approachable wines paired with a creative menu for lunch, a pre-theater bite or post-theater nightcap, after-work drinks or dinner.

name: La Gioconda
summary: La Gioconda focuses on typical regional Italian cuisine using the finest ingredients
address: 226 East 53rd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: La Gioconda, which is the Italian name for Leonardo Da Vinci’s Mona Lisa, focuses on typical regional Italian cuisine using the finest ingredients—something it has done since opening in 1993. They offer more than 30 wines by the glass and 60 by the bottle; pair them with pasta dishes and cold-cut meat and cheese selections.

name: Il Carino
summary: Il Carino’s pride is their delicious, cooked-with-care Italian cuisines, and fine service to meet patrons' needs.
address: 1710 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10128, United States
summary2: Opened in 2017, Il Carino’s pride is their delicious, cooked-with-care Italian cuisines, and fine service to meet patrons' needs. It's a high-class restaurant hosting an intimate, tranquil, and romantic setting. Il Carino is a small business that embraces Italian culture in their Upper East Side neighborhood and strives to live the old school Italian dream.

name: Nar Restaurant
summary: Nar Restaurant serves reimagined regional Turkish cuisine, sourced to be clean, organic, and halal-certified.
address: 34 East 20th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Partners Andy E. Arkun, Erhan Bahceci and Zeynep Tansug brought together a team of Turkish chefs to execute their vision of reimagined regional Turkish cuisine. Nar Restaurant sources produce from the Union Square Farmers Market and proteins from Amish Country in Pennsylvania to serve clean, organic, halal-certified food. The restaurant offers a thoughtful wine list of 100+ selections that focuses on producers from Spain, France, Italy, and Turkey. An innovative Turkish-inspired cocktail menu that uses all house made juices and syrups and Turkish ingredients headlines the bar program, which also includes an extensive selection of craft beers.

name: Tavern on the Green
summary: One of NYC's most recognizable restaurants is tucked just inside Central Park. It serves up American fare in an elegant indoor-outdoor setting.
summary2: Restaurateurs Jim Caiola and David Salama have created a Tavern on the Green for this generation of diners. Jim and David's aim to re-establish Tavern on the Green as a restaurant for all, New Yorkers and visitors alike, restores this renowned dining hub to its Upper West Side neighborhood. Tavern on the Green celebrates New York and Central Park in all its glory, embracing the limitless, delicious foods for which this diverse culinary city is known. The menu by Executive Chef Tomas Surowka is celebratory and accessible with a nod to Tavern's storied history.

name: Rosemary's Midtown
summary: The beloved West Village institution comes to Midtown with another sun-filled dining room, large sidewalk cafe, beautiful private dining room, spacious bar and wine bar.
address: 825 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: The beloved West Village institution comes to Midtown with another sun-filled dining room, large sidewalk cafe, beautiful private dining room, spacious bar and wine bar, and a separate grab-and-go Pantry counter. Crowds continue to flock to Rosemary's for their familial hospitality, elegant yet fun ambiance, community engagement, and seasonal Italian cooking that highlights locally-sourced produce, hand-shaped pastas, and ingredients from their rooftop farm. The Midtown menu adds Neapolitan pizza and a reasonably-priced familial dining experience, La Sagra, which showcases the best of Rosemary's seasonally.

name: Havana Central
summary: Through its festive ambiance, vibrant décor and mouth-watering food, dining at Havana Central is like taking a mini vacation.
address: 151 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Havana Central evokes the 1950s golden era of Cuba, capturing Havana’s heyday as the world’s most tantalizing playground. Through its festive ambiance, vibrant décor and mouth-watering food, dining at Havana Central is like taking a mini vacation. Traditional dishes like vaca frita, ropa vieja and arroz con pollo are a celebration of Cuban cuisine, and the cocktail list includes some of the best mojitos and sangrias in New York.

name: Jade Eatery & Lounge
summary: Jade Eatery & Lounge serves favorite Pan-Asian and southeast Asian dishes, as well as creative culinary innovations that have become neighborhood favorites.
address: 11375 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Nestled into a cobblestone square next to a Long Island Railroad station, Jade Eatery & Lounge's address hints at why it's said to be "Forest Hills' hidden gem." The space integrates a zen-like atmosphere with inspirational quotes that adorn the walls, a serene koi pond, and a large Buddha statue smiling benevolently on guests guiding them to a choice entree. Jade serves favorite Pan-Asian and southeast Asian dishes, as well as creative culinary innovations that have become neighborhood favorites, including signature dishes like Sushi Pizza and Calcutta Chicken.

name: Barawine
summary: This chic wine bar—overseen by Fabrice Warin, a restaurateur with roots in upmarket New York institutions like François Payard Bakery and Le Cercle Rouge—is an oenophile's dream.
address: 200 Malcolm X Boulevard, New York, New York 10027, United States
summary2: This chic wine bar—overseen by Fabrice Warin, a restaurateur with roots in upmarket New York institutions like François Payard Bakery and Le Cercle Rouge—is an oenophile’s dream. It has a list of 200 wines by the bottle, originating from vineyards in South Africa, Europe, the US and Australia. If you’re not in the mood for vino, you can still avail yourself of the spot’s craft beer selection or bistro fare like branzino Provencal and roasted duck.

name: Francie
summary: Francie is a New American brasserie serving a menu inspired by French and Italian flavors.
address: 136 Broadway, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Francie is a New American brasserie serving a menu inspired by French and Italian flavors. There are snacks, shellfish, handmade pastas, and Crown Roast of Duck for two. Francie has a full wine list and bar as well.

name: The Dram Shop Bar
summary: The Dram Shop Bar is a locally owned sports bar and restaurant in Park Slope.
address: 339 North 9th Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: The Dram Shop Bar is a locally owned sports bar and restaurant in Park Slope, Brooklyn. For over 15 years, Dram Shop has been serving classic American dishes with a Tex-Mex twist—chicken wings, the Dram burger, salads, nachos, tacos, and more—all made fresh daily, alongside a wide selection of beers, liquors and cocktails, served by a friendly and welcoming staff. Dram Shop is the perfect destination to eat and drink, watch your favorite team, play pool and have fun. They offer indoor and outdoor dining, games, vegetarian options, free delivery, and they're family friendly.

name: Molyvos
summary: A meal at this high-end Midtown eatery is sure to put you in a sunny mood.
address: 402 West 43rd Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Molyvos is a celebration of the Livanos Family’s ancestral hometown on the island of Lesvos, offering a fresh perspective that blends the modern energy and ancient culture that make Greece one of the most spectacular places in the world. Molyvos celebrates the lifestyle and foodways of Greece, bringing filoxenia—Greek style of hospitality—to Hell’s Kitchen, a block from the Theatre District. Molyvos offers a variety of spreads, seasonal raw seafood dishes, whole grilled fish, and beloved classics alongside the country’s largest cellar of wines exclusively from Greece.

name: Gui Steakhouse
summary: Gui Steakhouse is elevated steakhouse experience that integrates the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling.
address: 776 8th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: The team behind Gui Steakhouse wanted to create an elevated steakhouse experience by integrating the unique flavors and techniques of Korean beef grilling. Unlike traditional steak preparation, the Korean method highlights diverse charms and tastes, which they've modernized to bring a distinctive twist to the classic steakhouse concept. This Times Square restaurant takes pride in the quality of their premium steaks, which stems from two main partnerships that ensure they always have access to exceptional beef. These partnerships are carefully selected based on their commitment to sustainable farming methods and superior animal husbandry: Creekstone Farms is committed to excellence, combining superior Black Angus and Duroc genetics, top-tier livestock management, and advanced processing; and Pat LaFrieda Meat Purveyors has delivered butchery excellence for 100 years, sourcing premium meats from small domestic farms, offering all-natural, organic, and grass-fed options.

name: Benoit Restaurant & Wine Bar
summary: There were high expectations for this Midtown French bistro even before the doors opened, as it was the latest in the restaurant family of Alain Ducasse, arguably the top French chef in the world.
address: 60 West 55th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: There were high expectations for this Midtown French bistro even before the doors opened, as it was the latest in the restaurant family of Alain Ducasse, arguably the top French chef in the world. An airy, open space with comfortable red banquettes, Benoit does not disappoint. Each traditional French dish, from the pâté en croûte appetizer to the roasted chicken with garlic cloves and French fries, is made with love and authenticity.

name: Stout NYC Financial District
summary: You’ll find all the signature Stout NYC favorites here on the corner of John and Gold Streets in the Financial District.
address: 90 John Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: You’ll find all the signature Stout NYC favorites here on the corner of John and Gold Streets in the Financial District. If your office is in the area, drop in for lunch or a well-deserved after-work drink. Stout NYC hosts a bottomless brunch on the weekends. It's also the best meeting point if you’re headed to an event at the Seaport (or leaving one).

name: The Chemistry Room
summary: The Chemistry Room is an innovative and modern take on traditional Japanese cuisine that combines tradition with unforgettable modern flair.
address: 132 West 47th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: The Chemistry Room is an innovative and modern take on traditional Japanese cuisine that provides a dining experience rooted in tradition, combined with unforgettable modern flair. With culinary inspirations from Japan, France and Italy, The Chemistry Room features an omakase tasting menu with the highest quality of sourced items that bring together subtle and robust flavors. For $125 per person, there's a 15-course tasting menu by executive chef Frankie Chen. Guest will enjoy an up-close and intimate dining experience where fresh seasonal ingredients are used to curate a mouth-watering and innovative omakase.

name: The Flatiron Room - Murray Hill
summary: The experience at The Flatiron Room - Murray Hill is meant to be a theatrical and memorable trip to Old New York.
address: 9 East 37th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Crafted by Michelin-starred culinary director Jiho Kim—and brought to life by chef de cuisine Randle Pagaragn and kitchen manager William Kyaw—The Flatiron Room - Murray Hill's menu reflects New American cuisine with strong Asian influences. The experience at The Flatiron Room - Murray Hill is meant to be a theatrical and memorable trip to old New York. The live jazz every night makes for the perfect background music to accompany the over-the-top cocktails, diverse wine selection and elegant cuisine.

name: RA Sushi Bar Restaurant – Times Square
summary: RA Sushi serves up a fresh, creative, Japanese menu with a unique blend of creative sushi and an innovative menu from the kitchen.
address: 229 West 43rd Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: RA Sushi in Times Square serves up a fresh, creative, Japanese menu with a unique blend of creative sushi and an innovative menu from the kitchen. Join RA for a casual lunch in the afternoons, a night out in the evenings or a RA'ckin Happy Hour (offered Monday–Saturday from 3–6pm).

name: Wagamama - Nomad/Flatiron
summary: Wagamama first opened in London in April of 1992 with a clear purpose: to feed guests fresh and nourishing Asian food inspired by the flavors of Japan.
address: 210 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Wagamama first opened in London in April of 1992 with a clear purpose: to feed guests fresh and nourishing Asian food inspired by the flavors of Japan. Their 210 Fifth Avenue location is Wagamama’s first restaurant in New York City. Their food and juices are made in open kitchens. The Fifth Avenue location offers a full bar and cocktail menu—another first for Wagamama.

name: Pete's Tavern
summary: Pete's Tavern is the oldest continuously operating bar and restaurant in New York City.
address: 129 East 18th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Pete's Tavern, the oldest continuously operating bar and restaurant in New York City, opened its doors in 1864 and remained open as a speakeasy throughout prohibition. Since then, Pete's Tavern has remained exactly as it was when the doors opened, with a beautiful original rosewood bar, pressed tin ceiling and original tiled floor. In 1905, O.Henry wrote "The Gift of the Magi" in the first booth in the bar room. The food, beverages and service are all outstanding, and this historic restaurant is a must-visit for New Yorkers and tourists alike.

name: Danji
summary: Danji showcases authentic Korean flavors prepared with classic techniques to enhance the taste, textures and aesthetic of each dish.
address: 346 West 52nd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Danji showcases authentic Korean flavors prepared with classic techniques to enhance the taste, textures and aesthetic of each dish. They offer small but shareable portions served in multiple courses, allowing diners to enjoy each dish hot out of the kitchen. From its decor to its music, Danji represents the owners' idea of a great place to enjoy amazing food. Danji uses meat raised with no antibiotics or growth hormones, their fish are caught wild but not overfished or endangered, they strive to use organic and local produce, and do not use chemicals, such as MSG, to enhance flavors.

name: Lincoln Ristorante
summary: Lincoln Ristorante combines Chef Shea Gallante’s refined interpretation of Italian cuisine with the vision of restaurateur Nick Valenti.
address: 142 West 65th Street, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Lincoln Ristorante offers guests an authentic interpretation of Italian cuisine in New York at Lincoln Center. While the restaurant boasts breathtaking panoramic views of Lincoln Center’s reflecting pool and Henry Moore sculpture and a grass lawn roof, the heart lies within its central open kitchen. Featuring an all-Italian wine list with over 350 selections, and a bespoke build-your-own Negroni Bar program.

name: Dante
summary: Founded more than 110 years ago, Caffe Dante is the legendary Greenwich Village restaurant and bar on MacDougal Street that helped define New York’s aperitivo culture.
address: 79-81 Macdougal Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Founded more than 110 years ago, Caffe Dante is the legendary Greenwich Village restaurant and bar on MacDougal Street that helped define New York’s aperitivo culture. A beloved neighborhood institution with a global reputation, Dante has been honored as World’s Best Bar and North America’s Best Bar, earning numerous international awards for its iconic cocktails and warm, effortless hospitality. The historic dining room offers chef-driven seasonal dishes, a world-class beverage program, and the laid-back energy that has made it a Village staple for generations. Guests can grab a table inside the original café space, relax in the intimate lounge, or take a seat at the lively marble bar. Walk-ins are always welcome, and reservations for NYC Restaurant Week are available up to 28 days in advance.

name: Stella 34 Trattoria
summary: This modern Italian trattoria and bar on Macy's sixth floor boasts soaring ceilings and beautiful natural light, not to mention impressive views of the Empire State Building.
address: 151 West 34th Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: This modern Italian trattoria and bar on Macy’s sixth floor boasts soaring ceilings and beautiful natural light, not to mention impressive views of the Empire State Building. The menu features authentic, Neapolitan pizza, al forno entrées and house-made pastas, alongside an all-Italian wine list of more than 100 selections. The restaurant's showpieces include three wood-burning ovens and the 240-foot long Carrara marble and stainless steel sculptural bar sweeping through the spacious dining room, said to be the longest bar set for dining and drinks in NYC.

name: Altesi Ristorante
summary: The elegantly modern and sophisticated Altesi Ristorante, on the Upper East Side, offers a menu consisting of Tuscan-inspired dishes.
address: 26 East 64th Street, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: Conveniently located just off Madison Avenue on the Upper East Side, the elegantly modern and sophisticated Altesi Ristorante offers a menu consisting of Tuscan-inspired dishes. Altesi is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner and has an outdoor dining space in its enclosed garden. Altesi is a neighborhood gem that is a destination in the search for elegant and authentic Italian food.

name: Michael's
summary: Michael's has long functioned as a power-breakfast-and-lunch scene for the who's who of media.
address: 24 West 55th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Michael’s has long functioned as a power-breakfast-and-lunch scene for the who’s who of media. The contemporary California cuisine—omelets, Cobb salad, pan-roasted chicken—serves as a backdrop for the crowd, which on any given day might include Martha Stewart, Ron Perelmen and Les Moonves. Michael’s Garden Room is decorated with art by Frank Stella, Jasper Johns and David Hockney, and it can be booked for private parties.

name: Legasea
summary: Legasea combines a top-tier seafood menu with a fun atmosphere.
address: 485 Seventh Avenue, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: Located in the heart of Midtown blocks away from some of New York City’s most popular destinations including Madison Square Garden, Penn Station and Times Square, Legasea Bar & Grill is a fresh take on bar and grill classics with a fun-casual atmosphere for an entertaining dining experience.

name: Serra
summary: Eataly's seasonal rooftop restaurant will transport you the Italian Alps.
address: 200 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Step into the Italian countryside at Serra by Birreria, Eataly's "greenhouse" pop-up on the roof. The restaurant will transport you from the hot pavement of Manhattan to the rolling fields of Italy. Sit down at rustic tables in the shade, and share down-to-earth dishes made with simple but quality ingredients from our favorite farmers in Italy and the US and served family-style, just like in the countryside.

name: Fogo de Chão Brazilian Steakhouse
summary: Fogo de Chão is an authentic Brazilian steakhouse (churrascaria) that has been setting the standard in Brazil since 1979.
address: 40 West 53rd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Fogo de Chão is an authentic Brazilian steakhouse (churrascaria) that has been setting the standard in Brazil since 1979. The menu includes delectable cuts of grilled meats such as sizzling steaks, lamb, chicken and pork carved tableside by Brazilian trained gaucho chefs as well as a lighter seafood option. Also offered is a gourmet salad and sides bar consisting of salads, fresh-cut vegetables, cured meats and imported cheeses, as well as a variety of traditional Brazilian side dishes, delectable desserts and award-winning wine list.

name: Mito - Bayside
summary: Mito's esteemed head chef, who has devoted numerous years to the masterful art of cooking, brings with him a wealth of experience at esteemed establishments such as Jean Georges and Buddha Bar.
address: 26th Avenue, Astoria, New York 11102, United States
summary2: The definition of modern Japanese cuisine is innovation. It refers to a new and imaginative approach to cooking and presentation of food, it pushes the boundaries of traditional culinary techniques, and it incorporates unexpected ingredients and flavors to create unique and unforgettable dining experiences. Mito's esteemed head chef, who has devoted numerous years to the masterful art of cooking, brings with him a wealth of experience at esteemed establishments such as Jean Georges and Buddha Bar. With his addition to their team, the owners anticipate elevating Mito to unprecedented heights.

name: Nami Nori - Williamsburg
summary: Nami Nori is a cozy Williamsburg spot to try the innovative temaki hand rolls—a sort of Japanese version of tacos.
address: 236 North 12th Street, Brooklyn, New York 11211, United States
summary2: Think of temaki as the Japanese version of tacos. Nami Nori is a cozy Williamsburg spot to try the innovative hand rolls, stuffed with tuna poke and crispy shallots, yellowtail and scallion or lobster tempura and yuzu aioli (the menu also offers vegan options). There is also a good selection of beer, cider, sake, wine and matcha.

name: Cull & Pistol Oyster Bar
summary: The Cull & Pistol Oyster Bar is a Michelin-acclaimed seafood restaurant located in Chelsea Market.
address: 75 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: The Cull & Pistol Oyster Bar is a Michelin-acclaimed seafood restaurant located in Chelsea Market. Since opening in 2013, it has become a go-to dining destination, beloved by locals and tourists alike. Cull & Pistol is known for delivering exceptional service and a seasonal menu that takes full advantage of the remarkably fresh and varied offerings from of their sister seafood market, The Lobster Place.

name: Mable's Smokehouse and Banquet Hall
summary: Smoky brisket, pulled pork and St. Louis–style ribs taste authentic and won't set you back too much.
address: 44 Berry Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Enter Mable's Smokehouse and you're not in New York anymore. Kansas City, Lubbock or Little Rock come to mind—places that are more likely to harbor such a big, rustic saloon. This is the first restaurant from co-owner Jeff Lutonsky, an Oklahoma native, who named it for his grandmother, Mable. Her secret barbecue sauce recipe is almost as rich as caramel, and you may want to buy a bottle. And maybe a whole peanut butter pie, since one slice is never enough. Smoky brisket, pulled pork and St. Louis-style ribs taste authentic and won't set you back too much.

name: French Louie
summary: French Louie is a modern French-American bistro from the team behind Buttermilk Channel.
address: 320 Atlantic Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: French Louie is a modern French-American bistro from the team behind Buttermilk Channel, located at the crossroads of Cobble Hill, Brooklyn Heights, Downtown Brooklyn and Boerum Hill, conveniently close to the Barclays Center and BAM. The hearty but vegetarian-friendly menu includes a selection of three steaks frites as well as a raw bar along with a variety of iced and baked local oysters. The bar offers a list of signature and traditional cocktails along with an extensive selection of French and American wines, regional beers and ciders. French Louie is open for brunch, weekday lunch and dinner.

name: Veselka
summary: Find 24-hour comfort food and Ukrainian specialties at this East Village standby.
address: 144 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: You can hardly call yourself a New Yorker without having a favorite dish at the famous East Village Ukrainian eatery Veselka Restaurant. In business since 1954, it offers neighbors and visitors 24-hour comfort food in a diner-type atmosphere. The kids love the pierogis and potato pancakes; the adults love the borscht and sweet cheese blintzes. On the way out it’s hard to pass up the pastry counter with its pies, cupcakes, cookies and homemade muffins. The restaurant also has a seasonal outdoor café.

name: Indochine
summary: French-Vietnamese cuisine is served in this perennial hot spot.
address: 430 Lafayette Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: It opened its doors more than 30 years ago, and Indochine still holds onto the elements that made it famous, including a crowd of yuppies mixed with the fashion world and on-the-rise celebrities. Utilizing exotic-meets-tropical design elements such as Japanese box lights, palm trees painted onto the walls and a sleek tiled floor worked in the late ’80s for this French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant, so why change now? Some consider Indochine to be past its prime, but revelers still frequent this pioneer for the consistent spring rolls, the reliable sole steamed in a banana leaf and the glazed duck breast.

name: The Palm - Midtown
summary: The second in a chain of Palm restaurants, this one is located in the Theatre District.
address: 250 West 50th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: The second in a chain of Palm restaurants, this one is located in the Theatre District. This has steadily become a staple in the highly trafficked Times Square area. Be sure to keep an eye out for Broadway's finest actors catching a Prime Aged New York Strip steak and a bottle of Barberesco after the evening's final performance.

name: Society Cafe
summary: Hidden inside Walker Hotel is Society Cafe, a market-to-table American restaurant by chef Nicholas McCann.
address: 52 West 13th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: With more 20 years of experience in the kitchen, Nicholas McCann, now executive chef of Society Cafe, has always been passionate about food. Drawing inspiration from his family recipes, Nicholas quickly fell in love with the culinary world at a young age and began his career at The French Culinary Institute in NYC. Since then, he has worked with some of the City’s most acclaimed chefs and restaurants, including working alongside chef Luis Bollo of Salinas before moving on to become an executive chef at Tessa, The Milling Room, and Corkbuzz. At Society Cafe, chef Nicholas flexes his creativity by bringing a fresh perspective to the restaurant’s ‘market-to-table’ concept. With a rotating seasonal menu reflective of the City’s local farmers and markets, guests can expect to experience chef Nicholas’ unique culinary creations alongside its intimate and classic art deco inspired space.

name: Bond 45
summary: This enormous, bi-level, Italian-ish venue offers a huge variety of meals and dishes.
address: 221 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Restaurateur Shelly Fireman engineered a two-block move for Bond 45, keeping the name although it’s on 46th Street now, across from the Richard Rodgers Theatre (where Hamilton is in residence). The enormous, bi-level, Italian-ish venue offers breakfast all day, a lavish antipasti bar and, in the downstairs bar, postshow happy hour discounts nightly after 9pm. Thin-crust pizzas, pasta, big salads, grilled fish and burgers with cacio e pepe-dusted fries are available for lunch or dinner.

name: Catch NYC
summary: Catch NYC is a globally influenced seafood restaurant set in a landmark building in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District.
address: 21 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: A globally influenced seafood restaurant, set in a landmark building in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District, Catch NYC features modern renditions of classic dishes served in a streaming, shareable style of dining. Marrying simple yet elegant seafood, sushi, and steak with excellent service and a lively atmosphere, the 400-seat, tri-level restaurant, complete with al fresco dining on the roof, features signature dishes including the Catch Roll, Truffle Sashimi, A5 Wagyu on a hot rock, Mushroom Spaghetti, and Cantonese Lobster.

name: Amity Hall Uptown
summary: Amity Hall is a premier sports destination on Manhattan's Upper West Side, best known for its lively atmosphere, handcrafted cocktails, and delicious food.
address: 982 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, New York 10025, United States
summary2: Amity Hall is a premier sports destination on Manhattan's Upper West Side, best known for its lively atmosphere, handcrafted cocktails, and delicious food. Try the chipotle chicken and chorizo egg rolls, pickled japaleno grilled cheese or jerk BBQ fried chicken paired with a local brew on draft. Named after the once-known Amity Street in Greenwich Village, Amity Hall was established in 2009 with the opening of its flagship location on West 3rd Street. Open seven days a week, Amity Hall features lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch, and offers the perfect venue for hosting special events or watching a game.

name: Pink Taco
summary: Pink Taco isn’t just another taco joint. What they’re after is a detonation of flavors dancing on your tastebuds.
address: 7 Times Sq, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Pink Taco isn’t just another taco joint—it’s sacred ground. You won’t find them playing it safe. What they’re after is a detonation of flavors dancing on your tastebuds...a beautiful mess, made with the kind of reckless attitude they infuse into their house-made margaritas.

name: Estiatorio Milos Hudson Yards
summary: Pristine Mediterranean-style seafood shines in an industrial-chic setting at Milos, featuring a view of the Vessel and Hudson River.
address: 20 Hudson Yards, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Pristine Mediterranean-style seafood shines in an industrial-chic setting at Milos, featuring a view of the Vessel and the Hudson River. Amid stark concrete walls and a giant white curtain studded with garlic cloves, customers get to pick their meal from the display of glistening chilled fish. It’s then prepared in the kitchen and grilled to perfection with a dash of olive oil and lemon. Just remember that you’ll be charged by the pound, so don’t be too shocked by the bill for that gargantuan Greek snapper. Prix fixe lunch is available daily.

name: Pulperia Latin Mediterranean Kitchen
summary: Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes.
address: 338 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: As Restaurant Row has long been a culinary destination offering flavors from around the globe, Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen serves the flavors of Latin America with Mediterranean touches by executive chef Miguel Molina, who prides himself on his creativity for reimagining dishes. At Pulperia, he focuses on fresh, simple, clean, healthy ingredients. The menu offers small plates, paellas, and unique larger fare designed for sharing, plus an extensive cocktail list, all served with the warm hospitality and fun that the Latin culture brings to dining. Leading the team is seasoned restaurateur Orhan Cakir, known for his acclaimed Argentinian steakhouses Palermo Argentinian Steakhouse & Bistro, Palermo Argentinian Bistro Gramercy, and Pierre Loti Wine Bar. Karla Medina, director of operations, brings deep industry knowledge from her experience managing the original La Pulpería location. Now, the beloved concept is reborn as Pulpería Latin Mediterranean Kitchen, refreshed and reimagined for a new era.

name: Crave Fishbar - Midtown
summary: Crave Fishbar—NYC’s first 100% sustainable seafood restaurant—is home to the #Oystergram Happy Hour, one of NYC’s best oyster happy hour deals.
address: 945 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Crave Fishbar—NYC’s first 100% sustainable seafood restaurant—is home to the #Oystergram Happy Hour, one of NYC’s best oyster happy hour deals. This Midtown East location serves creative seafood in an upscale neighborhood setting, complete with warm hospitality since 2012. Global flavors and innovative preparations highlight their sustainable seafood, heritage meats, and organic produce. The raw bar features a daily selection of East Coast and West Coast oysters, sometimes up to 20 varieties each night. For business dinners, special occasions, and dining out just-because, Crave serves a sustainable and memorable meal.

name: Pomp & Circumstance
summary: Pomp & Circumstance is a cozy Mediterranean restaurant with sidewalk seating.
address: 577 Lorimer Street, Brooklyn, New York 11211, United States
summary2: Borrowing its name from everyone's favorite graduation march, Pomp & Circumstance is a cozy Mediterranean restaurant with sidewalk seating. Try some labneh or bottarga with your fresh-baked pita, and follow with some vegetarian-friendly plates or an interesting dish like the fettucine with smoked trout roe or the tripe alla romana. There's a compact list of wines and cocktails.

name: Osteria 57
summary: Osteria 57 offers a different kind of Italian menu, combining seafood choices and vegetarian dishes.
address: 453 Sixth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Osteria 57, which opened its doors in September 2017, offers New Yorkers a different kind of Italian menu, combining seafood choices and vegetarian dishes. Turtledove colors and soft lights will make each guest feel at home in this West Village favorite. Traditional Italian seafood dishes are executed to perfection and North Atlantic delicacies are paired with the freshest products. Thanks to its many vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options, Osteria 57 provides an experience tailored to each diner’s needs.

name: Alice
summary: Alice is a sophisticated, intimate Italian seafood and lobster bar set in the basement of a historic brownstone.
address: 126 West 13th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Alice is a sophisticated, intimate Italian seafood and lobster bar set in the basement of a historic brownstone. They do Italian spins on calamari, oysters, halibut and other seafood. Alice’s fish is sustainably sourced, most of the produce is local and organic, and their pantry is GMO-, canola- and soybean-free.

name: Lure Fishbar
summary: With decor that evokes a luxury yacht, Lure puts a contemporary spin on its classic fish-house menu.
address: 142 Mercer Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: With decor that evokes a luxury yacht, Lure puts a contemporary spin on its classic fish-house menu. Enjoy bacon-laced clam chowder and a fresh lobster roll, or try something more complex, like steamed red snapper with bok choy in red curry broth.

name: Giorgio's of Gramercy
summary: A classy, well-rated Italian eatery decorated in beige and burgundy in the neighborhood of Gramercy, Giorgio's offerings include salad, pasta, sandwiches and entrees such as filet mignon.
address: 27 East 21st Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: A classy Italian eatery decorated in beige and burgundy in the neighborhood of Gramercy, Giorgio’s serves salad, pasta, sandwiches and entrees such as filet mignon. Order online and have a catering order delivered. Look for the penne ragu and the Berkshire pork chop with pumpkin seed-sesame soy glaze—or perhaps the mustard-crusted rack of lamb with fingerling potatoes will catch your eye. Try the s’more bread pudding for dessert.

name: Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown
summary: This newly renovated subterranean dining space offers a family-style menu that emphasizes traditional Beijing cuisine with an elevated twist.
address: 355 West 16th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown continues the brand’s legacy of elegant Chinese dining, bringing chef Philippe Chow’s signature dishes to Chelsea near the Meatpacking District. The subterranean dining space offers a family-style menu that emphasizes traditional Beijing cuisine with an elevated twist, with cult favorites like Chicken Satays, Green Prawns and the legendary Peking Duck. Catering to the buzzy downtown crowd, Philippe by Philippe Chow Downtown features rotating DJs on weekend nights and is open til 2am, serving a special late night menu for those looking for a bite after dark.

name: Iris
summary: Inspired by the rich culinary traditions of the Mediterranean, chef John Fraser explores the cuisine of the Aegean at Iris.
address: 1740 Broadway, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Recognized as one of the world's leading vegetable chefs, John Fraser (The French Laundry in Napa Valley; Taillevent and Maison Blanche in Paris) has played a significant part in redefining the role of vegetables in American cuisine. Inspired by the rich culinary traditions of the Mediterranean, chef Fraser explores the cuisine of the Aegean at Iris. He draws upon his Greek heritage and deep admiration for Turkish cuisine to create a menu that suggests a sense of place, while leaving room for innovation and imagination in flavor, texture and presentation.

name: Mezze on the River
summary: This casual, family-friendly restaurant on the Manhattan waterfront features shareable dishes such as artichoke and spinach dip and a quartet of mac-n-cheese cones.
address: 375 South End Avenue, New York, New York 10280, United States
summary2: This casual, family-friendly restaurant on the Manhattan waterfront features shareable dishes such as artichoke and spinach dip and a  quartet of mac-n-cheese cones. Entrees include sesame-crusted tuna, penne Bolognese and the house burger.  Rounding out the menu are salads, desserts and signature cocktail. The indoor décor is classic American bistro, down to the copper-top bar. There’s outdoor seating on two terraces, with views of the Hudson River across to the Colgate Clock.

name: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar
summary: Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine.
address: 309 East 5th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Rynn Thai Restaurant & Bar was founded in the East Village by a group of women who have the same dreams and goals. "Rynn" (รินน์) means to pour—the owners pour their memories into their dishes and glasses—and the restaurant is a place where memories come to life through the art of culinary creations and mixology. Every dish and cocktail they serve is carefully crafted using ingredients and details inspired by the memories and childhood experiences of the owners. It's a place where nostalgia blends with creativity to create a unique and unforgettable dining experience. Whether you are a Thai food enthusiast or someone new to the cuisine, Rynn offers the vibrant tapestry of Thai cuisine. The restaurant has 30 seats in the dining area plus 8 bar seats and 6 more seats for outdoor dining.

name: Prohibition
summary: This bar/restaurant offers a wide variety of cocktails, casual American fare and live music every night after 9pm.
address: 503 Columbus Avenue, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: This bar/restaurant, located three blocks from the American Museum of Natural History, offers a wide variety of cocktails, casual American fare and live music every night after 9pm. From Gavin Degraw to Dan Ackroyd to former New York Yankees outfielder Bernie Williams, one never knows just who they might see perform when they come to hang at Prohibition. Menu items include a selection of appetizers—including mini cheeseburgers, macaroni and cheese, fried calamari and buffalo wings—as well as a large dinner menu consisting of comforting American fare.

name: Del Friscos Double Eagle Steakhouse New York
summary: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse New York is an energetic, sprawling, three-story restaurant in Midtown, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows that offer grand views of Sixth Avenue.
address: 1221 Sixth Avenue, New York, New York 10020, United States
summary2: Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse New York is an energetic, sprawling, three-story restaurant in Midtown, featuring floor-to-ceiling windows that offer grand views of Sixth Avenue. Their guests are treated to an unforgettable experience through the chef-driven cuisine, world-class wine program and unparalleled hospitality. Del Frisco's offers a variety of private and semi-private dining and reception spaces perfectly suited for special occasions or business gatherings. They provide their private diners with warm hospitality and custom menus featuring the finest steak and seafood. Dedicated private dining coordinators will help to plan and personalize your event so you can sit back and relax.

name: The Bar Room at The Modern
summary: The lively Bar Room at The Modern, a Michelin-starred contemporary American restaurant at MoMA, offers Chef Abram Bissell's vividly seasonal contemporary cooking à la carte.
address: 9 West 53rd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Founded by Danny Meyer’s Union Square Hospitality Group, The Modern is a Michelin-starred contemporary American restaurant at the Museum of Modern Art. The lively Bar Room offers chef Tom Allan's seasonal contemporary cooking à la carte, along with an award-winning wine program along with carefully curated cocktails, beer and spirits. Guests have the option of sitting in The Bar Room, the adjacent lounge, or at the vibrant 24-seat marble bar. Walk-ins are accepted in all three areas, and The Bar Room also welcomes reservations up to 28 days in advance.

name: Leuca
summary: Inspired by Southern Italy, Leuca is a neighborhood restaurant from Chef Andrew Carmellini's NoHo Hospitality Group serving house-made pastas, wood-fired pizzas and rustic dishes in a sunlit corner space in Williamsburg.
address: 111 North 12th Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Inspired by Southern Italy, Leuca is a neighborhood restaurant from Chef Andrew Carmellini's NoHo Hospitality Group serving house-made pastas, wood-fired pizzas and rustic dishes in a sunlit corner space in Williamsburg. At Leuca, chef Carmellini, executive chef Anthony Ricco and pastry chef Jason Casey source the finest seasonal ingredients to create elevated yet rustic dishes with a distinctly Italian flair. The wine list focuses on Italian regions south of Abruzzo with a heavy emphasis on Sicily, Campania and Calabria.

name: Le Gratin
summary: Le Gratin echoes the traditional bistros and bouchons of chef Daniel Boulud's hometown of Lyon, France, known for their welcoming ambiance and soulful cuisine.
address: 5 Beekman Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: Located in the Financial District, Le Gratin echoes the traditional bistros and bouchons of chef Daniel Boulud's hometown of Lyon, France, known for their welcoming ambiance and soulful cuisine. The rustic menu reflects a soulful approach to seasonality, bright flavors, and classic techniques highlighting special ingredients from local purveyors. Lyonnais classics such as “Quenelle de Brochet au Gratin” and “Steak Tartare à la Parisienne” share space with seasonal dishes and “Plat du Mois”—a rotating dish of the month showcasing regional cuisine, meant to share. The wine list boasts more than 100 offerings, with a special focus on Lyon.

name: The Dynamo Room
summary: Featuring steakhouse classics, a raw bar, and curated cocktails, The Dynamo Room channels the vibrant spirit of New York’s historic grills.
address: 2 Pennsylvania Plaza, New York, New York 10121, United States
summary2: The Dynamo Room is a steakhouse from the team behind Sunday in Brooklyn, Café Chelsea, and Rule of Thirds, located next door to Madison Square Garden above Penn Station. The menu is classic, old-school New York steakhouse, with plenty of raw oysters, prime cuts, burgers and martinis on offer. Dine beneath vaulted ceilings and satellite-inspired lighting, surrounded by art from renowned and emerging artists, including a sculptural installation by Vincent Leroy and works curated by Karma. With richly detailed design elements inspired by the original Pennsylvania Station and New York’s spirit of innovation, The Dynamo Room offers a one-of-a-kind backdrop for a meal, private dining and celebrations of all kinds.

name: Jue Lan Club
summary: Occupying the historic Limelight space, this elegant Flatiron restaurant serves Asian food with modern touches.
address: 49 West 20th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Occupying the historic Limelight space, this elegant Flatiron restaurant serves Asian food with modern touches. Jue Lan Club features a fantastic cocktail list, fresh sushi and sashimi, and signature Chinese and Japanese dishes served in a wonderful setting with plush booths, elaborate lighting and amazing artwork. They also have an incredible outdoor garden and multiple rooms for events that feature fireplaces, plasma TVs and private bars.

name: Travelers Poets & Friends
summary: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings.
address: 457 Sixth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Travelers Poets & Friends captures the essence of the Italian coastline with its authentic offerings. Proprietor Emanuele Nigro, known for Osteria57 and Alice, has created a multi-faceted venue with a bakery, espresso bar, and market. The eatery offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner menus curated by Italian chef Riccardo Orfino, emphasizing seasonal ingredients and pescatarian-friendly dishes. Highlights include tuna Bolognese lasagna, grilled fishes, and eclectic pizzas. The marketplace section provides fresh and dry pasta, exotic salts, spices, and specialty drinks. Nigro's dedication to sustainable and high-quality seafood is evident, and the venue's ambiance reflects his Italian culinary philosophy.

name: Comal
summary: Comal, located on Manhattan's Lower East Side, celebrates the vibrant spirit of the cuisine in Mexico City.
address: 116 Forsyth Street, New York, New York 10002, United States
summary2: Comal, located on Manhattan's Lower East Side, celebrates the vibrant spirit of the cuisine in Mexico City. The menu is built around peak-season produce from the Northeast US, thoughtfully grown and sourced from small farms, alongside sustainably caught seafood and heritage meats. Comal was founded by Gaz Herbert, who was born in Cuernavaca, Mexico. His time there and in Mexico City has given him a strong sense of connection to the city’s welcoming hospitality and culinary creativity. Comal is also a culmination of these experiences in Mexico, as well as his exposure cooking in London’s diverse dining scene. Every dish aims to create a deep sense of flavor, harnessing the fresh and sustainable ingredients that New York City has to offer, and utilizing their curated pantry of chiles, spices, and other ingredients from across Mexico.

name: Obao Midtown East
summary: Michael Bao Huynh, of Bia Garden and Baoguette fame, brings his formula—Pan-Asian food in a sleek setting—to the east side.
address: 222 East 53rd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Michael Bao Huynh, of Bia Garden and Baoguette fame, brings his formula—Pan-Asian food in a sleek setting—to the east side. Obao offers tasty noodles, both pan-fried and in soups, and barbecue in filling portions. At lunch it's packed with young business types, and at night it's a relaxed nightspot for locals.

name: Boucherie Union Square
summary: Boucherie Union Square is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse, celebrating Joie de Vivre, that prepares a menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, in addition to dry-aged steaks.
address: 225 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Boucherie Union Square is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse celebrating Joie de Vivre. The restaurant features an ample menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, such as the Soupe à l’Oignon and Steak Frites, in addition to delectable dry-aged meats. Alongside an extensive wine list featuring the exclusive Boucherie Wine Collection, guests can enjoy signature cocktails, absinthe drinks, non-alcoholic options, craft beers, and more. Surrounded by walls of majestic wooden-framed mirrors and original Belle Époque posters, seating at this Union Square location varies among pristine white marble and wood bistro tables, cozy burgundy leather booths, a 32ft. handmade pewter bar, and an option for a 40-guest private room, to make the 222-seat restaurant feel timeless.

name: The Otter
summary: Acclaimed chef Alex Stupak serves a menu focused on simply prepared seafood using the freshest ingredients from carefully selected purveyors.
address: 58 Thompson Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Located inside The Manner Hotel in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan, The Otter is a charming neighborhood restaurant. Acclaimed chef Alex Stupak serves a menu focused on simply prepared seafood using the freshest ingredients from carefully selected purveyors. The Otter is open daily for dinner, cocktail hour, and brunch on weekends. They offer indoor and outdoor seating, weather permitting, and a dog-friendly patio.

name: Manuela
summary: Manuela is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant and bar in SoHo where great contemporary art and food combine to create a convivial atmosphere and sense of abundance.
address: 130 Prince Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Located on the corner of Wooster and Prince Street in SoHo—New York’s historic cast iron district—Manuela is a welcoming neighborhood restaurant and bar where great contemporary art and food combine to create a convivial atmosphere and sense of abundance. The restaurant is named for Manuela Wirth, who co-founded Artfarm with her husband Iwan Wirth, and like its sister restaurant in the Downtown Arts District of Los Angeles, Manuela in SoHo takes its cues from its namesake’s legendary hospitality, culinary talents, and famous warmth as a hostess whose passion for freshly prepared cuisine, local culture, and community are complemented by the guiding conviction that art and life are indivisible. Manuela hews to the belief that great food and delicious, nourishing meals are not luxuries but essentials to be generously shared.

name: Del Frisco's Grille - Brookfield Place
summary: Del Frisco’s features a steakhouse-style menu, with classic starters like a wedge salad and choice cuts of broiled steaks.
address: 250 Vesey Street, New York, New York 10281, United States
summary2: Located in Lower Manhattan’s Brookfield Place, Del Frisco’s features a steakhouse-style menu, with classic starters like a wedge salad and choice cuts of broiled steaks—though you’ll also find variety with ahi tacos, wild mushroom flatbreads, truffled mac and cheese and a cauliflower steak. Meat and seafood meal kits are available, desserts are prepared in house and the wine list is unsurprisingly long.

name: Jing Li
summary: Jing Li is a fine-dining destination in Long Island City, Queens, that serves a mix of Szechuan, Shanghai and Cantonese cuisines.
address: 27-35 Jackson Avenue, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Jing Li is a fine-dining destination in Long Island City, Queens, just a short trip from Manhattan. Jing Li serves a mix of Szechuan, Shanghai and Cantonese cuisines that serves as inspiration for their concept of global flavors. Each dish is created with the freshest ingredients and skillful attention to detail by the executive chef.

name: Lido
summary: James Beard Award–winning author Serena Bass, Lido's executive chef, creates unique twists on Northern Italian classics on Harlem's "Restaurant Row."
address: 2168 Frederick Douglass Boulevard, New York, New York 10026, United States
summary2: James Beard Award–winning author Serena Bass, Lido's executive chef, creates unique twists on Northern Italian classics at this eatery on Harlem's "Restaurant Row." Just a few blocks from the Apollo and a short subway ride from Midtown, Lido is a relaxed, open space featuring street-facing French doors. The venue's friendly, professional service enhances the culinary experience.

name: So & So's
summary: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway.
address: 302 West 52nd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: This sumptuously-appointed, dimly-lit piano-bar-meets-supper-club evokes the feeling of stumbling into a local legend’s living room during a night out in NYC—but is also an ode to Broadway and the theatrical pedigree of Hell’s Kitchen. So & So’s space is anchored by an upright blue piano on a raised stage—an homage to practice rooms and rehearsal studios. Luxurious red banquettes, upholstered walls and custom lighting take cues from vintage City nightlife, and the entertainment features everyone from local acts to Broadway stars and A-list talent, with special guest pop-ups possible.

name: Kimika
summary: Kimika is an eclectic meeting point of Japanese and Italian comfort foods that merge in a delightful and satisfying way.
address: 40 Kenmare Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Kimika is an eclectic meeting point of Japanese and Italian comfort foods that merge in a delightful and satisfying way. Chef Christine Lau serves intriguing Japanese-Italian fare like porchetta with miso mustard, dry-aged ribeye with sesame ponzu and wasabi chutney, and a dish with both lobster and uni. Diners can choose from a vast array of refreshing house cocktails as well.

name: Metropolis
summary: Metropolis is a vibrant contemporary American restaurant from Marcus Samuelsson within the Perelman Performing Arts Center in Lower Manhattan.
address: 251 Fulton Street, New York, New York 10007, United States
