summary2: Metropolis by Marcus Samuelsson is a vibrant contemporary American restaurant from Marcus Samuelsson within the Perelman Performing Arts Center. It is the culinary anchor of this new cultural cornerstone of Lower Manhattan. The menu explores the rich culinary traditions of New York City through a modern lens with theatrical cocktails, a fun and worldly wine list, and gracious hospitality. Metropolis, designed by David Rockwell, features a dazzling and yet warmly inviting dining room and a bustling bar, a landscaped outdoor terrace, and a lobby lounge featuring free-to-the-public artistic programming.

name: Henry's End
summary: For more than 50 years in Brooklyn Heights, Henry’s End has offered classic staples and neighborhood favorites alongside a seasonally oriented program of specials.
address: 72 Henry Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Located in Brooklyn Heights, this neighborhood institution is known for their inviting atmosphere. For more than 50 years, Henry’s End has offered classic staples and neighborhood favorites alongside a seasonally oriented program of specials. The award-winning wine list and commitment to service make a great meal simple and approachable. They also serve beer, cocktails and spirits. Henry's End features a seasonal menu highlighted by their annual Wild Game Festival in the fall and winter.

name: Acadia
summary: Executive chef Ari Bokovza's menu is inspired by Levantine traditions, brought to life through innovative preparation.
address: 101 West 57th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Acadia strikes the perfect balance between upscale and casual, ensuring patrons feel comfortable while still indulging in a refined experience. It's a vibrant gathering place, open to all who seek a memorable night out paired with exceptional cuisine. Executive chef Ari Bokovza's menu is inspired by Levantine traditions, brought to life through innovative preparation. Each dish carries with it a rich history, reimagined with a contemporary twist. Indulge in creations like the delicate eggplant varpaccio, adorned with a veil of tuna bresaola, or savor the bold flavors of rotisserie harissa BBQ Sasso chicken and delicious shrimp shish barak.

name: Temple Court
summary: Tom Colicchio serves a menu of quintessential New York City dishes in Lower Manhattan.
address: 5 Beekman Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: Steps away from The Beekman's centerpiece atrium and the bustle of The Bar Room is Tom Colicchio's Temple Court. Surrounded by a series of stained-glass windows, and full of historic charm, Temple Court's dining room is a destination for the fine dining devout. Now under the stewardship of executive chef Travis Sowards, Temple Court is a tour de force of Tom Colicchio's most classic flavor profiles, reimagined and assembled on a showcase menu in Downtown Manhattan.

name: Il Nonno
summary: The folks at Il Nonno, an Italian restaurant in Astoria, Queens, are passionate about creating a memorable dining experience for every guest.
address: 25-17 Astoria Boulevard, Astoria, New York 11102, United States
summary2: The folks at Il Nonno, an Italian restaurant in Astoria, Queens, are passionate about creating a memorable dining experience for every guest. Recent specialties have included Limoncello Night (zesty sips and limoncello-infused dishes), homemade black squid ink linguine, and Pera Della Helena (white wine poached pear with mascarpone cheese in a saffron and lavender compote).

name: The Lodge Bar by Stout NYC at Bryant Park
summary: Stout NYC joins forces with Boston chef Jen Royle at The Lodge Bar at Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park.
address: 42 West 42nd Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Stout NYC joins forces with Boston chef Jen Royle at The Lodge Bar at Bank of America Winter Village at Bryant Park. In 2019, the opening night of Royle's restaurant, Table, was documented on The Food Network’s “Opening Night,” highlighting its unique concept, a 32-seat communal prix-fixe family-style eatery in Boston’s historic North End. Two years later, Table was awarded the coveted Best of Boston award for “Best North End Restaurant” by Boston Magazine and has made the magazine's Top 50 Restaurant list for four of the past five years. Chef-owner Jen Royle has since added two more venues: Table Caffé, featuring homemade gelato, and Table Mercato, the neighboring Italian market which is home of the viral sensation, the focaccia sandwich.

name: Four Twenty Five
summary: This new restaurant from chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten perfectly blends culinary excellence with architectural marvel and sustainability practices.
address: 425 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Renowned chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has expanded his New York footprint with the launch of Four Twenty Five. This new restaurant perfectly blends culinary excellence with architectural marvel and sustainability practices.

name: Charlie Palmer Steak IV
summary: Chef Palmer adds new twists to his acclaimed cuisine to create the Knickerbocker Hotel's signature "Honest American Cuisine" in an open-action kitchen.
address: 6 Times Sq, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: With dazzling Times Square views overlooking Broadway and 42nd Street from an enviable fourth-floor corner perch in Midtown Manhattan, Charlie Palmer Steak IV brings together two of the most iconic names in hospitality. Inspired by the rich history of The Knickerbocker, a 1906 landmarked New York City treasure that serves as Times Square's premier luxury lifestyle hotel, chef Palmer adds new twists to his acclaimed cuisine to create the hotel's signature "Honest American Cuisine" in an open-action kitchen.

name: Lele's Roman
summary: Inspired by the lively neighborhood of Trastevere, Lele’s Roman brings a fresh take on Roman cuisine to Brooklyn's Boerum Hill neighborhood.
address: 252 Schermerhorn Street, Brooklyn, New York 11217, United States
summary2: Inspired by the lively neighborhood of Trastevere, Lele’s Roman brings a fresh take on Roman cuisine to Brooklyn's Boerum Hill neighborhood. Led by chef Francesco Battisti, the menu stays true to tradition, from beloved breakfast maritozzi to an all-day selection of Roman classics like amatriciana, cacio e pepe, puntarelle, and carciofi, alongside a selection of shareable pinsas. The beverage program celebrates Italian classics, featuring a robust amaro selection and a thoughtfully curated list of Laziale and regional Italian wines by LDV’s Alessio de Sensi. Designed by Whitley Esteban and Ernesto Gloria of Studio Tre, the space blends the brutalist character of the building with a touch of '70s Italian funk, setting the stage for a love letter to Rome, the city of LDV’s namesake, la dolce vita.

name: Bottino
summary: Since 1997, Bottino has offered classic and contemporary Tuscan Italian cuisine and boutique wines—as well as house cocktails and a bar menu—steps from the vibrant West Chelsea gallery scene.
address: 246 10th Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Since 1997, Bottino has offered classic and contemporary Tuscan Italian cuisine and boutique wines—as well as house cocktails and a bar menu—steps from the vibrant West Chelsea gallery scene. From a century-old hardware store, architect Thomas Leeser fashioned a mid-century modern eatery with a beautiful garden. Lovely for a romantic dinner, an evening with family or friends, Bottino's private dining spaces make it an ideal venue for large events as well.

name: Palermo Argentinian Bistro - Gramercy
summary: Executive chef Carlos Barroz and his partners in Palermo Argentinian Bistro on Manhattan’s Restaurant Row have opened this second location in Gramercy.
address: 53 Irving Place, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Executive chef Carlos Barroz and his partners in Palermo Argentinian Bistro on Manhattan’s Restaurant Row have opened this second location in Gramercy. The steakhhouse draws it inspiration from Palermo, a destination in Buenos Aires known for its fashionable bars and restaurants. Chef Barroz introduced seafood from the parrilla to this new location—prepared with the same attention and simplicity that defines their traditional Argentinian cuisine—premium steaks, grilled seafood, seasonal vegetables, housemade pastas, and classic dishes prepared with time and care.

name: The Ivy Room
summary: The Ivy Room is a modern, swanky take on the NYC piano and cocktail lounge.
address: 420 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: The Ivy Room, located at the Royalton Park Avenue, is a modern, swanky take on the NYC piano and cocktail lounge—a modern music experience highlighted by their electric yellow grand piano. Every Tuesday to Saturday, take in live music by local entertainers performing in various genres. The cocktail menu is designed by Gilded Group's mixologist Daniel Bedoya (try the Dirty Vesper, made with celery-infused vodka and mushroom-infused gin), alongside small plates by chef Jonathan Rodriguez, whose new age flavors take inspiration from classic favorites such as salmon tartare and grilled hanger with romesco. Reservations are strongly recommended.

name: JoJo
summary: A lavishly gorgeous and perfectly refined town house is home to one of Jean-Georges Vongerichten's greatest dining accomplishments.
address: 160 East 64th Street, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: Jean-Georges Vongeritchen’s first restaurant, established in 1991 and named after the childhood nickname his mother would call him, is situated in a duplex townhouse on the Upper East Side. With a modern and fresh design, JoJo maintains an understated, warm and friendly atmosphere. It’s a simple and casual neighborhood restaurant serving a farm-to-table menu with mostly organic, local ingredients.

name: El Coco - Hell's Kitchen
summary: El Coco is a new taqueria in Hell's Kitchen with a twist, featuring authentic Mexican dishes, empanadas, traditional tacos, and a variety of signature sauces.
address: 828 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: El Coco is a new taqueria with a twist, featuring authentic Mexican dishes, empanadas, traditional tacos, and a variety of signature sauces. You can dine in or take out for a one-of-a-kind experience in Manhattan's Hell's Kitchen neighborhood. El Coco is open 7 days a week for lunch and dinner, and is also available for special events.

name: Gaia
summary: With a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients and artfully crafted dishes, Gaia offers a dining experience that blends elegance and flavor in a vibrant, modern atmosphere.
address: 42 West 35th Street, New York, New York 11358, United States
summary2: Gaia is an upscale Mediterranean-inspired restaurant located in Manhattan's Herald Square. With a focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients and artfully crafted dishes, Gaia offers a dining experience that blends elegance and flavor in a vibrant, modern atmosphere. Perfect for intimate dinners, celebrations, and private events, the menu showcases Mediterranean classics reimagined with a contemporary twist.

name: Kashkaval Garden
summary: Kashkaval Garden offers a casual, relaxed environment in which to enjoy wines, cocktails and Mediterranean food in Hell's Kitchen.
address: 852 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Kashkaval Garden offers a casual, relaxed, and rustic environment in which to enjoy wines, cocktails and Mediterranean-inspired food in Hell's Kitchen. Appetizers include homemade tapas with hot pita; grilled halloumi cheese sticks served with tomato-harissa dipping sauce; peppadews, spicy-sweet peppers stuffed with feta and mint or goat cheese and basil; and kale salad with figs and Pecorino. Move on to fondues made with Bulgarian Kashkaval cheese, classic gruyère, and truffle. Enjoy skewers of marinated chicken, lamb kofte, salmon in grape leaves, grilled vegetables, “Impossible” meatballs or grilled octopus. Finish things off with baklava or a chocolate torte.

name: La Sirene
summary: The menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season.
address: 558 Broome Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Chef/owner Didier Pawlicki lived in the hotel of his parents in the Pyrenees Mountains in France from the age of 6 to 16, when he left to attend the French Culinary School in Toulouse. His menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season. The restaurant's focus is on French Southern homemade styles and quality ingredients (Cuisine Bourgeoise) paired with a respectable wine list and friendly, professional service.

name: Empellón
summary: Alex Stupak’s Midtown flagship is a warm and inviting venue with an extensive agave program and inventive menu.
address: 510 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Empellón Midtown, Alex Stupak’s flagship restaurant and third New York City location, is a warm and inviting venue with an extensive agave program, inventive menu and custom artwork and installations. The restaurant was awarded three stars by The New York Times, and nominated as a James Beard finalist for best new restaurant.

name: Naks
summary: Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez.
address: 201 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: In Tagalog, the word "Naks" carries the beautiful essence of surprise and admiration, serving as the team's inspiration to craft gastronomic delights that aim to evoke these heartfelt emotions. These meals are meticulously prepared to spark joy and wonder with every flavorful bite. Naks by Unapologetic Foods offers a gastronomic tour of the Philippines framed by the personal memories of the restaurant’s chef, Eric Valdez. Chef Eric is crisscrossing Philippines and taking inspirations from locals homes and smaller towns to present a part of the cuisine that is still hidden from many around the world. There are two ways to experience Naks—a la carte or the communal Kamayan Feast—and each offers its own unique perspective.

name: Little Maven
summary: With an exciting and approachable menu featuring classics with a twist, Little Maven is a vibrant, fun and delicious choice.
address: 30 West 18th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Little Maven is a modern American neighborhood restaurant from the VCR Group. With an exciting and approachable menu featuring classics with a twist, Little Maven is a vibrant, fun and delicious choice. The restaurant also features a robust cocktail program and and extensive wine list.

name: Smith & Wollensky
summary: Find everything you’d expect from a classic NYC steakhouse at this Midtown East location: nice linen tablecloths, attentive service and abundant amounts of dry-aged steak.
address: 797 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: The good ol’ boys from Dallas who are in New York on business love this upscale steak joint with portions big enough to fill up even a Texas-size appetite. S&W has everything you’d expect from a large-scale steak and seafood restaurant: nice linen table cloths, enormous flower arrangements and abundant amounts of lobster, shrimp, crab and large slabs of steak.

name: Gaonnuri
summary: Gaonnuri's 39th floor penthouse in Koreatown affords wraparound views of Midtown.
address: West 32nd Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Gaonnuri boasts one of the most spectacular locations of any Korean restaurant in the City, occupying a 39th floor penthouse in Koreatown that affords wraparound views of Midtown. With a capacity of 300, and two private spaces that fit 40 each, it's a great place for business and social events. There is Seoul sophistication in the menu, which includes beef tartare marinated in sesame oil and soy sauce, seafood-and-scallion pancake, braised short ribs and spicy codfish stew. The bar/lounge, which offers views of the Empire State Building, emphasizes the vodka-like soju, but there's also an extensive wine list designed to match the Korean food.

name: Sabai Thai
summary: This elegant Thai restaurant in NoMad offers popular dishes such as pad Thai and tom yum goong, as well as chef's specialties that show the complexity of the country's cuisine.
address: 432 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Sabai, an elegant Thai restaurant located on Park Avenue South in the NoMad neighborhood of Manhattan, offers popular Thai dishes such as pad Thai and tom yum goong (hot and sour soup with shrimp), as well as chef's specialties that show the complexity of the country's cuisine.

name: Cut
summary: Wolfgang Puck’s first NYC steakhouse in the Financial District.
address: 99 Church Street, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: At Cut, acclaimed chef Wolfgang Puck introduces downtown Manhattan to his iconic California cuisine and modern take on the classic steakhouse. The menu boasts top-notch cuts of meat cooked to perfection; the signature Cut burger; sashimi and seafood (for the non-meat eater in your group); and small plates and sides such as mac and cheese, broccolini, bone marrow, suckling pig and pork belly. Cut’s striking decor includes red curtains accented by lightning-bolt-like red neon lights in the bar area; and in the dining room, guests will find a large artwork installation from Alex Israel featuring quotations with fireworks bursting through.

name: Bar Primi - Bowery
summary: A cozy Bowery space with two bars for dining and drinking, Bar Primi is a casual corner pasta shop devoted to primi piatti (the pasta course), a staple in chef and co-owner Andrew Carmellini's repertoire.
address: 325 Bowery, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: A cozy Bowery space with deep red leather booths and oak farm tables for communal dining and drinking, Bar Primi is devoted to primi piatti (the pasta course), a staple in chef and co-owner Andrew Carmellini's repertoire. Family recipes are traded between him and his team, who run daily meat or seafood entrée specials, seasonal antipasti salad and vegetable dishes, and housemade mozzarella. The pastas are housemade using non-GMO flours and organic eggs. There's also an affordable selection of Italian country wines along with the original frosé, craft beer on tap, aperitivi and signature cocktails.

name: Tarallucci e Vino - Union Square
summary: This neighborhood Italian restaurant features handcrafted pastries every morning, grilled panini on homemade focaccia and salads at lunch, and fresh pastas and locally and seasonally inspired Italian plates at night.
address: 15 East 18th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: This neighborhood Italian restaurant features handcrafted pastries every morning, grilled panini on homemade focaccia and salads at lunch, and fresh pastas and locally and seasonally inspired Italian plates at night. The culinary philosophy at the restaurant adheres to the Italian ideal of high quality ingredients, prepared with a delicate touch for a refined result. The exceptional wines they feature reflect their commitment to small-batch, family-run vineyards in Italy, many of which cannot be found anywhere else in the US.

name: Bocca Di Bacco—Chelsea
summary: Boasting an Italian-centric wine list of over 300 distinct selections to match with the menu overseen by executive chef Kristin Sollenne, the restaurant brings a contemporary, farm-to-table approach to Italian dining.
address: 169 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: With a name meaning "mouth of the wine god," it's no surprise that Bocca Di Bacco in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood embodies an atmosphere in which diners can enjoy both creative takes on Italian cuisine and outstanding wine. Boasting an Italian-centric wine list of over 300 distinct selections to match with the menu overseen by executive chef Kristin Sollenne, the restaurant brings a contemporary, farm-to-table approach to Italian dining.

name: Verde on Smith
summary: Verde on Smith is Cobble Hill, Brooklyn's neighborhood eatery, featuring regional Italian cuisine complemented by friendly service and warm ambiance.
address: 216 Smith Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Since 2009, Verde on Smith has been Cobble Hill, Brooklyn's neighborhood eatery, featuring regional Italian cuisine complemented by friendly service and warm ambiance. The menu is characterized by fresh, simple, but flavorful ingredients—the essence of Italian cuisine—specializing in fresh and delicious Italian seafood, pasta, appetizers, and tasty desserts. Paired with local brews, signature cocktails, and a wide selection of wine, there is something for everyone to enjoy. Verde on Smith's brunch and lunch menu offers a wide selection of burgers, savory and sweet brunch dishes such as French toast, omelets, pancakes, sandwiches, burgers, crepes, avocado toasts, fresh salads and more. At dinner, the menu highlights pasta, salads steaks, appetizers, chicken dishes and fresh seafood and fish.

name: Jack & Charlie’s No. 118
summary: At Jack & Charlie’s No. 118, nostalgia meets modern flair in a New American menu inspired by mid-century supper clubs.
address: 118 Greenwich Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: At Jack & Charlie’s No. 118, nostalgia meets modern flair in a New American menu inspired by mid-century supper clubs. Executive chef Ed Cotton—Top Chef finalist and seasoned alum of culinary icons—delivers indulgent dishes like handmade pastas, oak-fired steaks, and bone-in duck meatloaf. A dedicated martini menu, and a stylish setting with green leather booths and a glowing fireplace, make this West Village gem perfect for dinner or weekend brunch.

name: Barano
summary: Fire-roasted, grandma-inspired Italian food in Williamsburg.
address: 26 Broadway, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Barano is a charming Italian restaurant helmed by Albert Di Meglio, who named it for his grandmother’s birthplace on the tiny island of Ischia near Naples. She instilled in him a passion for the art of cooking, a heritage that he expresses in his hickory-smoked mozzarella, handmade pastas, pizza and wood-fired main courses. Di Meglio, formerly of Little Italy’s Rubirosa, is supported by a staff skilled in helping navigate the mostly Italian wine list and seasonal cocktail menu. You can book ahead at this Williamsburg destination, or arrive spontaneously and dine at the bar.

name: Oceana
summary: A beloved dining destination since 1992, Oceana is renowned for exceptional hospitality, an award-winning wine list, and world-class cuisine.
address: 120 West 49th Street, New York, New York 10020, United States
summary2: Oceana, the acclaimed American Seafood restaurant and flagship of the Livanos Restaurant Group, is located on 49th Street close to Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall, and Broadway’s famed theaters. A beloved New York City dining destination since 1992, Oceana is renowned for exceptional hospitality, an award-winning wine list, and world-class cuisine from executive chef Craig Dima.

name: The Parliament
summary: At The Parliament, located in the landmark Benjamin Royal Sonesta New York hotel, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu.
address: 557 Lexington Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: The Parliament serves breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, seven days a week. The restaurant is conveniently located in Manhattan's Midtown East, within walking distance to Rockefeller Center, Broadway, the United Nations and Grand Central Terminal. At The Parliament, chef Rakmin Lee brings to life his vision of a contemporary American Bistro dining menu. The menu offers signature American cuisine, concentrating on seasonal ingredients prepared with classic techniques. The Parliament is located at The Benjamin Royal Sonesta, a restored 1927 Emery Roth hotel, a New York City Landmark and a fitting complement to the restaurant’s refined style, café culture, and eclectic interior design.

name: Perry Street
summary: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's son Cedric leads the kitchen, which blends French, American and Asian influences
address: 176 Perry Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Yet another exploration by Jean-Georges Vongerichten, Perry Street has a minimalist space—fitting for its location in the Richard Meier Towers—and a simplified approach to elegant cooking. Vongerichten's son Cedric leads the kitchen, which blends French, American and Asian influences, as in the artichoke tagine and beef tenderloin with yuzu.

name: Mastro's Steakhouse NYC
summary: Mastro's collection of sophisticated steakhouses and Ocean Clubs has brought its masterful combination of world-class service, highly acclaimed cuisine and refinement to New York City.
address: 1285 Sixth Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Mastro’s collection of sophisticated steakhouses and Ocean Clubs has brought its masterful combination of world-class service, highly acclaimed cuisine and refinement to New York City. The menu features 16 different steaks and chops—ranging from an eight-ounce petite filet to a 48-ounce double cut porterhouse—and an array of fresh seafood selections. Enjoy live entertainment at the bar seven nights a week while sipping on hand-crafted cocktails and eclectic wines.

name: French Roast
summary: Upper West Siders have flocked to this popular French cafe for years for a taste of their bistro favorites, like croque monsieur, steak frites, French onion soup, duck confit and burgers, as well as a full brunch menu.
address: 2340 Broadway, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: This Upper West Side restaurant at West 85th Street and Broadway recreates the lively atmosphere of a Parisian bistro. French Roast pays homage to the City of Light with standards like steak frites, salad frisée aux lardons and croque monsieur. Whether you dine alone with a newspaper or with a group of friends, it’s always welcoming.

name: Carlotto
summary: Under the leadership of executive chef Andy Kitko and his culinary team, Carlotto’s menu honors Italy’s most celebrated regions.
address: 100 East 19th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Carlotto is an approachable Italian dining experience nestled between Gramercy Park and Union Square, adjacent to its sister restaurant, Oceans. Under the leadership of executive chef Andy Kitko and his culinary team, Carlotto’s menu honors Italy’s most celebrated regions, featuring pastas made daily. Carlotto is set in a modern intimate space designed by the award-winning Rockwell Group, and is anchored by a stunning bar featuring a thoughtfully curated cocktail list and Italian focused wine program.

name: Patsy's Italian Restaurant
summary: Serving the Theatre District with their classic Neapolitan menu since 1944, this celebrity hangout has played host to stars like Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Liza Minnelli and, most famously, Frank Sinatra.
address: 236 West 56th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Serving the Theatre District since 1944 (in their current location since 1954), this celebrity hangout has played host to stars like Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Liza Minnelli and, most famously, Frank Sinatra. The classic Neapolitan menu features signature dishes such as lobster fra diavolo and veal rollatine marsala, and famed chef Sal Scognamillo, who has been a frequent guest chef on TV (such as the Today show and the Martha Stewart Show), can be spotted on the premises. Reservations are recommended, and the dress code is smart-casual, so shorts are not allowed.

name: Sushi Ann
summary: Businesspeople flock to this no-frills sushi joint for both lunch and post-work dinners.
address: 38 East 51st Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: The chefs at Sushi Ann specialize in creating authentic Japanese dishes. The restaurant offers a seasonal, artisanal course that highlights the freshest ingredients at their disposal. Sushi Ann is ready to serve up a Japanese adventure and a great dining experience.

name: Marlow Bistro
summary: Marlow Bistro combines its Mediterranean roots with a European sensibility, and strives to create a warm and welcoming space.
address: 1018 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, New York 10025, United States
summary2: Marlow Bistro combines its Mediterranean roots with a European sensibility, and strives to create a warm and welcoming space with a casual approach and dedicated passion to its cuisine. Their team strives to support only local farms and businesses, in keeping with their belief in the power of community and advancing job opportunities through that support. Locally-sourced ingredients also shrink the carbon footprint, since your food does not have to travel thousands of miles to your plate. Marlow Bistro partners with many non-profit organizations to provide nutritious meals to New Yorkers in need.

name: Uva Next Door
summary: Seasonal Italian classics and fantastic Amalfi style pizza paired with a cocktail-forward beverage program make Uva Next Door the playful little sister to the original Uva.
address: 1484 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10075, United States
summary2: Seasonal Italian classics and fantastic Amalfi style pizza paired with a cocktail-forward beverage program make Uva Next Door the playful little sister to the original Uva. Uva Next Door is very vegetarian- and vegan-friendly, and makes gluten-free pasta in house every day. The vibe is eclectic nostalgia meets the new roaring '20s—the energy is high and the cocktails swing.

name: The Parlour Room
summary: The Parlour Room Bar and Grill is a classic American restaurant nestled near Herald Square that also features a collection of 450 of the world’s finest whiskeys.
address: 70 West 36th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: The Parlour Room Bar and Grill is a classic American restaurant nestled near Herald Square in Midtown Manhattan. The new menu, created by executive chef Stephen Woods, features craveable, delicious dishes that are classic but with fun, contemporary twists. Another point of pride is their collection of 450 of the world’s finest whiskeys, a treasure trove for whiskey enthusiasts, with selections from Ireland, Scotland, Japan, the United States, Canada and beyond.

name: Kru
summary: The concept at Kru is the modern interpretation of 100-year-old Thai recipes.
address: 190 North 14th Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: The concept at Kru is the modern interpretation of 100-year-old Thai recipes. Chef Ohm Suansilphong recreates and reimagines historic dishes from ancient recipes that are marked by their sophistication and surprising openness to worldly ingredients. These dishes are rarely served in the US, and are largely unknown, even to contemporary Thais. A thoughtful, curated selection of global wines accompanies his flavorful fare.

name: El Coco - Chelsea
summary: El Coco is a new taqueria in Chelsea with a twist, featuring authentic Mexican dishes, empanadas, traditional tacos, and a variety of signature sauces.
address: 202 8th Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: El Coco is a new taqueria with a twist, featuring authentic Mexican dishes, empanadas, traditional tacos, and a variety of signature sauces. You can dine in or take out for a one-of-a-kind experience in Manhattan's Chelsea neighborhood. El Coco is open 7 days a week for lunch and dinner, and is also available for special events.

name: Bad Roman
summary: Bad Roman is a playful, modern Italian restaurant from Quality Branded with stunning views of Central Park.
address: 10 Columbus Circle, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Bad Roman is a playful, modern Italian restaurant from Quality Branded with stunning views of Central Park. Bad Roman features an exciting menu of bright salads, unexpected pastas, a signature filletto, and more, all in a maximalist room filled with colorful fabrics and lush greenery. The beverage menu includes signature cocktails, Italian and American wines by the glass, plus an expansive bottle list. Bad Roman is located within The Shops at Columbus Circle, and is open for lunch and dinner daily.

name: Maggie's Place
summary: Family-owned since 1974, Maggie's Place serves up shepherd's pie, chicken pot pie, fish & chips, burgers and pub fare alongside a selection of wine and beer.
address: 21 East 47th Street, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Maggie's Place, one of the oldest family-owned restaurants in Midtown, was opened in October 1974 by Teddy and Maggie Whelan, who both immigrated from Dublin in 1958. Operated by the Whelans' son since 1992, Maggie's Place serves up shepherd's pie, chicken pot pie, fish and chips, burgers and pub fare alongside a selection of wine and beer.

name: Nick's Lobster House
summary: This historic South Brooklyn seafood restaurant features multiple dining rooms, including an outdoor deck, that all face the Mill Basin waterfront.
address: Flatbush Avenue Extension, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Established in 1955 by fisherman “Big Nick,” Nick’s Lobster House began with a single lobster shack along Flatbush Avenue where he would sell lobsters right off his boat to passersby. In the mid-seventies his children decided it would be a good idea to add a full-fledged fish market. Their historic seafood restaurant, set across from Marine Park Golf Course in South Brooklyn, features multiple dining rooms, including an outdoor deck, that all face the Mill Basin waterfront, and Nick's is still owned by the same family that decided to sell lobsters on Flatbush Avenue over 60 years ago.

name: ABC Kitchen
summary: ABC Kitchen by Michelin starred Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has a passionate commitment to offering the freshest organic and local ingredients possible.
address: 35 East 18th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: ABC Kitchen by Michelin starred Chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten has a passionate commitment to offering the freshest organic and local ingredients possible. Located within ABC Carpet & Home and sharing space with its sister restaurant, ABC Cocina (which features seasonal global Latin cuisine by Jean-Georges), this restaurant is a destination for visitors and locals alike.

name: Il Mulino Prime | Soho
summary: This culinary haven in SoHo embraces the unique character of the surrounding neighborhood.
address: 331 West Broadway, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Explore Il Mulino Prime | Soho, a culinary haven that embraces the unique character of the surrounding neighborhood. Indulge in the inviting atmosphere while savoring dishes crafted from the freshest ingredients. Join them for an authentic experience of Manhattan's trendy SoHo neighborhood.

name: Tarallucci e Vino - NoMad
summary: From their handcrafted pastries every morning, to their fresh pastas and locally and seasonally inspired Italian plates at night, Tarallucci e Vino invites you to start or end your day and unwind with them.
address: 44 East 28th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: The Italian saying, "All ends well with tarallucci e vino,” comes from a tradition of resolving any matter over a glass of wine and tarallucci, the classic southern Italian cookie. Since 2001, Tarallucci e Vino has applied this philosophy to every aspect of their dining experience. From their handcrafted pastries in the morning to their fresh pastas and locally and seasonally inspired Italian plates at night, they invite you to start or end your day and unwind with them. This NoMad location also has four incredible loft spaces for private events, and offers full-service catering on and off site.

name: Barbounia
summary: With ivy growing up the dimly lit columns, funky lighting and throw pillows strewn along several of the seating areas, Barbounia is anything but stuffy.
address: 250 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: With ivy growing up the dimly lit columns, funky lighting and throw pillows strewn along several of the seating areas, Barbounia is anything but stuffy. This Eastern Mediterranean’s strength, though, is its traditional Greek offerings, so make sure to order the grilled meats and fish—the lamb chops are some of the best in town. Another thing to keep in mind: the portions are all generous, so bring along some hungry friends to share.

name: Catria Cucina and Bar
summary: This all-day modern Italian spot draws inspiration from Italy's Marche region, offering a menu that highlights premium ingredients and house-made pastas.
address: 461 West 34th Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: In Hudson Yards’ Courtyard New York Manhattan/Midtown West is this all-day modern Italian spot. The restaurant and bar draws inspiration from Italy's Marche region, offering a menu that highlights premium ingredients and house-made pastas. The flavors of the Adriatic Coast come to life through robust dishes featuring meats, seafood, and savory, flavorful sauces. The drink selection captures the spirit of the region, with a focus on refreshing, earthy wines and cocktails crafted with traditional Italian spirits. Go for oatmeal at breakfast, Tuscan sandwiches at lunch and pastas, salads and burgers come evening time.

name: Rosemary's West Village
summary: Rosemary's evokes an enclosed Italian courtyard, full of greenery, reclaimed-wood tables, exposed-brick walls and terra-cotta flooring.
address: 18 Greenwich Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Since swinging open its doors in 2012, Rosemary's has become a beloved staple of the West Village. It's a neighborhood treasure known for its seasonal ingredient-driven menu, homemade pastas, and urban rooftop garden views. Named for founder Carlos Suarez's mother, Rosemary's celebrates the warmth and flavors of her Italian home in Lucca.

name: Pasta Louise
summary: Park Slope's Pasta Louise is a neighborhood gathering spot to eat pasta, grab a glass of wine, hang out with friends, have some hot chocolate and, on Wednesday evenings, enjoy a movie.
address: 8th Ave, Brooklyn, New York 11232, United States
summary2: Park Slope's Pasta Louise is a neighborhood gathering spot to eat pasta, grab a glass of wine, hang out with friends, have some hot chocolate and, on Wednesday evenings, enjoy a movie. You can pick up a coffee on the way to work or a pasta kit on your way home. Pasta, sauces and focaccia are homemade, and dishes use locally sourced ingredients whenever possible.

name: Ilili Restaurant
summary: Ilili is New York's premier contemporary Mediterranean restaurant, offering inspired Lebanese cuisine.
address: 236 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Since 2007, ilili has shared the cuisine and culture of Lebanon in the Flatiron District, introducing the Lebanese table to curious diners while comforting native Lebanese guests with a celebration of their homeland. Owner and executive chef Philippe Massoud expertly crafts a sophisticated blend of modern and traditional Lebanese cuisine drawing influences from the span of the ancient Silk Road trade routes. Their warm and generous hospitality drives their mission to make every guest and team member feel genuinely welcomed and fundamentally honored.

name: Craft
summary: Deceptively simple dishes shine at Tom Colicchio's beloved temple of green-market cuisine.
address: 43 East 19th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Superlative ingredients stand out in deceptively simple dishes at Tom Colicchio’s beloved temple of green-market cuisine. In a space done up in soothing blues and lit by filament bulbs, folks share family-style meals like pan-roasted day-boat scallops and braised beef short ribs—all sourced from around the country from high-quality purveyors. A timeless icon, Craft has altered the landscape of fine dining in America with its unique marriage of the finest ingredients and warm hospitality.

name: Eléa
summary: The Upper West Side welcomes a modern split-level Greek restaurant.
address: 217 West 85th Street, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: This modern split-level Greek restaurant has a sunny and welcoming atmosphere, with a big bar and plentiful tables. Eléa shares design and menu similarities with Kyma, its downtown sibling. Eggplant-zucchini chips with tzatziki dip and fried piquant kefalograviera cheese are an absolute must. From the raw bar, get yellow fin tuna tartare. Grilled lamb chops and creamy seafood orzotto laced with Metaxa brandy shine among the delicious main courses.

name: Victor's Cafe
summary: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food for decades.
address: 236 West 52nd Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Victor’s, in the Theatre District, has been a redoubt for high-end Cuban food for 50 years. In an airy space, the tropical theme is carried out with bright hand-painted murals, cane-backed chairs and old-time paddle fans gently waving in the rafters. The menu is more ambitious than a rice-and-beans joint, with both a classica menu of favorites like ropa vieja, skirt steak sautéed in onions, tomatoes, onions and peppers, then shredded by hand; and a nueva menu with ambitious fare like snapper, marinated in Seville oranges, and salmon, with a sugarcane glaze.

name: One Dine
summary: Set on the 101st floor with breathtaking views, One Dine features a specially curated menu ideally complimented by small production wines, a fine selection of local draft beers and handcrafted cocktails.
address: 117 West Street, New York, New York 10007, United States
summary2: At One Dine, the culinary experience is as elevated as the view. High above Manhattan inside One World Observatory, this premier restaurant offers a seasonal menu crafted with fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Guests can enjoy contemporary American cuisine with global influences, all curated by the expert culinary team. As the signature One World Observatory restaurant, it’s a destination for both food lovers and sightseers alike. Reservations are available on OpenTable.

name: Parklife
summary: Littlefield’s little sister bar claims an old warehouse space in Gowanus.
address: 11217 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Parklife is a year-round favorite with its landscaped 4000-square-foot front yard, outdoor heated solariums and indoor trellis and open kitchen/bar. Settle in and sample some of Parklife’s popular items including their house mezcarita and margarita, joojeh kabob taco, lamb beriyani tlayuda, loaded queso, chicken fried steak tlacoyo and Sunday BBQ tacos.

name: Hunt & Fish Club NYC
summary: Hunt & Fish Club NYC debuted in Midtown Manhattan in 2014 with a classic yet contemporary menu of exceptionally prepared steaks and game plus a unique selection of canapés and seafood offerings.
address: 125 West 44th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Hunt & Fish Club NYC debuted in Midtown Manhattan in 2014 with a classic yet contemporary menu of exceptionally prepared steaks and game plus a unique selection of canapés, seafood offerings, as well as an extensive wine list and specialty cocktails. Hunt & Fish Club NYC is pre-theater and post-theater friendly. The restaurant offers three spaces for private events up to 250 people.

name: Felice Montague
summary: Felice Montague serves classic Italian dishes inspired by the traditional cuisine of the Tuscan countryside.
address: 84 Montague Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Felice Montague serves classic Italian dishes inspired by the traditional cuisine of the Tuscan countryside. The menu emphasizes seasonal, locally sourced produce to ensure the highest quality ingredients, and an extensive Italian-drive wine program and a thoughtfully designed cocktail menu. Situated inside a 1930s art deco-style building in Brooklyn Heights, the restaurant was designed to both preserve its history and bring in touches of Italian culture. The restaurant offers open space with ample seating, making it ideal for families and large groups.

name: Zoì Mediterranean NoMad
summary: Located within The Life Hotel, a landmark of elegance and history, Zoì offers a refined yet welcoming dining experience where tradition meets innovation.
address: 19 West 31st Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Located within The Life Hotel, a landmark of elegance and history, Zoì offers a refined yet welcoming dining experience where tradition meets innovation. Their carefully curated menu brings together fresh, high-quality ingredients, masterfully crafted to create dishes that tell a story. Each plate reflects a passion for gastronomy, blending Mediterranean influences with modern culinary artistry.

name: Felice 83
summary: Felice reflects the soul of Italy, inspired by the sophisticated streets of Florence and the rustic warmth of the Tuscan countryside.
address: 1593 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10028, United States
summary2: Felice reflects the soul of Italy, inspired by the sophisticated streets of Florence and the rustic warmth of the Tuscan countryside. Felice 83 ristorante and wine bar offers a rustic and authentic Tuscan menu designed by executive chef Simone Parisotto. Owner Jacopo Giustiniani is the restaurateur and wine-buyer for all the Felice locations in addition to the Sant Ambroeus and Casa Lever restaurants.

name: Delmonico's
summary: The classic NYC steakhouse, in business since 1837, is where eggs Benedict and baked Alaska were said to be invented.
address: 56 Beaver Street, New York, New York 10004, United States
summary2: In business since 1837, Delmonico's revolutionized the way we eat out: these guys literally invented eggs Benedict, lobster Newberg and baked Alaska, among other now-standards, and changed the face of fine dining in early America. The financial district location looks exactly like you’d expect from an old-school steak house—deep hues, dark woods and understated opulence in which to enjoy the huge Delmonico rib-eye and the Parmesan creamed spinach.

name: Anton’s
summary: Try this romantic European-influenced bistro in the West Village.
address: 570 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Shake off the day at Anton’s, a cozy European-influenced bistro radiating with good cheer. Chef-partner Nick Anderer (ex-Marta, Maialino) tinkers with French and Italian classics, such as a silky omelette shrouded by a green salad and hand-cut angel hair pasta bathed in lemony-buttery francese sauce that crunches with bread crumbs. His West Village haven is also celebrated for its juicy roasted chicken. Grab a barstool if you just want a snack; try the “Hudson rarebit,” toast made with tangy melted cheese and béchamel.

name: Treadwell Park - Upper East Side
summary: Treadwell Park’s craft beer hall offers 20 rotating draft beers and ciders, delivered by on-site "flux capacitor."
address: 1125 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: Treadwell Park’s craft beer hall offers 20 rotating draft beers and ciders, delivered by on-site "flux capacitor." You’ll also find beer in some of the cocktails and ice cream floats. To accompany the brews, there are giant soft pretzels, in-house smoked chicken wings and juicy burgers. Ping pong, pinball, popcorn and big-screen TVs round out the entertainment.

name: Ginger Ristoranti
summary: Guided by the principles of the world’s Blue Zones—regions where vitality and longevity flourish—Ginger Ristoranti New York's cuisine is ingredient-driven, plant-forward, and rooted in refined simplicity.
address: 123 West 49th Street, New York, New York 10020, United States
summary2: Ginger Ristoranti New York is a reference point for those who choose a healthy and balanced Mediterranean diet. It's the right place for those who want a full and energetic breakfast, a tasty but light snack, a refined lunch or dinner. Their menus evolve with the rhythm of the seasons, celebrating ingredients that are thoughtfully sourced, organically grown, and prepared with a sense of harmony and purpose. Guided by the principles of the world’s Blue Zones—regions where vitality and longevity flourish—Ginger Ristoranti's cuisine is ingredient-driven, plant-forward, and rooted in refined simplicity. From breakfast through to the evening aperitivo, each dish is crafted with precision and purpose, embodying freshness, harmony and authenticity. This is Italian cuisine as it was meant to be: quietly wholesome, profoundly flavorful, and always a timeless pleasure.

name: Sake No Hana
summary: This lively, modern Japanese restaurant serves free-spirited izakaya dishes invigorated with New York attitude.
address: 145 Bowery, New York, New York 10002, United States
summary2: Occupying a dramatic, festive space, Sake No Hana is a lively modern Japanese restaurant that serves free-spirited izakaya dishes invigorated with New York attitude. With a shareable menu of grilled teppanyaki dishes, yakitori skewers, Wagyu beef, creative sushi rolls, and a curated list of sakes, beers, and cocktails highlighting Japanese spirits. The space buzzes with alluring energy perfect for any celebration.

name: DomoDomo NYC
summary: Domodomo is a premier Japanese restaurant specializing in handrolls, sushi, and modern interpretations of traditional Asian dishes.
address: 140 West Houston Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Domodomo is a premier Japanese restaurant specializing in handrolls, sushi, and modern interpretations of traditional Asian dishes. Their menu features classic options alongside unique, inspired dishes made with the freshest seasonal ingredients. Domodomo is renowned for their distinctive take on omakase, the "Domokase" course, which allows diners to sample a variety of their signature dishes at an accessible price point. Awarded the Michelin Bib Gourmand for eight consecutive years, Domodomo offers a delightful dining experience.

name: Moono
summary: Moono is the second project by chef Hoyoung Kim, building upon the success of his renowned Michelin 1-starred Jua, introducing the vibrant and evolving Korean food culture to New York City.
address: 29 East 32nd Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Moono is the second project by chef Hoyoung Kim, building upon the success of his renowned Michelin 1-starred Jua. Taking its name from the Korean word for “gateway,” Moono symbolizes a literal “door” to another world and represents a passage to diverse cultures. Housed in a stunning three-story building that is a recognized landmark of New York, Moono's mission is to serve as the ultimate gateway, introducing the vibrant and evolving Korean food culture to New York City, captivating the palates of the new generation.

name: Grand Brasserie
summary: The landmark Vanderbilt Hall, once Grand Central Terminal’s main waiting room, has been transformed into Grand Brasserie, a New York City meeting place with Parisian flair.
address: 89 East 42nd Street, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: The landmark Vanderbilt Hall, once Grand Central Terminal’s main waiting room, has been transformed into Grand Brasserie, a New York City meeting place with Parisian flair. The brasserie, open daily from 5:30am to 2:00am, is an airy 400-seat destination, featuring two impressive bars and dining rooms, offering a menu filled with timeless French classics. Whether you’re seeking a morning espresso, a leisurely lunch, or a late-night drink, Grand Brasserie is a go-to destination for authentic French cuisine in Manhattan's Midtown East.

name: Tanoreen
summary: Many are willing to travel far for food this good.
address: 7523 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10029, United States
summary2: Owner/chef Rawia Bishara is Palestinian, grew up in Nazareth, Israel, and named her restaurant for a town in Lebanon, so you know this isn't your standard Middle Eastern eatery. Many are willing to travel far for food this good, and the restaurant has been recognized with a number of awards. The hummus and baba ghanoush are dreamy, and grilled items, kebabs, meat pies and crunchy fattoush salad are equally satisfying.

name: The Gallery
summary: Enjoy artwork alongside delicious culinary creations and original cocktails at The Gallery, a new cultural space in the Flatiron District from chef Hiroki Odo.
address: 17 West 20th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Enjoy artwork alongside delicious culinary creations and original cocktails at The Gallery, a new cultural space in the Flatiron District from chef Hiroki Odo (Hall, Sushi Muse). Its debut exhibit, “Botanicals,” features fine-art prints of flowers, herbs and spices by photographer Cody Rasmussen. Chef Odo’s menu offers a variety of sushi and sashimi.

name: Del Frisco's Grille
summary: Located near Radio City and Times Square, Del Frisco's Grille features a sweeping bar with a wood-burning oven, expansive walls showcasing more than 700 bottles of wine and a sprawling patio perfect for al fresco dining.
address: 50 Rockefeller Plaza, New York, New York 10020, United States
summary2: Located near Radio City and Times Square, Del Frisco's Grille features a sweeping bar with a wood-burning oven, expansive walls showcasing more than 700 bottles of wine and a sprawling patio perfect for al fresco dining. The modern yet inviting décor is accented with stylish architectural elements and original works of art. The bar buzzes with the energy of the after-work scene, while the dining room provides the perfect setting for guests looking to escape from the rush of the City, meet with a client for a business lunch or dine with friends and family.

name: Blue Fin
summary: Set in Times Square—a neighborhood better known for trinkets and fast food chains—Blue Fin is an outlier and a standout.
address: 1567 Broadway, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Set in Times Square—a neighborhood better known for trinkets and fast food chains—Blue Fin is an outlier and a standout. Located in the groundfloor of the W Times Square, it shares the same sleek, design aesthetic, with modish appointments and a glitzy glass staircase. Meanwhile, the food is ambitious, but not outlandish: Scottish salmon is dressed with morels, sweet garlic and verjus; the fried softshell crab has a rhubarb vinaigrette, and some extra crunch from toasted macadamia nuts. In addition, there’s a raw bar, serving east and west coast oysters, assorted clams and caviar, and sushi, to boot.

name: Ma•dé
summary: Ma•dé draws inspiration from the sandy beaches of Bali for both its menu and décor.
address: 22 Spring Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: "Meaning “second born” in Balinese, Ma•dé is a new restaurant by chef Cédric Vongerichten, his wife Ochi Latjuba Vongerichten and their friend and business partner Ezra J. William. Ma•dé draws inspiration from the sandy beaches of Bali for both its menu and décor. At Ma•dé, Cédric serves a menu of fresh seafood and vegetable-centric dishes that emphasize global flavors and ingredients from diverse corners of the world, while the cocktail-driven beverage program boasts everything from vegetal and floral notes, to twists of savory umami that add a distinctive touch to each tipple.

name: Restaurant Nippon
summary: Opened in 1963, Restaurant Nippon became the first Japanese restaurant in the United States with an authentic sushi bar.
address: 155 East 52nd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Nippon has been the heartbeat of authentic Japanese cuisine in New York City since 1963. It's an East Midtown restaurant where tradition meets innovation in a setting as timeless as their heritage. The team at Nippon invites guests to indulge in a culinary journey through traditional Edo-mae (Tokyo) style dishes. Experience their signature dish, the iconic beef negimayaki, a dish that originated at Nippon and has since become a global favorite. Delight in the tempura straight from the tempura bar, a standout feature of their menu. Nippon also takes pride in their in-house creations, including premium ni-hachi soba noodles and house-made tofu, which elevate every dish to an extraordinary level. For a truly authentic experience, reserve the Japanese-style tatami room, a private space designed for intimate gatherings with traditional floor seating and elegant décor.

name: The Tuck Room
summary: Tucked away above iPic Theaters is this spirited drinking and dining den with an urban chic atmosphere.
address: 11 Fulton Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: Tucked away above IPIC Theaters at Fulton Market in the Seaport District is this spirited drinking and dining den, a vibrant social destination with an urban chic atmosphere. The Tuck Room showcases a diverse cocktail menu, which highlights the unique culture and liquid history of New York City. The dining menu at The Tuck Room presents unique and artful takes on classic, craveable American flavors.

name: Reyna
summary: Reyna is an alluring Mediterranean tapas restaurant and cocktail bar nestled in Union Square.
address: 11 East 13th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Reyna is an alluring Mediterranean tapas restaurant and cocktail bar nestled in Union Square. The moment you step through the door, you'll be transported to a world of robust flavors and tantalizing aromas. The convivial and fun ambiance is the perfect backdrop for a night of romance, spells of laughter among friends, or an anything-but-ordinary evening of indulgence. The menu features a selection of small plates and signature cocktails inspired by the vibrant cuisines across the Mediterranean.

name: Treadwell Park - Downtown
summary: Treadwell Park’s craft beer hall offers 20 rotating draft beers and ciders, as well as beer in some of the cocktails and ice cream floats.
address: 301 South End Avenue, New York, New York 10280, United States
summary2: Treadwell Park’s craft beer hall offers 20 rotating draft beers and ciders, delivered by on-site "flux capacitor." You’ll also find beer in some of the cocktails and ice cream floats. To accompany the brews, there are giant soft pretzels, in-house smoked chicken wings and juicy burgers. Ping pong, pinball, popcorn and big-screen TVs round out the entertainment.

name: The Quimby
summary: The Quimby is named after the United State's first licensed female pilot, Harriet Quimby, a pioneer in aviation, known for her style and adventurous spirit.
address: 135 West 142nd Street, New York, New York 10030, United States
summary2: The Quimby is a full-service restaurant and lounge located in Marriott New York JFK Airport that's open for breakfast, lunch, dinner and drinks. The Quimby is conveniently located next to one of the world's most well-known airports. Taking from those surroundings, The Quimby is named after the United State's first licensed female pilot, Harriet Quimby. Harriet was a pioneer in aviation, known for her style and adventurous spirit.

name: Virgil's Real BBQ - Times Square
summary: Good barbeque is surprisingly hard to find in New York, but Virgil's was among the first to boldly promise the real deal.
address: 152 West 44th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Good barbecue can be hard to find in New York, but Virgil’s was among the first to boldly promise the real deal. The interior is a version of classic, roadhouse Americana, and the kitchen serves ’cue in the many styles of the South: Thus you get Texas-style beef brisket, Carolina pulled pork, Memphis pork ribs and Georgia chicken-fried steak. But as any aficionado knows, the sides are just as important, and Virgil’s has a slew of them, including hush puppies, biscuits and gravy, and “Train Wreck Fries,” slathered in a mouthwatering mix guaranteed to infuriate your doctor: cheddar, bacon and ranch dressing.

name: Neir's Tavern
summary: The oldest bar in Queens (and possibly the City), Neir's serves up a simple setting and uncomplicated drinks.
address: 11421 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: The oldest bar in Queens (and possibly the oldest in the City—it dates its origin as far back as 1829, having been through a few incarnations since then), Neir's serves locals with a taste for a simple setting and uncomplicated drinks. Mae West performed here and Martin Scorsese filmed part of Goodfellas on site. Loycent Gordon, a firefighter, bought the bar back in 2009 and has been preserving its history ever since. Visitors should keep their eyes peeled when trying to find the place—it's housed in a relatively nondescript brown townhouse.

name: Masseria Dei Vini
summary: In the region of Puglia, in Southern Italy, masserias are fortified farmhouses, and many of them have now been transformed into restaurants or hotels.
address: 887 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: In the region of Puglia, in Southern Italy, masserias are fortified farmhouses, and many of them have now been transformed into restaurants or hotels. Masseria Dei Vini ("The Farmhouse of Wines") is the new venture from the La Masseria team. Restaurateurs Pino Coladonato, Peppe Iuele and Enzo Ruggiero have collaborated again with interior design expert Libby Langdon to bring you a modern and updated version of a masseria.

name: Socarrat Paella Bar - Midtown East
summary: Socarrat is the sensuous crust that forms on the bottom of the paella pan when the liquid is rendered and the rice reaches its peak of succulence.
address: 953 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Socarrat is the crust that forms on the bottom of the paella pan when the liquid is rendered and the rice reaches its peak of succulence. Socarrat Paella Bar–Midtown East is a lunch and dinner destination in Manhattan's bustling Midtown East neighborhood. This restaurant offers authentic Spanish cuisine and upscale service.

name: David Burke Tavern
summary: David Burke Tavern is a modern American tavern on the Upper East Side that features American plates as a reflection of chef Burke’s contemporary approach to cooking, with a nod to elevated New York classics.
address: 135 East 62nd Street, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: David Burke Tavern is a modern American restaurant situated in a stately townhouse on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The casual tavern atmosphere of the first floor gives way to sophisticatedly relaxed, clubby rooms on the second. It offers lunch, dinner and brunch, as well as a daily happy hour. The menu features the contemporary American cuisine of which chef/owner David Burke is a much-celebrated pioneer, often accented with his signature playful approach to cooking, with a nod to elevated New York classics, paired with a curated wine list, craft beers and a specialty cocktail program.

name: Becco
summary: Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service.
address: 355 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: The name Becco is derived from the Italian verb, beccare, which means "to peck, nibble or savor something in a discriminating way." Lidia Bastianich and her son, Joe, opened Becco in 1993, and since then it has been providing New York diners with outstanding service. Located on New York's famed Restaurant Row in the Theatre District, Becco is open seven days a week for lunch and dinner. Becco is most famous for its innovative pasta tasting menu and extensive wine list, featuring more than 100 bottles of wine, all priced at $40.

name: Maisonetta
summary: Maisonetta captures the true essence of fine French dining and the gastronomy of Mexican flavors and traditions.
address: 141 Lincoln Avenue, Bronx, New York 10454, United States
summary2: The vision at Maisonetta (the name is a combination of "maison" and "casita,"  the words for "house" in French and Spanish, respectively) is to provide a culinary experience that joins two cultures under one roof. Capturing the true essence of fine French dining and the gastronomy of Mexican flavors and traditions, Maisonetta is both unique and diverse.

name: Lillie's Victorian—Union Square
summary: Combines an authentic ostentatious decor and mellow ambiance, representing one of the last great Victorian "gin palaces" that once flourished in the industrial cities of Northern Ireland and England.
address: 13 East 17th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Lillie’s Victorian Establishment combines an authentic ostentatious decor with a down-to-earth, mellow ambiance representing one of the last great Victorian "gin palaces" that once flourished in the industrial cities of Northern Ireland and England. Lillie's serves an eclectic yet traditional menu and an impressive range of over 50 domestic and imported beers, as well as a fine selection of whiskeys, scotches and wines.

name: Lafayette
summary: Lafayette, a French restaurant in downtown Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood, is at once a gorgeous dining destination, vibrant nightspot and delectable French bakery.
address: 380 Lafayette Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Lafayette, a French restaurant in downtown Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood, is at once a gorgeous dining destination, vibrant nightspot and delectable French bakery. Open morning, noon and night, this grand café and bakery is dedicated to chef Andrew Carmellini's market-driven bistro cooking in a stunning setting. The light-filled dining room features soaring arched windows overlooking the NoHo streetscapes and a lively rotisserie bar. The corner boulangerie-patisserie is open all hours, offering artisanal breads, croissants, Stumptown coffee drinks, a light breakfast or lunch and a host of confections.

name: Nougatine at Jean-Georges
summary: Perhaps the best way to sample dishes from one of world-famous chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten's menus without breaking the bank is by dining at Nougatine, an overlooked gem on the Upper West Side.
address: 1 Central Park West, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Perhaps the best way to sample dishes from one of world-famous chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s menus without breaking the bank is by dining at Nougatine, an overlooked gem on the Upper West Side that's attached to Jean-Georges on Central Park West.

name: Mito - Forest Hills
summary: Mito's esteemed head chef, who has devoted numerous years to the masterful art of cooking, brings with him a wealth of experience at esteemed establishments such as Jean Georges and Buddha Bar.
address: 11375 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: The definition of modern Japanese cuisine is innovation. It refers to a new and imaginative approach to cooking and presentation of food, it pushes the boundaries of traditional culinary techniques, and it incorporates unexpected ingredients and flavors to create unique and unforgettable dining experiences. Mito's esteemed head chef, who has devoted numerous years to the masterful art of cooking, brings with him a wealth of experience at esteemed establishments such as Jean Georges and Buddha Bar. With his addition to their team, the owners anticipate elevating Mito to unprecedented heights.

name: Felice 64
summary: Italian wines and flavors from Tuscany are served in a modern space infused with traditional elements on the Upper East Side.
address: 1166 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10065, United States
summary2: This cozy Manhattan restaurant showcases a relaxed ambience, with subdued lighting, exposed brick walls lined with linear shelves filled with wine, as well as rich, tufted leather seats. Italian wines and flavors from Tuscany are served in a modern space infused with traditional elements on the Upper East Side.

name: Le B.
summary: Tableside presentations, intricate flavors, and forgotten pleasures mined from the history books are hallmarks of Le B.’s ethos.
address: 283 West 12th Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Le B. is a stylish, supper-club setting, taking inspiration from a 100-year history in Lower Manhattan. With a Continental menu interpreted for the modern diner, the cuisine celebrates all animals from the land and sea. Set in a jewel-like dining room, Le B. channels the energy and joie de vivre of Angie Mar’s beloved, cult favorite restaurant, The Beatrice Inn, while showcasing her unwavering dedication to technique and hospitality. Tableside presentations, intricate flavors, and forgotten pleasures mined from the history books are hallmarks of Le B.’s ethos, filtered through the lens of modern-day downtown NYC.

name: Jacob's Pickles
summary: Pickles are more than just a garnish at this Southern-inspired eatery; they're a way of life.
address: 680 Columbus Avenue, New York, New York 10025, United States
summary2: Pickles are more than just a garnish at this Southern-inspired eatery; they’re a way of life. Diners can partake of the spot’s many different pickled veggies, from your standard kosher dills to pickled green beans and beets. Those not in a briny state of mind can opt for neo-Southern grub including sausages made from humanely raised beef, and shrimp and bacon grits and biscuits crafted from sustainable ingredients.

name: Luigi's
summary: Since 1992, guests have come to Luigi's in New Hyde Park, Queens, to enjoy a well-made cocktail, a diverse selection of wines and an unforgettable meal.
address: 11040 12th Avenue, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Since 1992, guests have come to Luigi's, located on the eastern edge of NYC in New Hyde Park, Queens, to enjoy a well-made cocktail, a diverse selection of wines and an unforgettable meal. These elements, plus the warm and welcoming atmosphere, the friendly and familiar service, and the personal greeting at the door have enticed them to return again and again. Whether you're bringing the entire family for Sunday Dinner, your partner for date night, your client for a lunch meeting for the first time or for the 100th, Luigi's promises to provide an effortless and memorable experience.

name: Kissaki
summary: The East Village is home to a luxurious sushi experience in a narrow space curved like a knife blade.
address: 319 Bowery, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Kissaki means "point of a sword" or "cutting edge" in Japanese, both of which apply here since the sushi bar is curved like a knife blade. Executive chef Edgar Valerio (formerly of Jewel Bako) mixes traditional and nontraditional flavor and technique to create inventive omakase, and a la carte sushi is available at the cocktail bar.

name: Twin Tails
summary: Twin Tails is a new Thai and Vietnamese restaurant from Quality Branded, located within The Shops at Columbus Circle.
address: 10 Columbus Circle, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Twin Tails is a new Thai and Vietnamese restaurant from Quality Branded, the team behind Bad Roman, Zou Zou’s, and other Manhattan staples. The menu includes fresh crudos, bright, herbaceous salads and small bites, and entrée favorites like Tiger Prawn Pad Thai, Red Curry Sea Bass, and the best-selling Cho Lon Duck. On the beverage side, the cocktail menu features a new take on the Lychee Martini and many fun riffs that will soon become signatures, while the wine list has strong French influence with entire sections dedicated to Sancerre, demi-secs, and vintage Bordeaux. Twin Tails is located within The Shops at Columbus Circle, and is open for lunch and dinner daily.

name: Petite Boucherie
summary: Located at the historic intersection of Christopher and Gay Streets, Petite Boucherie brings a touch of France to the cultured and eclectic neighborhood of the West Village.
address: 14 Christopher Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Located at the historic intersection of Christopher and Gay Streets, Petite Boucherie brings a touch of France to the cultured and eclectic neighborhood of the West Village. An intimate window-laden, corner restaurant serves French classics like Les Escargots and Steak au Poivre, along with the exclusive Boucherie Wine Collection, a proprietary staple of the Boucherie brand. Petite Boucherie is inspired by the elegance of Parisian Belle Époque, and with a hand-crafted menu of timeless​ dishes, the intimate bistro serves as a community hub for engaging conversation.​

name: Brooklyn Chop House - Times Square
summary: This clubby spot serves steakhouse classics and Asian dishes in Times Square.
address: 253 West 47th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: This clubby spot serves steakhouse classics and Asian dishes in Times Square. Dine on strip steak, rib-eye or filet mignon, and enjoy clever appetizers like deli-sandwich-influenced dumplings (including pastrami, Rueben, and lamb gyro). There are plenty of other options, too—including chopped house salads, Kung Pao chicken and a slow-roasted seven-pound Peking duck.

name: Greywind
summary: Chef Dan Kluger offers a seasonally-driven, vegetable-forward dining experience that creatively highlights seasonal ingredients and rotisserie cooking.
address: 451 10th Avenue, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: At Greywind, James Beard Award-winning chef Dan Kluger offers a seasonally-driven, vegetable-forward dining experience that creatively highlights seasonal ingredients and rotisserie cooking. To complement chef Kluger’s menu, the beverage program has a special focus on small and up-and-coming producers, distillers, and brewers in New York.

name: Indian Table
summary: Indian Table showcases the flavors, herbs, spices and cooking techniques of Goa, the coastal Indian state once colonized by the Portuguese, with a distinct British influence.
address: 234 Court Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Indian Table pays homage to the food, art and culture of India in Brooklyn’s Cobble Hill neighborhood. Indian Table showcases the flavors, herbs, spices and cooking techniques of Goa, the coastal Indian state once colonized by the Portuguese, with a distinct British influence. The menu is inspired by executive chef Eric McCarthy, who grew up in the Goan village of Candolim and led the kitchens of acclaimed NYC restaurants Tamarind, Tulsi and Brick Lane Curry House.

name: Il Falco
summary: Chef-owner Bolivar Perez has decades of experience cooking Italian fine cuisine.
address: 21-50 44th Drive, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Chef-owner Bolivar Perez has decades of experience cooking Italian fine cuisine. He came to the US in the mid-1980s and worked his way up at one of the most acclaimed and recognized restaurants in NYC, Il Mulino. He has served numerous celebrities and dignitaries, including former Presidents Barack Obama and Bill Clinton.

name: Kraam
summary: Kraam, a restaurant in NoMad, serves up authentic Thai cuisine with playful culinary twists.
address: 254 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Kraam, a restaurant in NoMad, serves up authentic Thai cuisine with playful culinary twists. The name comes from a Thai word for indigo or organic dye, and is also a word synonymous with "craft" or "wisdom passed down through generations." The menu incorporates dishes from various regions of Thailand with seasonal and higher quality ingredients. Expect appetizers like Koi Tuna, a Thai style yellowfin tuna tartare on lettuce cups garnished with crispy shallots and toasted rice. Aromatic soups include Tom Kha Artichoke, a creamy coconut base soup with banana blossoms and aromatic herbs. The menu rotates seasonally.

name: L'Express
summary: Enjoy the Gallic fare at L'Express 24/7—breakfast, lunch, dinner, brunch, pre-club, post-club, and instead of club.
address: 249 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: For the Francophile who craves French cuisine all day, every day, take note. You can enjoy the Gallic fare at L'Express 24/7—breakfast, lunch, dinner, brunch, pre-club, post-club, and instead of club. And they deliver. Not up for French cuisine? Not to worry: order Le Burger.

name: Villa Berulia
summary: Located on 34th Street in the historic Murray Hill district of Manhattan, Villa Berulia offers a bucolic retreat from the hectic area around the Empire State Building only four blocks away.
address: 107 East 34th Street, New York, New York 10016, United States
summary2: Located on 34th Street in the historic Murray Hill district of Manhattan, Villa Berulia offers a bucolic retreat from the hectic area around the Empire State Building only four blocks away. The menu will put you in a European state of mind with its homemade pastas, wild game dishes and Croatian and Dalmatian Coast delicacies, including venison osso bucco and seafood Buzara, a traditional Dalmatian Coast stew with sea bass, shrimp and clams. The restaurant opened in the early 1980s and is a mainstay with the locals.

name: T Bar
summary: New York has some of the best steaks in the country, and this restaurant on the Upper East Side certainly holds its own.
address: 116 East 60th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: New York has some of the best steaks in the country, and this restaurant on the Upper East Side certainly holds its own. Formerly the Lenox Room, it reopened as T-Bar Steak and Lounge in 2007 with a renovated downtown décor. This new T Bar is a tri-level space with a sensual luxe vibe, the perfect setting to experience a lavish menu featuring accents and flavors from the world over.

name: Kyma
summary: Dine on pristine seafood at this upscale Greek restaurant.
address: 15 West 18th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Within Kyma's modern ambiance, the threads of the traditional Greek taverna are woven with the stylish island chic of Mykonos. The menu guides you to the sun-drenched islands of Greece to embrace the rich character of its traditional dishes. Kyma adheres to strict standards, using the highest quality extra virgin olive oil from the Peloponnese and fresh fish flown in daily from the Mediterranean.

name: Sinigual
summary: Sinigual celebrates a fusion of contemporary and native flavors of Mexico.
address: 640 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Sinigual celebrates a fusion of contemporary and native flavors of Mexico. Even the name itself is a fusion of words, meaning “without equal, above the rest and unique.” A visit starts with handmade tortillas served with fresh salsa quemada, salsa roja and signature honey butter. Creative dishes honor traditional Mexican classics.

name: The Dolar Shop Hot Pot
summary: The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.
address: 55 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: The Dolar Shop Hot Pot story began in the Las Vegas of the East: Macau. The name “Dolar” comes from a Chinese term embodying the people’s willingness to work hard to gather prosperity, fortune, and never turning down any opportunities.
