And "Shop?"... they are artisans in their workshop, and their craft is hot pot. Be prepared to indulge in the delectable house-made ingredients. Hot Pot is one of the most beloved ways of dining in Chinese culture. Influences from both the East and West in Macau led to love for home-made fish balls and slices of high-grade beef. These top notch ingredients paired with the blend of sauces makes it a unique experience. The Dolar Shop's philosophy is to continuously innovate, always serve fresh ingredients, and to excel in customer service to build a strong connection with their guests, and proudly showcase the Macau hot pot culture.

name: Noreetuh
summary: Noreetuh is a modern Hawaiian restaurant in the East Village from chef Chung Chow.
address: 128 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10009, United States
summary2: Noreetuh is a modern Hawaiian restaurant in the East Village from chef Chung Chow. The menu is complemented by a carefully curated wine list of approximately 200 selections with a strong representation from France. In addition to the wines, there are a number of craft beers and specialty sakes on the list as well. The restaurant’s goal is to create an atmosphere where guests can enjoy artfully crafted food paired with a  wine list in a casual, enjoyable environment, thus reflecting the place's name, which translates as "playground."

name: Casa Brazilian
summary: This charming Tribeca restaurant has been serving up Brazilian home cooking in the West Village since 1998.
address: 157 Duane Street, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Now located in Tribeca, this charming restaurant has been serving up Brazilian home cooking since 1998 in the West Village. Brazil’s varied geography and rich cultural history are reflected in a diverse menu that includes coastal seafood preparations like Bahian seafood stew, southern churrasco meat dishes such as grilled steak and national favorites like pao de queijo, a savory gluten-free cheese bread. Brazilian expats in the know finish up their meals with the house-made pudim de leite (caramel flan).

name: Bar56
summary: A Modern American menu with Italian and French influences is complemented by a carefully curated wine list to provide "Palate Character."
address: 53 Water Street, Brooklyn, New York 11201, United States
summary2: Bar56 is restaurateur and owner James Fantaci’s modern American restaurant located under the Brooklyn Bridge in DUMBO in a landmark building dating back to 1892. Leading the culinary vision is executive chef Quentin Demarre, crafting a seasonally-driven Modern American menu with Italian and French influences. The cuisine is complemented by a carefully curated wine list, organized by style which they call "Palate Character," a distinctive reserve list, and handcrafted cocktails. All of the wines on the list available for purchase next door at taste56.

name: Seawolf - Bushwick
summary: Seawolf feels like a friendly surf shack in the middle of Bushwick, with cheery décor and a focus on sustainable seafood and fresh ingredients.
address: 19 Wyckoff Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11237, United States
summary2: Seawolf is a vibrant seafood and American restaurant rooted in Brooklyn's coastal spirit. Established in the Bushwick neighborhood in 2016, Seawolf has become a local favorite for its sustainable sourcing and community-driven ethos. The menu features fresh oysters, lobster rolls, tacos, burgers, and craft cocktails, all served in a laid-back, welcoming space that captures the energy of Bushwick. The restaurant proudly supports the Billion Oyster Project, donating thousands of oyster shells annually to help restore New York Harbor's reef ecosystems. Whether you visit for Lobster Madness Mondays with $55 seafood specials, sip $12 martinis and sing karaoke every Thursday, or join the weekend crowd for happy hour and late-night parties, you'll find good food, good drinks, and good times.

name: La Pecora Bianca Midtown
summary: La Pecora Bianca Midtown offers an expanded menu from Mario Batali alum Cruz Goler in a bright, sophisticated space nearly twice the size of the original in NoMad.
address: 950 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: La Pecora Bianca Midtown offers an expanded menu from Mario Batali alum Cruz Goler in a bright, sophisticated space nearly twice the size of the original La Pecora Bianca in NoMad. Chef Goler takes Italian fare back to its roots as an inherently local and seasonal cuisine with a menu emphasizing vegetables and house-made pastas. In addition to classic La Pecora Bianca dishes such as gramigna with sausage and broccolini, the expanded menu features spuntini (small Italian snacks), shareable plates and a broad selection of fish and meat.

name: Jacques Brasserie
summary: Jacques Brasserie is a romantic bistro that feels like one of those off-the-tourist track places that you always hope to find in Paris.
address: East 85th Street, New York, New York 10028, United States
summary2: Jacques Brasserie is a romantic bistro that feels like one of those off-the-tourist-track places that you always hope to find in Paris. There's cozy atmosphere, great food and ambiance. Jacques Brasserie is known for its Nantucket fresh oysters and delicious steak au poivre.

name: Yakiniku Futago
summary: Sleek and dimly lit Yakiniku Futago specializes in Japanese barbecue.
address: 37 West 17th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Sleek and dimly lit, Yakiniku Futago specializes in Japanese barbecue (yakiniku means “to barbecue” in Japanese, and futago means “twins”—so named for the owners, twin brothers from Osaka). In addition to beer and wine, their drink menu includes sake by glass or carafe, shochu and chuhai. Don’t be surprised if some Korean specialties also appear on the menu. Futago offers bento boxes and DIY barbecue kits to-go.

name: Chito Gvrito NYC
summary: Chito Gvrito's seasonal menu offers classic Georgian flavors with modern twists using locally sourced ingredients paired with natural Georgian wines and craft cocktails.
address: 173 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Chito Gvrito NYC represents the spirit of the nation of Georgia: sunny, generous and eclectic. Their seasonal menu offers classic Georgian dishes with modern twists using locally sourced ingredients. Discover the vibrant flavors of Georgia, which offer something for everyone—vegetarians will love dishes like Mushroom Khinkali and Georgian Salad, while meat lovers can indulge in Heritage Pork Mtsvadi skewers or Chkmeruli Chicken Tabaka. Similar to Mediterranean flavors, their menu highlights fresh, locally sourced ingredients. Pair your meal with Georgian orange wine or a craft cocktail for a truly unforgettable dining experience.

name: Pinky Swear
summary: Pinky Swear is an art-forward restaurant and cocktail bar on Manhattan's Lower East Side where creativity, connection, and discovery collide.
address: 171a Chrystie Street, New York, New York 10002, United States
summary2: Pinky Swear is an art-forward restaurant and cocktail bar on Manhattan's Lower East Side where creativity, connection, and discovery collide. Interactive installations, rotating exhibitions, creative dishes by chef Will Horowitz, and a vibrant drinks menu are featured in the space where guests are invited to explore, play, and lose themselves in the unexpected—no two nights here are ever the same.

name: Churrascaria Plataforma Brazilian Steakhouse
summary: Churrascaria Plataforma Brazilian Steakhouse is a rodízio-style restaurant.
address: 316 West 49th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Churrascaria (choo-rah-scah-ree-ah) is the word for a restaurant that serves meat, mostly grilled, and the rodízio style—serving different cuts of meat—originated in the south of Brazil in the early 1800s. The concept is to serve a wide variety of different cuts of meat, including beef, pork, lamb and chicken, in succession to each diner individually right at their table, thus there is not a traditional menu. Churrascaria Plataforma is the authentic NYC rodízio-style restaurant that features an all-you-can-eat fixed price with continuous table-side service.

name: Ayza
summary: Enjoy an impeccable experience amid sleek, modern décor as you choose from 90 fine wines and champagnes from around the world.
address: 11 West 31st Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Ayza Wine & Chocolate Bar, conveniently located near the Empire State Building and Macy’s since 2007, celebrates New York's rich diversity and vibrant spirit. Their signature pairing of fine wines and gourmet chocolates offers a unique indulgence for wine lovers and sweet tooths alike. Ayza's original chocolate martinis are always a guest favorite. In addition to these pairings, they offer a full menu catering to all tastes, from fine dining in a casual, elegant setting to a relaxed space to unwind. Enjoy an impeccable experience amid sleek, modern décor as you choose from more than 100 fine wines and champagnes from around the world. Meet friends or have drinks after work in an elegant, comfortable atmosphere, and take advantage of their enclosed heated garden. Choose from a full menu of salads, tapas, main courses, savory cheese and charcuterie, Jacques Torres chocolates, chocolate martinis and more.

name: Dos Caminos Meatpacking District
summary: The fourth NYC outpost of this mod-Mexican mini-empire boasts a chic Meatpacking District address (in the prominent space formerly occupied by Vento Trattoria).
address: 675 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: The fourth NYC outpost of this mod-Mexican mini-empire boasts a chic Meatpacking District address (in the prominent space formerly occupied by Vento Trattoria). Like its sister restaurants, you can count on Dos Caminos Meatpacking for mouthwatering guacamole—made tableside, of course—inventive cocktails (such as a prickly pear cactus margarita), more than 100 types of tequila and contemporary takes on traditional Mexican delicacies, including tequila-cured salmon ceviche and braised short rib and tamarind tacos. Unique to this branch, however, is the kitchen’s wood-fired oven, which accounts for smokier subtleties in many dishes.

name: Planet Hollywood New York
summary: Located in Times Square, this famous eatery shares the bustle and flash of its surroundings.
address: 136 West 42nd Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: The new Planet Hollywood represents more than just an evolution—it’s a full sensory experience where contemporary design meets interactive storytelling, redefining the way we connect over great food and unforgettable moments.

name: Kyma Hudson Yards
summary: Kyma's whitewashed interior, decorated with Greek pottery and ceramics, echoes the style of a restaurant in Santorini.
address: 445 West 35th Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Within Kyma's modern ambiance, the threads of the traditional Greek taverna are woven with the stylish island chic of Mykonos. The menu guides you to the sun-drenched islands of Greece to embrace the rich character of its traditional dishes. Kyma adheres to strict standards, using the highest quality extra virgin olive oil from the Peloponnese and fresh fish flown in daily from the Mediterranean.

name: The Long Room
summary: The Long Room is an authentic Irish bar and gastropub located in Times Square.
address: 120 West 44th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: The Long Room is an authentic Irish bar and gastropub located in Times Square. The menu features a variety of creative dishes, from standard American fare to delicious and hearty traditional Irish fare with a New York twist. Like any good (spirits) library, they stock a large selection of Irish whiskeys, single malts, top-shelf liquors, craft cocktails and fine wines. In addition to domestic and imported draught beers, rotating craft beers, they also offer beers by the bottle/can.

name: Rosevale Cocktail Room
summary: Rosevale Cocktail Room,  located inside the Civilian Hotel, offers a world-class beverage experience alongside delectable bites.
address: 305 West 48th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Rosevale Cocktail Room offers a world-class beverage experience alongside delectable bites. From table-side mixology to reimagined classics, the Cocktail Room has something for everyone. The sprawling venue features soaring ceilings and red brick walls that spill out into a serene outdoor terrace. The intimate Blue Room is encircled with original Broadway relics and perfect for small groups.

name: Tonchin Brooklyn
summary: A modern Japanese restaurant featuring a full a la carte menu grounded in traditional flavors, with a New American twist.
address: 109 North 3rd Street, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Tonchin Brooklyn is a modern Japanese restaurant featuring a full a la carte menu grounded in traditional flavors, with a New American twist. The extensive natural wine list and signature ramen anchor the journey as Tonchin explores the intersection between Tokyo and Brooklyn, uncovering new ways of preparing fresh local food in the Japanese spirit.

name: Melba’s
summary: Restaurateur Melba Wilson says she is "born, bread and buttered" in Harlem.
address: 300 West 114th Street, New York, New York 10026, United States
summary2: Restaurateur Melba Wilson says she is “born, bread and buttered” in Harlem, and this sleek, busy uptown spot lives up to that motto from top to bottom. The menu features handed-down favorites from Melba’s Southern Carolina grandmother: wine-braised short ribs, catfish po’ boys, the requisite chicken and waffles, and sides such as black-eyes peas and collard greens.

name: A La Turka
summary: A La Turka is a Turkish restaurant known for its family recipes, lively atmosphere and authentic Mediterranean-style flavors.
address: 1417 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10021, United States
summary2: A La Turka is a Turkish restaurant known for its family recipes, lively atmosphere and authentic Mediterranean-style flavors. Although its menu is heavily populated with kebabs and seafood, A La Turka also offers a wide variety of healthy and vegetarian appetizers selected from different regions of Turkey and Ottoman cuisine.

name: abcV
summary: Jean-Georges Vongerichten performs magic with vegetables.
address: 38 East 19th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's abcV (“V” stands for vegetables) is a radiant outgrowth of Flatiron gems ABC Kitchen and ABC Cocina. The bathed-in-white showroom has a bar and communal standing table up front; in the rear is a dining room facing the windowed kitchen. Good knife skills are key for chefs here, and the dice is precise on yams and broccoli stems dotting beluga lentils flavored with black vinegar and sneaky heat from chili oil. Diners can substitute shaved crudité for pita to scoop up drop-dead gorgeous kabocha squash dip. The beverage menu is creative and wide-ranging.

name: Psaraki
summary: Psaraki, the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis, evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece.
address: 420 Kent Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11249, United States
summary2: Psaraki, meaning “little fish” in Greek, is the creation of longtime hospitality veteran James Paloumbis. The restaurant evokes the charm of seaside tavernas found along the shores of Greece. It offers spectacular views of the Brooklyn Bridge, the Manhattan skyline, and the Williamsburg Bridge, juxtaposing the tranquility of its serene ambiance with the vibrant energy of nearby Manhattan. Psaraki is a place to unwind, enjoy a perfect cocktail, and savor traditional homemade Greek dishes meant for sharing while escaping NYC's hustle and bustle. Psaraki’s menu is inspired by James’ culinary philosophy, which he terms “homemade,” where each dish is a testament to the authenticity and connection of family recipes, traditionally prepared and presented as if one was a visitor in James’ seaside home. Guests can enjoy a sampling of classic Greek dishes and a selection of Greek island favorites.

name: Arte Cafe
summary: This family-owned restaurant presents an upscale Italian cuisine with artisanal homemade pizzas and gourmet desserts.
address: 106 West 73rd Street, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Arte Cafe is located in a landmark brownstone on the Upper West Side, steps away from Central Park and just west of beautiful Strawberry Fields. This family-owned restaurant, which recently celebrated 25 years, presents an upscale Italian cuisine with artisanal homemade pizzas and gourmet desserts. The location has two private event rooms available for special occasions at all budgets. All areas accommodate small intimate parties and larger events.

name: Schilling
summary: Schilling offers a day-to-night bistro that features Michelin-starred chef Eduard Frauneder's contemporary take on Austrian fare.
address: 109 Washington Street, New York, New York 10006, United States
summary2: Located in the Financial District, Schilling is another endeavor by Michelin-starred chef Eduard Frauneder of the East Village's beloved Austrian tavern Edi & the Wolf, cocktail bar The Third Man and Greenwich Village brasserie Freud. With a name that nods to the surrounding neighborhood and the former Austrian currency, Schilling offers a day-to-night bistro that features Frauneder's contemporary take on Austrian fare, this time with a Mediterranean touch. A menu of classic cocktails from the team behind The Third Man complements the market-driven, seasonal menu.

name: The Noortwyck
summary: Set in the West Village, The Noortwyck exudes an elegant yet intimate charm, offering a timeless, New American menu that celebrates seasonal dishes, an extensive wine selection and specialty cocktails.
address: 289 Bleecker Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Set in the West Village, The Noortwyck exudes an elegant yet intimate charm, offering a timeless, New American menu that celebrates seasonal dishes, an extensive wine selection and specialty cocktails. Founded by executive chef Andy Quinn and sommelier Cedric Nicaise, the restaurant is committed to delivering the best quality for each guest and supporting the local community. Embracing the ethos of sourcing from nearby New York purveyors, The Noortwyck crafts everything in-house, from pasta and breads to dry aging. The wine list reflects both the team’s interest and Cedric’s expertise, curated to cater to the diverse tastes of their guests, running the full gamut of styles, from earthy and funky to clean and fruity. Garnering acclaim from critics and locals alike, The Noortwyck is “the middle ground between grandeur and informality.”

name: Chazz Palminteri Italian Restaurant
summary: Chazz Palminteri's features the finest meat, seafood and pasta dishes, as well as antipasto and traditional Italian desserts.
address: 30 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Chazz Palminteri's is an upscale Italian eatery, opened by actor Chazz Palminteri in partnership with the owners of Empire Steak House. This restaurant offers the finest meat, seafood, and pasta dishes, as well as antipasto and traditional Italian desserts. Chazz offers a global wine list boasting close to 250 wines and is curated to pair with the bold, rich flavors of classic Italian fare. There's also custom cocktails featuring spirits blended with seasonal ingredients, with an Italian twist.

name: Baires Grill New York
summary: The menu at Baires Grill New York features homemade dishes that capture the rich, traditional flavors of Argentine cuisine.
address: 350 West 50th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Experience the true spirit of Argentina at Baires Grill, recognized as one of the top Argentine steakhouses in the United States. Founded in 1999 at South Beach, Florida, Baires has several locations across Florida as well as this Hell's Kitchen location in Manhattan. The menu features homemade dishes that capture the rich, traditional flavors of Argentine cuisine. Baires Grill is perfect for romantic dinners, business meetings, or family gatherings, providing the ideal ambiance for any occasion. Delight in a harmonious fusion of flavors, complemented by a premium cocktail menu and an extensive wine list featuring exceptional Argentine labels alongside top selections from around the world.

name: The Library at The Public
summary: The Library, named for the building's original use as the Astor Library, is a central element of the mezzanine level of this landmark edifice at Astor Place (which famously houses downtown performance venue The Public Theater).
address: 425 Lafayette Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: The Library, named for the building's original use as the Astor Library, is a central element of the mezzanine level of this landmark edifice at Astor Place (which famously houses downtown performance venue The Public Theater). This warmly decorated supper club, open late nightly for dinner and cocktail service, is a dinner bar, watering hole and backstage lounge for downtown denizens and neighborhood dwellers, theatergoers, academics and artists alike. Chefs Andrew Carmellini and Zach Faulisi offer an eclectic American menu of bar snacks, shareable appetizers, sandwiches, dinner plates and desserts sourcing local ingredients with a New York influence.

name: The Half Pint
summary: Enjoy a craft beer—the Half Pint's specialty—with a sandwich, burger or something else from the pub-grub menu.
address: 76 West 3rd Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: If the name didn't give it away, know that The Half Pint specializes in craft beers, with about two dozen on draft in addition to many in cans and bottles. Enjoy one with a sandwich, burger or something else from the pub-grub menu. Ernie's at The Half Pint is an ode to Ernie's 3 Ring Circus located at this address back in the 1940s-'60s. Visit Ernie's for classic American beers and cocktails from the period plus a small menu of fine fare.

name: Chelsea Ristorante
summary: Chelsea Ristorante combines the rich tradition of Italian cuisine with casual but elegant design and architecture in an updated and innovative setting.
address: 108 8th Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Chelsea Ristorante combines the rich tradition of Italian cuisine with casual but elegant design and architecture in an updated and innovative setting. Homemade pasta, risotto and traditional Italian fare together with dishes from its wood-burning oven make up the menu of this Chelsea neighborhood icon. Chelsea Ristorante serves lunch and dinner every day of the week with the option of sidewalk dining in warmer months. Whether for business or pleasure, an intimate private lunch or dinner party, or cocktails for a large gathering, Chelsea Ristorante and its amicable and attentive wait staff provide a perfect dining experience.

name: The Stand
summary: The Stand was recently voted New York's "Best Comedy Club" by New York magazine and regularly hosts top comedians like Judah Friedlander, Todd Barry, Janeane Garofalo and more.
address: 116 East 16th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: This Union Square-area comedy club has hosted both bold-faced talent and up-and-comers, and features an impressive menu of Italian victuals. Look out for pizzas, steak, rotisserie chicken, an all-day brunch and a menu of tasty mixed drinks.

name: Zoì Mediterranean UES
summary: Blue Mezze Bar - UES is a unique Mediterranean restaurant/bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side with an extensive mezze and cocktail menu, ideal for sharing and tasting.
address: 1480 2nd Avenue, New York, New York 10075, United States
summary2: Blue Mezze Bar - UES is a unique Mediterranean restaurant-bar on Manhattan's Upper East Side. It has an extensive mezze and cocktail menu, ideal for sharing and tasting—perfect for friends, family or that upcoming date. The Blue serves a Mediterranean menu with a modern twist—fresh fish, tenderloin, vegetables, salads, a noteworthy lentil dish and homemade signature hummus—designed to elevate the fresh ingredients to the next level.

name: Stout NYC Grand Central
summary: Find Stout NYC Grand Central in the midst of New York City icons including the Chrysler Building and the New York Public Library.
address: 60 East 41st Street, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Located in the Murray Hill neighborhood of East Midtown Manhattan, you can find Stout NYC Grand Central in the midst of New York City icons including the Chrysler Building and the New York Public Library. They're open for lunch, dinner and drinks. This two-story Stout location is so close to Grand Central Terminal that you can have “just one” before you catch the train home—they’ll even watch the time for you.

name: Boucherie West Village
summary: Boucherie West Village is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse, celebrating Joie de Vivre, that prepares a menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, in addition to dry-aged steaks.
address: 99 7th Avenue South, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Boucherie West Village is a traditional French brasserie and steakhouse celebrating Joie de Vivre in the West Village. The restaurant features an ample menu of French classics and timeless bistro favorites, such as the Mousse de Foie Gras and the signature Boucherie Burger, in addition to delectable dry-aged meats. Alongside an extensive wine list featuring the exclusive Boucherie Wine Collection, guests can enjoy signature cocktails, absinthe drinks, non-alcoholic options, craft beers, and more. Located in the building that used to house the prominent Circle Repertory Theater, the 320-seat restaurant provides a diverse array of dining options from the spacious dining room, a seat at the butcher counter, the intimate second-floor gallery with private dining and outdoor cafe.

name: Lattanzi Cucina Italiana
summary: Set in a romantic and welcoming Restaurant Row townhouse, Lattanzi is celebrated for its "Roman Jewish-style specialties.
address: 361 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Opened in 1984, Lattanzi Cucina Italiana is a fine dining Italian restaurant set in a romantic and welcoming Restaurant Row townhouse. Lattanzi is celebrated for its "Roman Jewish-style specialties," and is ideal for both the pre-theater and post-theater crowd. Owned and operated by the Lattanzi family, the restaurant has been recognized as one of the City's finest. Executive chef Paolo Lattanzi's kitchen produces authentic Italian cuisine, such as their signature carciofi alla giudia—artichokes deep-fried in olive oil and garlic—a guest favorite.

name: Momoya Soho
summary: The beloved Japanese restaurant Momoya has evolved into this stunning new incarnation on the border of Soho and Nolita.
address: 47 Prince Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: The beloved Japanese restaurant Momoya has evolved into this stunning new incarnation on the border of Soho and Nolita. The two-level space is surrounded by windows, and has an unencumbered view of the bustle of a busy intersection, and of one of New York’s most historic churches. Inside, however, is a serene scene of Japanese fare that showcases picture-perfect nigiri and sublime foods highlighting the beauty of the vast array of dishes.

name: Oceans
summary: With a name like Oceans, it’s no surprise to learn that this restaurant’s menu is inspired by fresh catches from the Atlantic, Pacific and Mediterranean.
address: 233 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: With a name like Oceans, it’s no surprise to learn that this restaurant’s menu is inspired by fresh catches from the Atlantic, Pacific and Mediterranean. Start with a selection of sushi or something from the raw bar. Small plates like soups, salads and crab cakes are followed by “from the sea” choices—salmon, black cod, sea bass—as well as “from the land” dishes like filet mignon, braised short rib and even a cauliflower steak for vegans.

name: Club A Steakhouse
summary: This creation of restaurateur Bruno Selimaj (of Bruno Restaurant fame) combines characteristics of a traditional steakhouse with New World modernism in both the menu and decor.
address: 240 East 58th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Not far from Sutton Place and the Queensboro Bridge, this creation of restaurateur Bruno Selimaj (of Bruno Restaurant fame) combines characteristics of a traditional steakhouse with New World modernism in both the menu and decor. Executive chef Jean Christophe Villard—a Five Star Diamond Award winner formerly of such notables as Les Deux Gamins, Cafe Centro and Bobby Van's Steakhouse—offers an expectation of culinary perfection, whether it's the Prime dry aged Porterhouse steak or the grilled Atlantic blue fin tuna. Musical director Daniel Nye hosts the second floor piano lounge nightly, as he did at Bruno Restaurant.

name: Wallsé
summary: This modern European restaurant offers an impeccable integration between fine dining and fine art.
address: 344 West 11th Street, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: Wallsé is the flagship restaurant of Michelin-starred chef Kurt Gutenbrunner, serving contemporary Austrian cuisine that reflects his passion for aesthetics, taste, quality and seasonality. Nestled on a cozy corner of the West Village, Wallsé's modern and minimalist interiors play host to Gutenbrunner’s innovative menu, making it an ideal spot for those looking to find their inspiration in a New York cultural gem. The dining experience at Wallsé is light and refined. The dishes are characterized by their polished adaptation of traditional Viennese and European classics, elegantly paired with a world-class wine list.

name: Clara
summary: Set inside the iconic New-York Historical Society building across from Central Park, Clara offers upscale New York classics.
summary2: Clara, at The New York Historical, is helmed by longtime collaborators: Food Network star Alex Guarnaschelli and chef Michael Jenkins in partnership with Great Performances. The menu prioritizes local greenmarket and Katchkie Farm produce for its seasonal American menu. Clara's thoughtfully curated menu features fresh salads, homemade pastas, and a classic cheeseburger. Be sure to save room for dessert with the surprise cake of the day. Clara honors the work of Clara Driscoll (1861–1944), head of Tiffany Studios’ women’s glass-cutting department. For years, Driscoll and her team of "Tiffany Girls" worked in anonymity, until The New York Historical's research uncovered her role as the designer behind many of the firm’s most celebrated glass shades. Today, several of her creations are on display in the Museum’s Gallery of Tiffany Lamps.

name: Sant Ambroeus—Brookfield
summary: The menu by chef Iacopo Falai reflects the brand’s culinary vision and historic origins of Northern Italy, including its signature vitello tonnato, cotoletta milanese and risotti.
address: 200 Vesey Street, New York, New York 10281, United States
summary2: The menu, by chef Iacopo Falai, reflects the brand’s culinary vision and historic origins of Northern Italy, including its signature vitello tonnato, cotoletta milanese and risotti. The wine list offers a wide selection of Italian wines, and the espresso bar serves coffee lovers with unique blends of the highest-quality coffee to accompany cornetti and homemade cakes and cookies.

name: Red Hook Lobster Pound
summary: The famous lobster rolls at this Red Hook mainstay aren't all you'll find on the menu, but their popularity is a sure sign you should sample one.
summary2: The famous lobster rolls at this Red Hook mainstay aren't all you'll find on the menu, but their popularity is a sure sign you should sample one. Chalk up their deliciousness in no small part to the fact that those buttery, sweet lobster chunks are imported to Brooklyn from the Maine coast. Diners can also opt to try other seafood creation—including lobster mac 'n' cheese, shrimp rolls and New England clam chowder—since nothing here disappoints.

name: No Work Allowed
summary: No Work Allowed is a Japanese izakaya with a northeastern Thai twist—a unique culinary destination where good food, great drinks, and live jazz come together in a relaxed, vintage-inspired atmosphere.
address: 235 East 53rd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: No Work Allowed (NWA) is a Japanese izakaya with a northeastern Thai twist. It's a unique culinary destination in Midtown East where good food, great drinks, and live music come together in a relaxed, vintage-inspired atmosphere. Founded by a team of food enthusiasts with a passion for American nostalgia and jazz, NWA invites guests to unwind after a long day and experience an unforgettable meal. Leading the kitchen is Hawk Rodman, a talented chef with years of experience in Thai cuisine and training under the renowned chef Masayoshi Takayama at the three Michelin-starred Masa in NYC. Chef Hawk brings a refined fusion of Japanese techniques and Thai flavors to the menu, delivering dishes that are both innovative and comforting. Be sure to try his signature Pad Thai, a tribute to his time with Chef Masa.

name: Isabelle's Osteria
summary: Isabelle’s Italian menu adds unusual touches to traditional appetizers and entrees.
address: 245 Park Avenue South, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Isabelle’s opened in the Flatiron District in late 2020. Its Italian menu adds unusual touches to traditional appetizers and entrees—garlic mayo with crispy calamari, nduja butter with mussels, pickled peppers on the pork chop Milanese—and the brunch offerings include a chicken and waffle dish with Calabrian chili syrup.

name: The Sea Fire Grill
summary: Having perfected the classic steakhouse, the Benjamin Steakhouse Restaurant Group has moved beyond beef to conquer the seafood market.
address: 158 East 48th Street, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Having perfected the classic steakhouse, the Benjamin Steakhouse Restaurant Group has moved beyond beef to conquer the seafood market. The Sea Fire Grill offers approachable contemporary American seafood, where consistency in execution and highlighting the fish itself is a priority. Open for lunch Monday through Friday, and dinner seven nights a week, the Sea Fire Grill boasts a sleek and energetic bar, elegant dining rooms featuring a roaring fireplace and dark walnut wine racks throughout.

name: Carmine's - Upper West Side
summary: About as old-school Italian as it gets, the legendary family-style Southern Italian Carmine's delivers everything but the red-checkered tablecloth.
address: 2450 Broadway, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: About as old-school Italian as it gets, the legendary family-style Southern Italian Carmine’s delivers everything but the red-checkered tablecloth. Sopranos fans will feel comfortable in both the Times Square and Upper West Side locations, where the portions are absurdly generous, bottles of Chianti abound and the river flows with red sauce.

name: Essex
summary: Located in the historic Essex Street Market Building, Essex is a loft-like multilevel space with contemporary cuisine inspired by the flavors of the Lower East Side.
address: 124 Rivington Street, New York, New York 10002, United States
summary2: Located in the historic Schapiro's Winery, Essex is a loft-like multilevel space with contemporary cuisine inspired by the flavors of the Lower East Side. Essex is known for its weekday dinner and happy hour specials as well as its lively weekend dinner and bar scene. The weekend brunch is a New York institution and is always a top pick on Open Table Diner’s Choice and other sites. The expansive layout allows for intimate balcony and banquette seating as well as festive group dining and private parties. Enjoy outdoor dining rain or shine on the covered, heated decks.

name: Dear Strangers
summary: Dear Strangers is a Latin-inspired Modern American restaurant and cocktail bar located in Greenwich Village.
address: 147 West 4th Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Dear Strangers is a Latin-inspired Modern American restaurant and cocktail bar located in Greenwich Village. Chef Diego Rodriguez oversees the culinary program, while cocktail veterans Bratislav Glisic and Ivan Radulovic oversee the bar program. Reservations are available for dining guests in the 47-seat dining room, while the 12-seat bar is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

name: Park Ave Kitchen by David Burke
summary: Park Ave Kitchen by David Burke brings together delicious and authentic American fare with top-notch service in a fun atmosphere.
address: 277 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10172, United States
summary2: Cosmopolitan and fun, Park Ave Kitchen by David Burke is a modern American restaurant with a dual personality, each expressed by distinct menus and ambiance—one part casual European-esque café with a grab-n-go option, one part sophisticated dining destination. Both feature the creative cuisine of David Burke, one of the first celebrity chefs, whose often playful approach to his food lends a delightful additional dimension to the Park Ave Kitchen experience.

name: Momofuku Noodle Bar
summary: David Chang’s original Korean-American sensation.
address: 171 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: In 2004, Chef David Chang opened his first restaurant, Momofuku Noodle Bar, in the East Village of New York City. Noodle Bar serves a constantly changing roster of noodles, steamed breads, soft serve, and daily dishes. There's another location uptown at Columbus Circle.

name: Redeye Grill
summary: This cavernous restaurant captures the richness of NYC with a big, inclusive menu that ranges from miso to matzo ball soup and Cobb salad.
address: 890 7th Avenue, New York, New York 10106, United States
summary2: New York is the city where you can get anything your heart desires—and this cavernous restaurant located across from Carnegie Hall captures the richness of the city with a big, inclusive menu that ranges from miso & matzo ball soup and Cobb salad to seafood paella and Wiener Schnitzel, plus murals of Big Apple scenes painted by an assortment of artists and dramatic flourishes like a flashy raw bar featuring sculptures of dancing shrimp. The California Room offers a more intimate, subdued atmosphere.

name: Nudibranch
summary: Nudibranch is a Korean-Spanish restaurant that serves thoughtful small plates, juicy wines and cocktails in a chic space in the East Village.
address: 125 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Nudibranch, named after the species of colorful and diverse sea slugs, is a Korean-Spanish restaurant that serves thoughtful small plates and juicy wines in a chic space in the East Village...plus cocktails and porrons. Owned by chefs Jeffrey Kim and Matthew Lee, Nudibranch was a winner of Esquire magazine's Top 40 New restaurants in America 2022, and The Infatuation’s Best New Restaurants in New York 2022.

name: Aromi
summary: Aromi is a restaurant and pizzeria with a mission to bring classic, authentic Italian recipes to Carroll Gardens in Brooklyn.
address: 552 Court Square West, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Aromi is a restaurant and pizzeria with a mission to bring classic, authentic Italian recipes to Carroll Gardens in Brooklyn. The name evokes the owners' grandparents' gardens, their fruit trees and the vegetables they grew. In Italy, that is where you will find those bushes of aromatic spices that bring out the special flavors from their childhood. Their homemade pasta, pizza, focaccia, and cocktails, are all enriched with these authentic “aromi.” Aromi has a beautiful wood oven, a cozy indoor dining room, a nice  backyard, and a welcoming bar.

name: Aqua Kyoto
summary: Aqua New York has two separate restaurants—Aqua Roma and Aqua Kyoto—each a master of its own cuisine to bring this unique lifestyle dining concept to the table.
address: 902 Broadway, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Aqua New York has two separate restaurants—Aqua Roma and Aqua Kyoto—each a master of its own cuisine to bring this unique lifestyle dining concept to the table. With two amazing cuisines, contemporary Japanese and Italian, served as one fabulous experience, Aqua New York offers dining on a grand scale. Order from one menu or both, wherever you are seated. The menu reads Italian from the front and Japanese from the back. Their dinners often start with a signature Japanese sushi platter to share, followed by an Italian entrée and a delicious dessert. Italian and Japanese cooking match perfectly because they both share the same culinary philosophy: using  the freshest seasonal produce and preparing theme simply to let their natural flavors shine.

name: State Grill and Bar
summary: State Grill and Bar, an elegant addition to the newly renovated Empire State Building, is open for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
address: W 33rd St, Astoria, New York 10001, United States
summary2: State Grill and Bar is an elegant addition to the Empire State Building. Locally sourced dishes harken back to the way food used to be prepared—from a modern chef’s point of view. Guests can watch their food being prepared in the open kitchen by chef Morgan Jarrett, whose inspiration is the Empire State and its bounty of market ingredients, from the Hudson Valley to the North Fork. Echoing the Empire State Building's striking aesthetics, the interior features a balanced design of art deco and modern architecture.

name: Godunk Thai Street Food
summary: Godunk is a new Thai street food destination in NoHo from master chef Nate Limwong, known for her acclaimed work at Chalong and Unglo.
address: 332 Bowery, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: Godunk is a new Thai street food destination in NoHo from master chef Nate Limwong, known for her acclaimed work at Chalong and Unglo. Celebrating the breadth and vibrancy of Thailand's street food culture—from the seafood-rich South to the bold, aromatic flavors of the North—Godunk showcases both beloved classics and rarely-seen regional specialties. Chef Nate draws from her global culinary background, weaving techniques and inspirations from her travels into meticulous broths, and handcrafted sauces. Guests can expect elevated noodle bowls, seafood-driven dishes, and nostalgic comfort plates alongside an inventive cocktail menu from Angel's Share alum Ryan Saputra that pays homage to iconic films through Thai and Asian ingredients. Set against a warm, vintage-meets-modern backdrop of maroon hues, textured walls, and analog film accents, Godunk brings an immersive, cinematic experience to Manhattan's NoHo neighborhood.

name: Maison Pickle
summary: Maison Pickle offers Continental classics and that iconic American sandwich, the French Dip, in a refined and relaxed setting for food and drink.
address: 2315 Broadway, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: Maison Pickle offers Continental classics and that iconic American sandwich, the French Dip, in a refined and relaxed setting for food and drink. Their cocktails share the stage with food, with more than 200 types of spirits to take neat or on the rocks. Cocktails are old school but progressive—top-shelf spirits with imaginative ingredients mixed with a little madness. Located in Manhattan's West 80s, this contemporary American restaurant is comfortable, inventive and inviting.

name: Palo Santo
summary: At Palo Santo, you’ll find chef Jacques Gautier’s pan-Latin cooking in a Brooklyn brownstone.
address: 652 Union Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11211, United States
summary2: At Palo Santo, you’ll find pan-Latin cooking in a Brooklyn brownstone. Chef Jacques Gautier’s changing menu blends Latin American and Caribbean influences with high-quality, seasonal ingredients including local produce from the nearby Grand Army Plaza Greenmarket. Palo Santo’s wine list has over five dozen wines from South America and New York State. Imported Latin American beers are available in bottles and cans, and local craft brews are on tap.

name: Monterey
summary: Simon Oren, Dudi Sasson and chef James Tracey bring midtown Manhattan a glamorous bold American restaurant: Monterey.
address: 37 East 50th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Simon Oren, Dudi Sasson and chef James Tracey bring midtown Manhattan a glamorous bold American restaurant: Monterey. The raw bar features every crustacean imaginable, and servers stroll through the dining room brandishing custom gueridon carts preparing items tableside. The menu circles the globe, offering chef Tracey’s seasonal cuisine alongside an extensive selection of prime dry-aged steaks, and roast prime rib of beef. Beverage director Aviram Turgeman’s wine list is award-winning, and his cocktails are expertly shaken and stirred.

name: The Clocktower
summary: This chic 88-seat, David Rockwell-designed restaurant serves contemporary cuisine with British sensibilities.
address: 5 Madison Avenue, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: The Clocktower, located on the second floor of the New York Edition Hotel (formerly the iconic Metropolitan Life building), is a collaboration between acclaimed restaurateur Stephen Starr and Michelin-starred British chef Jason Atherton. The chic 88-seat, David Rockwell-designed restaurant serves contemporary cuisine with British sensibilities, classic and contemporary cocktails, and a diverse selection of wines, along with local and global beers.

name: Il Fiorista
summary: Il Florista is a restaurant, bar, café, florist, boutique, and community education space that embraces the manifold uses and beautiful benefits of flowers.
address: 17 West 26th Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Il Florista is a restaurant, bar, café, florist, boutique and community education space that embraces the many uses and benefits of flowers. The Mediterranean-centric menu features flowers throughout. The endive and kohlrabi salad comes with an apple blossom caper vinaigrette. The pappardelle is served with black pepper, lemon, pecorino and lavender. The coriander-glazed lamb steak is accompanied by picked green tomato, preserved shiro plum and rose.

name: Nizza
summary: Nizza takes its name from the Italian word for the French region of Nice, and its menu is French-Italian fusion.
address: 630 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Nizza takes its name from the Italian word for the French region of Nice, and its menu leans on regional favorites from the Italian Riviera. House-made rigatoni, pizza and a few specialties highlight the options at this relaxed Theatre District institution, which also has gluten-free alternatives and an approachable wine list.

name: La Sirene UWS
summary: Chef/owner Didier Pawlicki's menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season.
address: 416 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: Chef/owner Didier Pawlicki lived in the hotel of his parents in the Pyrenees Mountains in France from the age of 6 to 16, when he left to attend the French Culinary School in Toulouse. His menu at La Sirène is crafted to reflect the best of South France and the freshest ingredients of the season. The restaurant's focus is on French Southern homemade styles and quality ingredients (Cuisine Bourgeoise) paired with a respectable wine list and friendly, professional service.

name: Morton's The Steakhouse—Manhattan
summary: There are quite a few venerable steakhouses in Midtown, but Morton's stands tall among them.
address: 551 5th Avenue, New York, New York 10176, United States
summary2: Fine dining reaches its peak in Midtown Manhattan at Morton’s The Steakhouse. Step into timeless opulence with inviting interiors and a highly attentive staff. Morton’s is the perfect place to lock in a business deal, unwind after a busy day, or recharge after taking in the Big Apple. The chef-crafted menu features classic steakhouse selections like a substantial dry-aged porterhouse to share, a delicate center-cut filet, and the famous Legendary Hot Chocolate Cake (with a molten chocolate center). Morton’s The Steakhouse is conveniently located on Fifth Avenue, near upscale shopping (Bergdorf Goodman, Saks Fifth Avenue) and local attractions such as Rockefeller Center and St. Patrick’s Cathedral).

name: Taste of India II
summary: Taste of India offers a sophisticated fine dining experience with effortlessly charming staff and discreet service.
summary2: Now in its third decade in New Dorp, Staten Island, Taste of India continues to offer a sophisticated fine dining experience with effortlessly charming staff and discreet service. It is the reinvented combination of a restaurant, lounge and bar that provides a culinary journey through India to savor and discover new ingredients and dishes.

name: Hav & Mar
summary: Hav & Mar is a vibrant seafood house in Chelsea from chef Marcus Samuelsson.
address: 245 11th Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Hav & Mar is a vibrant seafood house from chef Marcus Samuelsson located in the Manhattan arts district of Chelsea. The stunning dining room and dazzling bar, a mix of contemporary and classical design, features original work by award-winning artist Derrick Adams. Chef Samuelsson and executive chef Fariyal Abdullahi’s energetic and globally inspired menu focuses on thoughtfully sourced seafood and seasonal greenmarket produce. Gracious hospitality, show-stopping cocktails, and a groundbreaking wine list spotlighting BIPOC and female producers contribute to Hav & Mar’s convivial and festive atmosphere.

name: Red Rooster Harlem
summary: Marcus Samuelsson's restaurant focuses on elevated American comfort food.
address: 310 Malcolm X Boulevard, New York, New York 10027, United States
summary2: Paying homage to Harlem's culturally rich and diverse neighborhood, Marcus Samuelsson has created a restaurant that focuses on elevated American comfort food against a backdrop of warm colors, stimulating art and soulful sounds. The 3,400 square-foot space houses a restaurant, a breakfast cafe, a grocery, a horseshoe-shaped bar and a communal table. The basement space is reserved for private parties and cooking classes and demonstrations.

name: Le Pavillon
summary: Le Pavillon expresses chef Daniel Boulud’s roots in New York City with a fresh and unique approach to fine dining in a dramatic setting.
address: 1 Vanderbilt Avenue, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Le Pavillon is a culinary oasis in Midtown East by chef Daniel Boulud. Evoking a “pavillon”, a festive gathering dining space surrounded by nature, Le Pavillon expresses chef Boulud’s roots in New York City with a fresh and unique approach to fine dining in a dramatic setting. With a focus on seasonality and locally sourced ingredients from both land and sea (“terre et mer"), chef Boulud’s celebrated French cuisine, rooted in tradition with a contemporary New York spirit, is at the forefront of the seafood and vegetable-focused menu. Situated in Manhattan’s state-of-the-art-skyscraper One Vanderbilt, Le Pavillon offers a unique setting, both relaxed and inviting with a refined elegance. Designed by Isay Weinfeld, the space boasts a natural landscape composed of lush gardens and tall olive trees living among the tailored dining room and soaring ceilings, evoking a deep sense of natural splendor and genuine serenity.

name: Raval Steakhouse
summary: Set on Staten Island’s vibrant north shore, Raval Steakhouse is the vision of lifelong friends who have brought their passion for great food and hospitality back to their Staten Island roots.
summary2: Set on Staten Island’s vibrant north shore, Raval Steakhouse is the vision of lifelong friends Naz and Gent. From bustling Manhattan kitchens to the heart of their hometown, they’ve brought their passion for great food and hospitality back to their Staten Island roots. Inspired by the Raval neighborhood outside ancient Roman walls, the steakhouse is named after this historic district, once a refuge outside the city—a place where people from all walks of life gathered, shared stories, and felt at home. The team at Raval Steakhouse are redefining the classic steakhouse experience. With a commitment to uncompromising quality and a fresh urban vibe, they offer more than just a meal—their doors are open to anyone who wants to enjoy expertly crafted dishes, share in good company, and feel a sense of belonging.

name: Felice Columbus
summary: Felice Columbus brings the vineyards of the Tuscan countryside to the Upper West Side.
address: 240 Columbus Avenue, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Felice Columbus brings the vineyards of the Tuscan countryside to the Upper West Side. The two-level space includes a ground-level dining room flooded by light from a wall of floor-to-ceiling windows, showcasing a striking 40-foot-plus-long bar, while the lower level is an intimate cocktail and wine lounge. The menu consists of Felice favorites including the fusilli al ferretto e burrata, pappardelle con salsiccia, and house specials using cured and smoked fish, as well as seasonal vegetables sourced from local farms.

name: City Winery
summary: City Winery's flagship location includes two performance venues, a restaurant that includes a pizza bar and coffee roasting station, and a tasting room.
address: 25 11th Avenue, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: City Winery's new flagship location, with views of Hudson River Park, Pier 57 and sunsets over the Hudson, includes two performance venues—a seated 350-seat concert hall, and a smaller 150-capacity loft space—plus a 100-seat restaurant that includes a pizza bar and coffee roasting station, and a tasting room. The tasting bars feature the company’s proprietary tap system, which dispense 12 or more wines straight from the keg. This fully functioning winery/wine production facility strives to create wine that contains low to no sulfites while reducing their carbon footprint.

name: When in Bangkok
summary: When in Bangkok is a Thai restaurant that will transport you to a kitchen in Bangkok.
address: 11358 Queens Boulevard, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: When in Bangkok is a Thai restaurant that will transport you to a kitchen in Bangkok. The team from Malii Thai Kitchen presents popular dishes of Bangkok food scenes, like poo karee (softshell crab in spicy curry sauce), shrimp pad thai, and pineapple fried rice. The drink menu includes a variety of colorful cocktails from different districts of Bangkok.

name: Off the Hook Raw Bar & Grill
summary: Off the Hook Raw Bar & Grill is a cozy seafood grill and raw oyster bar in Astoria.
address: 28-08 34th Street, Astoria, New York 11103, United States
summary2: Off the Hook Raw Bar & Grill is a cozy seafood grill and raw oyster bar in Astoria, Queens, that specializes in updated classic dishes, cocktails and craft ales. Executive chef Iglent Feizulla and his team source their fresh ingredients from local fish and farmers' markets to ensure high quality, seasonal ingredients.

name: Docks Oyster Bar
summary: Docks Oyster Bar has been serving the freshest seafood and oysters for more than 25 years in Midtown Manhattan.
address: 633 3rd Avenue, New York, New York 10017, United States
summary2: Docks Oyster Bar has been serving the freshest seafood and oysters for more than 25 years in Midtown Manhattan. They have a large open floor plan with tables lining windows along both Third Avenue and 40th Street, and an expansive bar that serves tasty martinis, wine and cocktails. Docks' daily specials and simply prepared fish are reasons for their longevity, along with an outstanding service team, a great wine list and an amazing New York atmosphere in which guests can create memories.

name: Mamo
summary: Mamo brings a long tradition of Italian hospitality and provençal charm to New York City's SoHo neighborhood.
address: 323 West Broadway, New York, New York 10013, United States
summary2: Established in 2015, Mamo takes its name from the family nickname for Mikaël ´Mamo’ Mammoliti. Mike was raised in the restaurant industry in the South of France with his father, and is inspired by the tradition and warmth of his Italian grandfather Angelo 'Mamo' Mammoliti. With the help of his partners, chef Salvatore Marcello and Steven Fruman, Mike brought a modern twist on Italian nostalgia by introducing Mamo. Located in SoHo, Mamo is open daily for lunch and dinner.

name: Hupo
summary: This Long Island City restaurant is dedicated to presenting Szechuan food in a contemporary way, while maintaining traditional virtues, too.
address: 10-07 50th Avenue, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Szechuan cuisine is "Chinese people's most beloved style of cooking," according to Hupo. This Long Island City restaurant is dedicated to presenting Szechuan food in a contemporary way, while maintaining traditional virtues, too.

name: Marseille
summary: Taking its name from the port town in southern France, the restaurant, like the town, is a melting pot of influences and ideas.
address: 630 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: With multi-design tiled floors and a complex interior that is a clear throwback to an earlier era and a different part of the world, Marseille delivers on uniqueness yet somehow seems to lack a consistent point of view—and that’s the probably the point. Taking its name from the port town in southern France, the restaurant, like the town, is a melting pot of influences and ideas. The main thrust of the menu is French, but accents from northern Africa and the rest of the Mediterranean can be seen (and tasted) throughout.

name: Heritage Grand Bakery
summary: Heritage Grand Bakery, inspired by the Mediterranean, serves signature breads, pastries and wood-fired pizzas in a stylish and worldly setting.
address: 8 West 40th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: Heritage Grand Bakery Restaurant & Pizza Bar is located near Bryant Park and the New York Public Library. Inspired by the Mediterranean, they serve signature breads, pastries and wood-fired pizzas in a stylish and worldly setting. The Grand Bar features classy cocktails and a refined assortment of wine and beer. The open kitchen, open mixing room, and pizzaiolo-manned pizza ovens offer customers a glimpse into the restaurant's operation. The retail bakery sells freshly baked breads, pastries, viennoiseries, grab and go breakfast items, hot and cold lunch sandwiches, salads as well as premium coffee and teas.

name: Stout NYC Bryant Park
summary: The newest Stout NYC location is just steps away from Bryant Park, Times Square and the Theatre District.
address: 109 West 39th Street, New York, New York 10018, United States
summary2: The newest Stout NYC location is just steps away from Bryant Park, Times Square and the Theatre District. Here you’ll find a grand bar right in the center. Come by for lunch, after-work drinks or dinner. Catch your favorite sports events on the 10' projector or one of the 29 TVs around the space.

name: Sempre Oggi
summary: Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage.
address: 164 West 75th Street, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Directly translated as "Always Today," Sempre Oggi focuses on embracing the very best of right now. Born from Italian tradition and heritage, executive Chef Phillip Basone's menu takes seasonal and local ingredients and places them center stage. Brought forth by Robert Guarino in partnership with Simon Oren of Chef Driven Hospitality, Sempre Oggi draws inspiration from renowned Italian architect and designer, Gio Ponti. The bar's handmade ceramic tiles mimic Ponti's worldwide collaboration with Ceramica D'Agostino. A custom floating chandelier nods to Ponti's love for playing with geometric forms, light and color; at once both modern and traditional.

name: Bixi
summary: Bixi offers dishes and drinks that are packed with unforgettable flavors and served by a knowledgeable, friendly staff.
address: 2164 Frederick Douglass Boulevard, New York, New York 10026, United States
summary2: Bixi offers dishes and drinks that are packed with unforgettable flavors and served by a knowledgeable, friendly staff. James Beard Award–winning chef Serena Bass has created an Asian menu that brings in influences from around the globe. Bartender and co-owner Kwame Biney oversees the impressive cocktail list.

name: Coqodaq
summary: This "cathedral of fried chicken" skillfully integrates Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team, alongside the largest restaurant champagne list in America.
address: 12 East 22nd Street, New York, New York 10010, United States
summary2: Coqodaq is an innovative fried chicken concept from Gracious Hospitality Management, designed by Rockwell Group as "the cathedral of fried chicken." They skillfully integrate Korean and American influences, featuring dishes cooked by a world-class culinary team. From certified humane, hormone- and antibiotic-free chicken to gluten-free and anti-inflammatory rice flour batter, and clean cultured oil—every ingredient is of the highest quality and sustainably sourced. The beverage program champions champagne as the pairing of choice, with the largest restaurant champagne list in America, with Blue Chip classics, pages of verticals of vintages, and 100 sparkling wines under $100, breaking down the cost barrier of bubbly. Classic cocktails with an innovative twist, as well as premier beer and wine selections, round out the menu.

name: Playa Betty's
summary: Playa Betty's takes its inspiration from the length of the California coastline.
address: 320 Amsterdam Avenue, New York, New York 10023, United States
summary2: Playa Betty's takes its inspiration from the length of the California coastline. The sunny vibe extends from Baja fish tacos and healthy grain bowls to margaritas and tropical cocktails.

name: San Carlo
summary: San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is a corner of Turin in Soho.
address: 90 Thompson Street, New York, New York 10012, United States
summary2: San Carlo Osteria Piemonte is like a corner of Turin in Soho. The restaurant, with its minimalist and elegant design, serves dishes that are well-crafted, beautifully presented Piedmont specialties that are reproduced with passion and flair. Evenings can start with a vermouth-based cocktail, just like in an old Torinese cafe, and continue with a Fassona chopped beef, then tajarin pasta with truffle or homemade agnolotti pockets with roast sauce. The kitchen is from Piedmont and so wine is abundant, and not just Nebbiolotry—try the peppery rhythm of a good Pelaverga.

name: Barbetta
summary: Owned by the same family for more than a century, Barbetta is a romantic Italian restaurant with ornate décor and a lush back garden.
address: 321 West 46th Street, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Owned by the same family for more than a century, Barbetta’s ornate décor and lush, fanciful back garden (replete with stone fountain) make it the most romantic Italian around. The focus is on the cuisine of the proprietors’ native Piedmont, where specialties include bollito, agnolotti and risotto. Don’t miss the Italian white truffles, an extra-luxurious treat when they are in season.

name: Little Chef Little Cafe
summary: Smoothies, salads, rice bowls and toasts help make up the healthy comfort-food menu at this Long Island City café.
address: 5-43 48th Avenue, Long Island City, New York 11101, United States
summary2: Little Chef Little Cafe provides Long Island City with health-conscious options for breakfast, lunch, daily brunch and early dinner. The menu offers nutritious salads, soups, rice bowls, toasts, smoothies and juices, pastries, snacks, coffee and tea with many vegetarian and vegan choices. They offer takeout and delivery daily.

name: Dagon
summary: The menu at Dagon, named for the Phoenician and Philistine god of agriculture and the earth, showcases modern Israeli cuisine with Levantine influences.
address: 2454 Broadway, New York, New York 10024, United States
summary2: This stellar Middle Eastern restaurant is exactly what the Upper West Side needed: adventurous yet soothing food served in a polished, vibrant dining room. There is plenty of outdoor seating, an open kitchen and a long, curving bar featuring innovative cocktails. Go with a group and share whipped eggplant with preserved lemon, Sasso chicken liver mousse sweetened with date syrup, pomegranate-glazed salmon, harissa barbecue chicken and delectably crisp, roasted lamb. The fresh-baked flatbread and Jerusalem bagel are also divine.

name: Wayward Fare
summary: Wayward Fare, a rustic and elegant culinary journey in Prospect Heights, offers a seasonally charged menu that weaves together a tapestry of some lesser-known Mediterranean flavors.
address: 554 Vanderbilt Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11238, United States
summary2: Wayward Fare is a rustic and elegant culinary journey nestled in the Prospect Heights neighborhood of Brooklyn. Their seasonally charged menu weaves together a tapestry of some lesser-known Mediterranean flavors. Chef Akhtar Nawab has added personal touches of his well-traveled background to every dish, taking cues from the Mediterranean and liberties from nearby regions, that speak to the global heartbeat of New York City.

name: Nino's
summary: Satisfy your Italian food craving at the plush-but-not-stuffy Nino's neighborhood restaurant (located in Midtown East), where the food is reliable and the atmosphere is warm.
address: 405 East 52nd Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Satisfy your Italian food craving at the plush-but-not-stuffy Nino’s neighborhood restaurant (located in Manhattan's Midtown East), where the food is reliable and the atmosphere is warm. This intimate spot is a great place to share good conversation while tucking into popular dishes like rigatoni in vodka sauce and osso buco.

name: Balade
summary: Suha Rihan, executive chef at Balade, is a culinary virtuoso in Middle Eastern cuisine, with a particular expertise in Lebanese dishes.
address: 208 1st Avenue, New York, New York 10009, United States
summary2: Suha Rihan, executive chef at Balade, is a culinary virtuoso in Middle Eastern cuisine, with a particular expertise in Lebanese dishes. Chef Omar, renowned for his authentic recipes, brings a rich tapestry of flavors to every dish he creates. His celebrated hummus epitomizes his dedication to authenticity and excellence. Each of his creations is a testament to his mastery and passion for Lebanese culinary traditions. Balade serves a wide range of dishes for both vegetarians and for those who love the traditional meat and fish.

name: Limani
summary: Limani, the Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Rockefeller Center, uses only the highest-quality local and Mediterranean seafood.
address: 45 Rockefeller Plaza, New York, New York 10111, United States
summary2: Limani, the Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Rockefeller Center, uses only the highest-quality local and Mediterranean seafood. Chef M. J. Alam ensures all dishes have the best ingredients that exemplify the simplicity of the Mediterranean way of life, whether using artisanal small-batch items such as capers from Santorini or saffron from Kozani, or local organic vegetables. Diners can also look forward to "seasonal surprises" throughout the year as chef Alam explores new arrivals on the market. Limani is located around the corner from Radio City Music Hall and walking distance from the Theatre District.

name: House of the Red Pearl
summary: The House of the Red Pearl is a clandestine fine dining restaurant.
address: 96 South Street, New York, New York 10038, United States
summary2: The House of the Red Pearl is a clandestine fine dining restaurant serving Chinese-inspired dishes that marry the innovation of chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten with flavors of the East, tucked away for a feeling of discovery. It's New York’s best kept secret, with intricate gold wallpaper and blue velvet banquettes.

name: The Uptown Garrison
summary: With specialty coffee, breakfast sandwiches, brick-oven pizza and craft cocktails on offer, The Uptown Garrison has something to satisfy your cravings from morning till night.
address: 821 West 181st Street, New York, New York 10033, United States
summary2: With specialty coffee, breakfast sandwiches, brick-oven pizza and craft cocktails on offer, The Uptown Garrison has something to satisfy your cravings from morning till night. On a sunny afternoon, the spacious outdoor patio is the place to be: catch up with a friend over an elderflower matcha latte and avocado toast. Come nightfall, it’s time to settle into the cozy and stylish dining room for dinner. Ask for a window table to get a front-row seat for some of the best Washington Heights people-watching action in the neighborhood.

name: San Sabino
summary: San Sabino is a seafood-focused Italian restaurant from wife and husband team, chefs Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli (Don Angie), in partnership with Quality Branded.
address: 113 Greenwich Avenue, New York, New York 10014, United States
summary2: San Sabino is a seafood-focused Italian restaurant from wife and husband team, chefs Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli, in partnership with Quality Branded. After working in some of NYC’s top Italian restaurants and dreaming of opening their own special neighborhood spot, Angie and Scott opened Don Angie in 2018 to tremendous critical acclaim. They quickly became known for boldly unexpected dishes that challenge your perception of traditional Italian-American cooking. Six years later and just a few doors down from Don Angie, they opened their second restaurant, San Sabino. Named after Scott’s grandfather (from Sanza, Italy, where most people are named after the patron saint Sabino), San Sabino offers a playful spin on Italian dishes from Shrimp Parm to Pasta Alle Vongole, with bold twists influenced by coastal American cities (where many Italians settled, from New Orleans to the Jersey Shore).

name: Ci Siamo
summary: Celebrating the beauty of simplicity, chef Hillary Sterling centers Ci Siamo's Italian-inflected menu around live-fire cooking and seasonal ingredients.
address: 385 Ninth Avenue, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Ci Siamo translates to "here we are" or "we've finally arrived." It's the clinking of glasses after a long week, the rush of arriving at a new destination, the relief of a familiar smile — it's an exhalation. Celebrating the beauty of simplicity, chef Hillary Sterling centers her Italian-inflected menu around live-fire cooking and seasonal ingredients, bridging the traditional with the contemporary in a transportive yet familiar space.

name: Siren Oyster Bar & Restaurant
summary: Siren is a contemporary European seafood restaurant in South Slope, Brooklyn, specializing in modern dishes and an extensive oyster selection.
address: 687 Grand Army Plaza, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: It’s fitting that Siren Oyster Bar & Restaurant is named after the deep-sea temptresses, as it is very difficult to escape the call of their snow crab legs, caviar, crab cakes, and lobster bisque. Siren is a contemporary European seafood restaurant in the South Slope area between Park Slope and Greenwood Heights, specializing in modern dishes and an extensive oyster selection. Their hibiscus margarita is a cocktail highlight. The folks at Siren pride themselves on being a local Brooklyn restaurant where friends and family make memories while enjoying the perfect bite or the best cocktails.

name: Via 13
summary: Via 13, set in the West Village, serves the essence of Italy today—bold flavors, warm hospitality, and surprising twists make every visit unforgettable.
address: 140 West 13th Street, New York, New York 10011, United States
summary2: Via 13 is the next chapter in the story of the West Village restaurant formerly known as Sotto 13. They've evolved—renovated, reimagined, and reenergized. So much has changed, it felt only right for the owners to change the name too. Via 13 serves the essence of Italy today—bold flavors, warm hospitality, and surprising twists make every visit unforgettable. It’s not a postcard from the past; it’s the next chapter in Italian dining.

name: Bocca Di Bacco—Theatre District
summary: Bocca Di Bacco is an Italian restaurant located near the Theatre District that is popular with celebrities, tourists and native New Yorkers.
address: 635 9th Avenue, New York, New York 10036, United States
summary2: Bocca Di Bacco is an Italian restaurant located near the Theatre District that is popular with celebrities, tourists and native New Yorkers. It has two additional locations in nearby neighborhoods Hell's Kitchen and Chelsea. Whether for drinks after work or dining before or after a show, Bocca Di Bacco aims to satisfy. Known for top-notch creative Italian cuisine including homemade pasta, meats and seafood, this restaurant also has an excellent wine selection with 500 of the best bottles from renowned Italian wineries.

name: Anassa Taverna - Manhattan
summary: Anassa ("breath of fresh air" in Greek) is an elegant interpretation of the traditional Greek taverna.
address: 200 East 60th Street, New York, New York 10022, United States
summary2: Anassa is an elegant interpretation of the traditional Greek taverna. Nestled in  Midtown East, Anassa transports diners through a true culinary and cultural journey through the cobblestone roads of the ancient historical neighborhood of Plaka, featuring simply prepared fresh fish and traditional Greek fare. At the entrance, traditional Greek worry beads and evil eyes are on display, and deeper within you will find breathtaking decor: a marble-covered bar, white curtains, weathered exposed brick walls and light wood.

name: Oscar Wilde
summary: This Victorian-themed bar features a cocktail list that reflects both the Victorian and Prohibition eras.
address: 45 West 27th Street, New York, New York 10001, United States
summary2: Celebrating the legendary Irish playwright, Oscar Wilde has New York City’s longest bar at 118.5 feet. Located at the former headquarters of NYC’s Bureau of Prohibition, the 5,874-square-foot, Victorian-themed bar features a cocktail list that reflects both the Victorian and Prohibition eras. Design features and artifacts have been hand-selected from all over the globe, including a Belgian piano from the 1890s, a standing clock from England from the 1880s, painted glass from Milan dating back to the late 19th century, antique fireplaces and more.

name: Sereneco
summary: Sereneco is an all-day restaurant in Greenpoint that serves seasonal New American cuisine alongside creative drinks.
address: 113 Franklin Street, Brooklyn, New York 11222, United States
summary2: Sereneco is an all-day restaurant that serves seasonal New American cuisine for dinner and brunch, alongside creative drinks, in Greenpoint. Menu highlights include braised beef short rib (creamy polenta, grilled corn, cucumber, pickled red onions, port wine reduction sauce) and Hudson Valley duck confit (braised borlotti beans, grilled cipollini onions, cherry tomatoes, crispy brussels sprouts, sage). The cocktails include the Fly Fig Fly (bourbon, fig, lemon, rosemary) and the Supernova (dill aquavit, gin, cucumber juice, jalapeno, lemon).

name: Vallata
summary: Inspired by his family and their home-cooked meals, Vallata is celebrity chef Tom Colicchio's first-ever Italian restaurant.
address: 47 East 19th Street, New York, New York 10003, United States
summary2: Inspired by his family and their home-cooked meals, Vallata is celebrity chef Tom Colicchio's first-ever Italian restaurant. First a pop-up, now a permanent resident located just steps from Union Square Park, Vallata shares straightforward Italian cooking in an intimate and eclectic space. This neighborhood trattoria, open for lunch, dinner and weekend brunch, serves simple, straightforward dishes that are fully executed in a lively open kitchen (and also available for pickup and delivery). Vallata aims to remind us of the connective powers of food and family.

name: Sarabeth's Central Park South
summary: At Sarabeth's Central Park South, you'll find contemporary American food, a warm atmosphere and the friendly service Sarabeth's restaurants are known for.
address: 40 Central Park South, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: At Sarabeth's Central Park South, you’ll find contemporary American food, a warm atmosphere and the friendly service Sarabeth's restaurants are known for. A neighborhood staple and easy destination for visitors, Sarabeth's CPS is within walking distance of the historic Plaza Hotel, Carnegie Hall and the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), and just steps from Central Park. They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner every day of the week, as well as weekend brunch, with a full bar and specialty cocktails.

name: Empire Steak House - Midtown West
summary: This second Empire Steak House opened by the Sinanaj brothers showcases modern decor in a classy but trendy atmosphere.
address: 237 West 54th Street, New York, New York 10019, United States
summary2: Empire Steak House on 54th Street showcases modern decor in a classy but trendy atmosphere. The all-white, 50-foot marble bar and sprawling dining room provide an air of sophistication. Empire is acclaimed for its dry-aged porterhouse for two, and the rest of the vast menu features a wide range of fresh seafood including 4- to 5-pound lobsters, Chilean sea bass, salmon, yellow fin tuna and towering seafood platters. The eatery offers a highly selective wine list with many sought-after California vintages.

name: La Marchande
summary: La Marchande is chef John Fraser’s modernized take on the French brasserie, set in The Wall Street Hotel.
address: 88 Wall Street, New York, New York 10005, United States
summary2: La Marchande is chef John Fraser’s modernized take on the French brasserie. Set in The Wall Street Hotel, La Marchande nods to the history of the rusticated beaux-arts building that was once the site of the original 18th-century stock exchange. The menu, co-developed by Fraser and executive chef Rick Horiike, reflects the sultry classics of French brasserie cuisine, reimagined by a global pantry. Signature dishes, such as grilled lobster with coconut sauce-américaine, steamed Dover sole with vermouth-lime butter, and lamb prime rib, are modernized and lightened by unique, global seasoning.

name: Lorenzo's Restaurant, Bar & Cabaret
summary: Lorenzos Restaurant, Bar & Cabaret serves modern Italian and American fare at breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily.
summary2: Lorenzo’s Restaurant, Bar & Cabaret is an upscale restaurant inside the Hilton Garden Inn New York/Staten Island that serves modern Italian and American fare at breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily. Lorenzo's offers happy hour Monday through Friday, romantic piano music on Friday and Saturday evenings, Sunday jazz brunch and Sunday Italian dinner buffet.
